Electronic Super Joy, although having quite a delightful name, isn't much fun (in my opinion, of course).
I'll start with one thing first: I haven't finished the game; I haven't even finished the first world. But the fact that I haven't just proves further that I really couldn't stand this game. From what I played, the main obstacles are the missiles: they home in on you and kill you in one hit, sending you back to the last checkpoint. However, the very nature of these missiles is what makes the game so frustrating.
Missiles home in on you: what's the problem? The problem is that the unpredictable nature of these hazards is contradictory to the main reason I enjoy platformers. Something that I enjoy in platformers (and mostly take for granted) is the fact that when I put in a set of inputs, I always get the same results. But the missiles' parameters change so easily that I really don't have room to improve because I don't know what I did wrong. The World 1 boss is a testament to the frustration that stems from missiles.
*I'm about to drop minor spoilers for the World 1 boss' gameplay, BTW*
The whole boss is about grabbing Rainbow Missiles, which make a secondary character fire them at the boss. There's a lot of things that urk me about this boss. Firstly, the unpredictable nature of the missiles, as previously stated, are really annoying, and they're all over this boss. Basically every 30 seconds, the boss spawns 3 more missiles (except when he doesn't), which never go away, and you have to avoid them on an incredibly small platform.
Secondly, as I just hinted at, the boss itself adds even more unpredictable attacks. Extra things that make the boss more rage-inducing include the random placement of Rainbow Missiles, the randomisation of the attacks, and the aforementioned weird movement of the regular missiles.
Third, the death animation is SO long. It takes anywhere from 2-3 seconds (from my experience), which doesn't sound like much, but over the course of 100+ deaths, that makes about 6 minutes or more of just waiting for the game to let you play again. I found you could press the restart button as the animation was playing to skip it, but it's a motion that grated on me after a while, and sometimes I would restart because I thought I died, but then I realise I wouldn't have died, which caused even more frustration.
Finally, the boss gives you no kind of telegraph. I'm sure that my character's position, time, etc. would influence the way in which certain behaviours would appear, but their methods were so convoluted that it just felt random to me. I can say that in something like Super Meat Boy (quite cliche that I bring it up), the bosses have predictable, telegraphed attacks, and even if you do die (which is quite easy), the boss in question behaves exactly the same way when you fight them for the second, or fourth, or hundredth, or thousandth time. The key difference is that in Super Meat Boy, with each death I feel like I'm learning something that I can apply on the next attempt, which is sadly not the case for this game.
That's not to say that Electronic Super Joy isn't without it's qualities: the game is quite pretty, and the plot, although simple enough, is a good motive for the actual game. However, I don't think that these can outweigh the negatives. Some people could tell me that this game gets better later on, and I would totally believe them. The problem with that though is the game has not engaged me enough to make me want to spend my time on getting to the 'fun' part. Overall, this game isn't awful: not even close. But personally, I couldn't put up with it's flaws, and I'm going to have to give it a pass.
...until the inevitable point where I'll need to complete every Steam game in my collection, and then I guess I'll have to get it over with.

I usually don't write reviews about games but this one really disappointed me.
At first glance, the game was great. I didn't care too much about the story line because I essentially wanted to just PVP like in any fighting game I play. It didn't take me too long to realize how broken the A.I. was and how some of the mechanics to the game were very imbalanced. Such as enemy A.I. having unlimited Ki (this was obvious because Super Saiyans would remain Super Saiyans for the entire fight without running out of ki and do nothing but spam their ultimate attacks) and Female Earhtlings being able to do an infinite by simply dive kicking. And let's not forget the notorious bugged Milk Cannon attack that launches multiple blasts depending on your FPS setting (this is only ONE of the several features in the game that are affected by your FPS settings).
I haven't even scratched the surface to how many broken concepts and bugged mechanics there are in this game. I honestly do not believe they had the concept of "balance" when they made this game nor does it really seem like they put any effort into porting this game to PC (one way this is evident because we can't even type a message we want. We're forced to select from a list of premade words and phrases. C'mon!).
And don't even get me started on the hackers who single handedly destroyed PVP. So many people are afraid to even step foot in a Player Match lobby because of how many hackers are in the game with edited attributes and skills that aren't even designed for custom characters. The saddest thing about it is the fact that the company won't even acknowledge the issue thus implying that they're not going to do a thing about it. There isn't even an anti-cheat system installed in the game.
With all of these flaws in mind, I do not plan on buying any DLC nor do I plan on buying the sequel if none of these issues get fixed. This game could have been one of the greatest DBZ games up to date.

As a fan of the LEGO game series, I enjoyed LEGO LoTR. If you've never played a LEGO game, though, I'm not sure if this is the one to start with unless you're a big huge fan of LoTR. One of the things I've enjoyed about the LEGO games is the anarchic sense of humor and the willingness to lovingly goof around with the source material. However, LEGO LoTR is oddly restrained. Maybe it's because it not only follows the story of the film series, but uses actual audio clips in doing so, that the sense of playing around with the material isn't there like it is with the other LEGO games, such as the silent Star Wars and Indiana Jones games. Maybe it was an intentional design choice. The humor is still there, but it's just not there in the same laugh out loud way that previous games in the series had.
Still, the game is fun to play. There's a wide range of characters, but the addition of the Mithril Treasures that allow any character to have the powers of any other character in some ways means that you won't be playing as quite so many characters in free play. Quite literally, once you've got the Mithril Treasures, you can play as a single character in Free Play and accomplish every task without switching out your character.
Pretty much every character of note in the film series makes their way into the game, as well as some that only found their way into the Extended Edition footage. There's also some that never made it out of pre-production, like the love-him-or-hate-him Tom Bombadil. I am not a giant LoTR fanboy but I consider myself decently familiar with the source material both in film and book form, and even I'll admit that there were several characters I had to go to an LoTR wiki to remember who they were. The film's locations are also recreated on a small scale but are instantly recognizable. The details are appreciated especially as the game has an extensive overworld with a lot of secrets and quests to complete.
If you're a veteran of the LEGO games looking to get your fix, or a big huge fan of LoTR (particularly the film series), I'd recommend this title. If you've never played a LEGO game, you may want to start with another title in the series to figure out whether they're your cup of tea before you pick this one up.

It's "OK", but not even the fabled 10.0 overhaul feature list puts it close to the Arma3 feature list and thus I wouldn't recommend it. A bunch of shooters spawned for the new generation of folks that just want their game tightly defined with a ruleset: DayZ, PUBG, this, etc. IE easily digestible candy. If I can make an Arma 50vs match with the game mode of Squad, then it's comparable to a narrow Arma3 feature list and all that's left is the actual delivery of that game mode. Given the Squad forums are wanting new animations, new weapons, new vehicles, it's as if they are trying to build it up to Arma's spec which sits there with all those features and a tonne more and isn't limited to the UR4 engine. I find it impossible to recommend where you make a choice between the two, but if I just pretend for a few seconds that Squad and a specific Arma game were in comparison on their own then I should rightly point out some bias towards Squad as follows:
Engine and graphics: Squad has an edge for standard boxed affects that you would need a combination of mods to achieve in Arma. Especially firing and under fire effects, explosion effects and particles. Arma needs JSRS, Blastcore and some others to be in line and still not as good as the effect of Squad.
Scalability. Performance is optimised for a specific small map PvP experience. Arma will not perform as well with bots on the same engine, or on the 270 square km Altis map. But should it? Should it compare to a 68km squared map? The level of detail is higher. Perhaps it's an advantage for Squad. Nevertheless I think Squad probably does better for FPS in a like-for-like.
Much of this adds up to an apples and oranges review based on a faulty comparison, but I cannot pick a canned game over something I can adapt, has a longer and more successful pedigree, has community developers, greater variety and depth and is at least finished. There's a reason A3 has 4x the players in game, and is two years earlier than Squads release date.
I find a typical review from players stating: "But the cooperation level is so amazing, i'm learning to play with other humans". Wow. I think that's a sad shame on our internet culture, at any given time you can join and cooperate with groups around the world who have been doing the same since the internet was born in every multiplayer coop game. What the issue I have is that it's down to luck if you have a good experience or a bad one, I've had both, leaning very much in the direction of bad. Should I review a game that needs luck to find good cooperation in a public game? Or should i look for a group that plays together well (more sensible approach). Thus again, go play milsim with a military simulator, not what is in effect a public matchmaker of random experience.
Unfortunately that brings be to the negative part of the game as is. You have no choice. Games are matched, you spend ages trying to get your friends onto the same team due to side balancing, only to dfind you are playing versus the server hosts and getting nailed. You have no option to play with a moving target and practice, the firing range is just ...ugh. You can't even zero your weapons on it, there's no range modelled on the guns and Kentucky windage is the primary method of correcting fires.
People want milsim, but they aren't prepared to cooperate for it or invest the time and discipline to join a group. They want milsim but no keybinds. They want to spawn in a battle, to last 15 mins and then go offline. Then if that's you, I think Squad is your choice, for either a public match or organised group play. It's not a crime to want things your way, but you have to be prepared to sacrifice a lot. If you want to invest in something, get Arma, go milsim and enjoy exactly the game you want. Zombies, dinosaurs, or ridculous simulation levels with campaigns and science, exactly how you want it with an amazingly in depth amount of variation and customisation. Arma3 is all things but not quite champion at the small level, it's an offputting simulator to someone needing to shoot another player in the head, now, please. But quite frankly, I don't see the point in having slighly shinier graphics if I can't make it do exactly what I want. Squad isn't a bad game, it's just not different and less capable in so many ways to others and thus I chose to keep my investment in something more in depth. YMMV.

Mabinogi is a very unique MMO and has came along way since 2008 when it was launched. Originally the game was very small with only a small main quest line and a few dungeons the player could partake in. With that being said it had one unique skill that wasn't introduced to the gaming world till LOTRO and that was the ability to play music and not just any music but what ever you wanted. There's a big difference in the 2 games though, like WoW, LOTRO is a tab targeting combat game were you hit tab and start mashing 1, 2 and 3 when ever they light up. Mabinogi's combat system is more strategy based and not tab targeting at all. When you go into combat you decide which skills to use and if they are going to be effective on your current target. Mabinogi is a very unforgiving game in the sense if you decide to use skills that are not going to be effective or deploy them in a ineffective way then you die and yes there is a death penalty like in most KR/JP RPGs.
Mabinogi today has grown huge from the 1 small main story line to 18 very big story lines that completes the last. Outside of the main quests there are things todo ranging from shadow missions to skill based quests. There are so many different things todo in mabi that it will keep you busy for a long time just trying them all out.
A few key features are your char isn't given to you, you have to earn what you got. If deciding to make a magi type char don't expect to get all your spells for free and be ready to put in the work to beable to cast those &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; spells, same goes for higher level skills. It a sense of reward when you do get them and you will remember the blood and sweat you put in for it.
Music - in mabi allows the player to compose any song they want weather against copyright or not so have a good time and try that out(Iron Man on Lute is amazing)
Fantasy Life - If you decide combat isn't your style then there's always crafting and yes you could craft and gain skills from crafting alone with little or no combat.
Lots of Events - I'll be the first to rag on Nexon for being the masters of the F2P MMO model but they do well to keep the player entertained with many events that they host ranging from Zombies to taking a spooky walk thru a hunted mansion.
Overall it is a F2P game with a cash shop so why not give it a try

I have been playing Mabinogi since its orginal US release back in 2008 so this review is long overdue.
If I had to describe Mabinogi in a few words, I have to say that this game has "LITERALLY EVERYTHING".  It amazes me that Mabinogi does not have much recognition in the MMORPG world because this game has great potential if it was optimized better with slightly better graphics.  I know not too many people are fond of the "cute anime" look and prefer stunning graphics.  If that already deters you from the game, I suggest playing games like Vindictus.  But if you are looking for content with a game that has both aspects of dungeoning and a casual social fantasy life, then I would give Mabinogi a try.
===THE SUMMARY===
Mabinogi is a VERY customizable game.  You can play any class you want from lance combat, melee, ninja, alchemy, magic, martial arts, music, puppetry, gunner, and a variety of life production skills.  There are tons of different outfits that can all (unless restricted) be customized by your own color dye.  Mabinogi also has a rebirth system that allows your character to rebirth and start over at level 0 but still KEEP your previous life skill ranks.  This prevents players from constantly grinding levels for ability points.  A lot of the environment in the game is interactive.  You can chop trees, gather wool from sheep, harvest crops in the field, fish at the lake, fight field enemies or bosses, etc.
===HISTORY OF MABI===
In the beginning, Mabinogi was actually a very complicated & challenging game.  You had to learn skills through interacting with NPCS and using the right keywords.  A lot of my friends that started Mabinogi with me instantly quit the game because it wasn't your typical "spam buttons" type of game.  Mabinogi's combat system required strategy and use something like a rock, paper, scissor effect where certain skills worked better against other skills.  If done properly, you could be untouchable by enemies with your combination of skills, but if you just run in there and mesh buttons, you would die in an instant.  Eventually Mabinogi made the game more friendly and made everything much more easier with extras here and there for new players.  This still required players to use the combat properly but at least they wouldn't die so quickly with a finger flick.  They even improved the game by including detailed tutorials that allow players to learn all of the different types of classes & an altruist system that rewards players for helping newer players.
===PROS & CONS===
Now for the pros and cons, here is what you'll need to know:
PROS:
*Customization.  From character look, clothes, color, etc.  Most of everyone in Mabinogi will have their own unique look.
*Content.  Plenty of quests, dailies, generation storylines, saga storylines, etc.  If you start out in Mabinogi, you will have PLENTY of things to do.  Even if you're a long time player, there are lots of dailies and events in the game to keep you busy.
*Class Freedom.  This is not one of those games where you have to worry you will choose a wrong skill tree path.  With Mabinogi's rebirth system, you can literally rank up every skill in this game with time.  You can switch between classes whenever you want because you are not binded to a specific class.  You are just a character learning EVERY type of class skill out there and it's YOUR CHOICE to decide which skill you want to use.
*Community & Support Response.  I know most people will not agree with me on this and I've listed this as a con in one of my Mabinogi videos, but it has changed significantly lately.  I want to say that the Mabinogi community has gotten better and people are more helpful than before.  You will still run into stuck up players that ignore you because they're rich or OP or act childish with their own petty in game dramas a girlfriend & boyfriend here or there.  Nexon's support also got a lot better and instead of waiting for weeks on a ticket response, I've gotten my tickets responded as quick as a few days or even the next day.  Again it varies, so it's a BORDERLINE con.
CONS:
*Cash Shop.  Since this game is free to play, the company has to make their money somehow.  Gachapons & reforges are the most popular sale items in the game.  It benefits most paying players because they can get the latest gears that may or may not be pre-ranked & enchanted or the rarest fashion outfits worth millions of gold.  Everything is RNG so people that spend money on these items may get junk rolls or get rare rolls.  It's a gamble but regardless, those that spend real money in Mabinogi will mostly likely rise up in the game with gold at least.
* Poor optimization.  This game uses so much, it's rather ridiculous that players need to have a pretty decent computer in order to run this game.  Many people complain about game crashing, graphics bugging out, disconnections, etc.
*Economy.  Economy is horrendous.  There are items worth a ridiculous amount of gold such as 50 - 100+ millions.  Most new players will see that as an impossible reach and it is if you are new.  Most merchants in the game are also heartless & rude and can be shady at times.  Once Mabinogi releases a better auction system between player items, this may get better, but for now it's a con.
===SHOULD I PLAY?===
Mabinogi is a decent game for a FREE TO PLAY game.  It's the only game I stuck with for so many years because either I really enjoy the game or I invested way too much time and money to quit.  I've had a few months here and there where I stopped playing Mabinogi to play another game but I would always return back to Mabinogi.  Mostly because the other games I played would always have one or two things missions.  Either it's too combat focused and not enough life skills, or it's got a lot of content but not enough customizations, or it heavily focuses on big groups and can't be solo'd, or it's gender locked and has way too many skill trees. etc.
Mabinogi for me never had that problem.  It has both combat & life skills for the hardcore & casual players, it's got lots of content and lots of customizations, it's got raids for big groups and plenty of missions for solo play, there are no gender locks (though somewhat some race locks on outfits lmao), and of course no skill tree except deciding on whether you want to be a dark knight or paladin.
If anything, I would give it a try if any of this interests you.
Please also check my Youtube channel at mabiBOBO if you want to stay updated with Mabinogi & learn more about the game.

The models in this game look great, but the animations do not. The main character's arms clip into her body, the dragon looks like a hand puppet, enemies cause damage-state animations that you get stuck in... The art of Toren is better ogled from screen shots than experienced first hand, I think.
That's not to even mention the gameplay, which I would describe as a sort-of puzzle game. I say sort-of because none of the puzzles are actually difficult to figure out. There is no satisfaction to be gleaned from standing behind statues to avoid wind, or hitting the dragon three times, or lighting fires with flames taken from already lit torches. Any seasoned gamer has seen those mechanics a hundred times, even if they weren't already simple and obvious. This annoyance is further enhanced when they make you repeat some of the "puzzle" solutions dozens of times. While hiding behind a statue and waiting the requisite 10 seconds for wind to die down so I could run to the next statue for the 20th or so time, I wanted to scream "I GET IT!". I solved this puzzle 10 times in the last chapter, and now you want me to do it 10 more? What am I proving by doing this? It's not hard, unless you count the game's slippery controls and floaty jumps as part of the difficulty. It's just aggravating.
:  This is one of those games that begs for a "It Depends." option on whether I'd reccomend it or not. It's an interesting fantasy world and game concept let down by a lack of gameplay and polish. If you are into games for the sake of art, give it a go. If you are looking for a game that is enjoyable to play, look elsewhere.

The stories that unfold are incredible.
Shortly after breakfast a crazed trio of man-eating dromedaries showed up. We all headed into the safety of our bedrooms.
The dromedaries broke down the front door, then headed around back. We could hear their horrible moaning calls through the walls as they hunted us.
Meanwhile, a wayward shipment of muffalo wool dropped out of the sky. Someone else was having a bad day too, I guess.
After breaking down the back door, the dromedaries entered our compound. War, our young cat, was in the wrong place at the wrong time. She got trampled by the camels while Ray shot at them, to little avail. Like War, Ray was downed quickly under crushing blows and violent kicks.
Immediately following Ray’s fall, five heavily armed members of The Razor Raccoons (a pirate faction) took the opportunity to attack.
Wallace pulled Ray to safety, and Kars went into battle with his trusty knife. Bravely, Kars killed one dromedary before being downed by another. Wallace died under the hooves of a furious and psychotic camel.
The dromedaries turned their aggression towards the pirates next. One of the remaining camels was downed by a pirate wielding a huge steel club, and the other was shot dead.
The pirates then came after the settlers.
Kars lost his right leg, and Wallace was beaten to death.
Ray got off easy with just a bruised arm, but started feeling withdrawal from her go juice addiction.
The pirates decided to kidnap Kars and leave, but not without first kicking the walls and starting a fire in our pantry. During all the confusion, an emu wandered inside and got stuck in our crafting room.
Ray recovered enough to go fight the fire, though she was starting to feel the effects of starvation. She finally collapsed from hunger, withdrawal, and fatigue.
A thunderstorm rolled in, so the fire did go out, but not before destroying a pantry wall and the power lines to the refrigeration units. Most of our meager food supply was lost in the blaze.
A radio message came in from The Razor Raccoons… they’re holding Kars for ransom for 1541 silver, which we must give them within 24 hours. We have a whopping 370.
Lightening struck near the house, starting another small fire.
Ray, the only remaining survivor, passed out from extreme exhaustion.
A heat wave struck, adding to her discomfort and pain.
A group of four tribesmen from the “Coalition of Louir” visited. Before they even got to our compound, two of them started fighting each other, apparently over an insult.
They found the unconscious Ray laying outside what was once the front foyer, but didn’t offer to help. They were deeply upset by the sight of Wallace’s body. They ate a great feast at our table, before leaving.
Ray is now extremely malnourished and has heat stroke.
The window for the ransom demand has just expired. Rest in peace Kars.
It’s 108 degrees inside our base.
Ray has died of starvation.

Money Value: Not worth $10.

Fox, the one that stopped the enemies, was badly burned and injured.  She tried to get into the medical bed but instead collapsed.  Belle was the only one that could save the prisoner (who had a terrible infection from the cat) and Fox (who was severely burned).  Unfortunately, all the death and destruction sent her into a daze.  She went into a depressed state and wandered far away.  A couple of times she walked into the fire and got mildly burned but she didn't finish it.  She was in shock and could not come to. Typer Shark is not one of Popcap's well-remembered titles. Unlike games like Bejeweled, Bookworm Adventures, Peggle and especially Plants vs. Zombies, you'll rarely hear this game being talked about in a discussion about Popcap. Is this because it's a bad game? Not by any stretch of imagination. Here's my review of the game.
You play the game as an unnamed yellow deep-sea diver. He is commanded to grab several treasures from shark and piranha infested waters. You are only given a keyboard as a weapon...??? What? Of all things, a goshdarn keyboard!? Why not a harpoon launcher!? I get It's there to fit into the plot, but... a keyboard. Anyway... As you go on, you encounter more powerful sharks and piranhas, making your venture through the waters much harder. You even encounter robotic sea creatures that shoot missiles and bombs at you! Beyond this, though, there's no real plot. However, it's enough to fit into the gameplay, so that's fine with me.
The graphics are very cartoony, which I'm thankful for. If they were any less cartoony, this game could easily be a horror game. It's overall nice looking. However, one thing I don't like is how Popcap directly ripped sprites from another one of their games, Insaniquarium. I do know that Popcap is a sucker for referencing their older games, which I am not against at all (In fact, that's one of the reasons I love them so much), but I feel this is a bit too far.
This is one of the things I don't like about this game. The music is forgettable, and I barely feel like I'm engaged by any of them (Even the bonus round music). It's not bad by any means, just... Bland.
Now for what you were probs looking for in this review. The gameplay is surprisingly fun. You type to attack the sharks and piranhas. Due to their speed, you can feel your typing skills and reflexes improving throughout the game. There's also a typing test in the beginning that recommends you a difficulty based on your typing skill. As you progress through the game, it introduces much harder enemies, such as sharks that are hard to read until they get to a certain point, sharks that take two or three words to take out, and sharks that mix up the words on them. There are also small minigames throughout the game that include typing random words with increasing values until your air runs out, a maching game involving typing single letters, and... Well, I don't know anything else, because I only took one path through the game.
I give the game a 7/10. It's a fairly fun way of improving your typing skills, and is a good game to pop in during your spare time. Definitely not Popcap's best work, but definitely one you should check out at least once if you like "think fast" types of games.

An interesting mmorpg. Having played many mmorpgs before, mabinogi is a favorite due to its dynamic combat system. There are infinite battle combo possibilities as the gameplay involves fast paced action with a unique do-it-yourself strategy allowing almost limitless freedom to choose how you play. While the game features talents (i.e warrior) like most mmorpg's, it doesn't limit what you can and can't do allowing you to choose what skills from any tab (melee, magic...etc) you want to train giving a really unique gameplay individual to the player rather than restriction, emphasizing complete freedom in how you like to play.
Another appealing factor for mabinogi is the anime-style graphics rather than the traditional realism based graphics that give the game a relaxed outlook rather than a serious tone.
Having played this game for several years and watching it change and grow i can point out a few perspectives on its pro's and cons:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Pro's:
- Freedom to play however you want, as whoever you want to be with no linear path set out for you to take. There are no penalties for doing what you want or neglecting to do certain things if you don't want to. This allows a player to choose what to do, whether it be fighting and training, crafting and trading, or even just socializing.
- Active and alive community full of players from veterans to newbies; never a dull moment no matter where you go (Alexina is one of the most active servers in-game and Dunbarton is one of the most active towns in-game).
- Immersive and involving storyline that spans out several chapters, events, and in-game years that pit you in the midst of the struggle as one of the "milletians" involved in the conflict between the gods and various factions in Erinn.
- Constant updates and add-ons to the game; whether in the form of a new storyline chapter or the many year-round events, mabinogi always keeps you coming back for something new or even something old that is a favorite.
Con's:
- Cash Shop: Some items you might want to acquire (like pets, high grade items or bags for example) are only obtainable through the cash shop, which is if you don't mind the $5-$10 price, and are otherwise difficult to obtain (trading in-game gold for NX codes to get a pet ***not recommended there are many scammers*** or paying millions of in-game gold for a bag or high stat items).
- Skills: Some advanced level skills require immense effort or dedication to obtain (in the form of grinding certain monsters or dungeons to receive quest items or completion points related to the skill you are trying to obtain. Alternatively these skills can be easily obtained by rebirthing into one of the Aces Hero talents, however that also requires direct NX payment or Pons purchased with NX.
- Outdated graphics (however still quaint): Mabinogi was coded and released in an earlier decade where archblade and warframe level graphics were not available. There have been many updates and upgrades since then but no real way to modernize the graphics without creating an entirely new mabinogi game. However the graphics still hold their charm if you enjoy anime-style art.
- Clash of personalities: unfortunately like many online games, mabinogi suffers from groups or individual players who are destructive rather than constructive in the community. This ranges from simple acts of annoyance or "trolling" of the general player-base to out-right scamming and arrogant im-better-than-you attitudes. Thankfully these groups of players are easily identifiable and are only a small part of the much larger community of helpful, respectful, and kind players.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I would say, try it out. If you like it, then enjoy it. If you don't then that's alright too. Don't knock it till you try it. It's one of the very few unique mmo's that are out there that feel different from generic mainstream mmo's.

My opinon on this is kind of two sided. I'm sure many people have stated this, but the combat can be not so great at times, however this does not make the combat terrible. I've played many MMOs and have run into some with far worse combat.
Mabinogis' combat holds up. The fact that Mabinogi isn't completely combat driven helps that.
As far as skills go, theres a lot that will keep you busy. The class system is set in a way that you may have chosen mage, but you can easily learn another classes skills. If it wasn't for that Mabinogi might have been slightly more boring. I know various MMOs have used this same concept, Runescape for example. Back in the day that is what kept me playing that game, and I'm sure this game for just as long, if not longer.
Okay now for the community. Like Any MMO there are helpful players, then there are those stuck up players who don't care about you unless you have something they want, or your what they would call "Strong". During my first few hours of playing I met this player who was a big help with questing. (Seeing as I for whatever reason couldn't make it through) Most of the community I've met through my experience are nice. (Thats just a personal preference of mine)
Overall, I would say if your looking for an MMO that you can invest loads of time into, check out Mabinogi. As long as your into a not so combat driven MMO you should fall in love with it.

Some people have problems getting used to the game, or have issues getting it running on their hardware. Just stepping over to the community with these problems and you will find a very enthusiastic and supportive dev group and player base that offer up loads of support to get you through the rough patch.

As long as this game stays on the current heading, it will become a classic that everyone will remember. I have so much fun with this game that I bought it for all my closest gaming buddies.
If you buy it based on this review, I only hope that you enjoy it as much as I do, or meet me on the server and let me help you work those new shoes in until they are comfortable.

This game was actually placed into my top 20 all time favorites. For a free weekend, I'd say I had a great weekend! I knew it was more tactical based which is a type of game I enjoy playing, but there are a few things I have noticed that took away from my enjoyment of the game. Regardless of the the cons I have noticed, I highly recommend playing this game... Thank  you for the free weekend, I will be buying soon!
Pros:
-Graphically it is well established, although not yet NVIDIA optimized, I had a very smooth gaming experience with zero stutters during graphically intense moments such as explosions and high amounts of gunfire.
-The sound engine is off the charts and gave me chills how realistic it is, better than Battlefield IMHO (I♥♥♥♥♥♥YOU NOT)
-Joining a squad can be both tactical and fun- the community that plays this game is amazing both being very pleasureable to work with towards playing objectives and humorous to chat with.
(The comms sound effect puts the icing on the cake)
-Every complexes in the maps are unique and you won't have deja-vu, which is rare in shooting games with a high player counts.
Cons:
-What frustrated me the most is trying to constantly keep track of and finding particular squad members. Players names don't appear unless you are looking directly at them which I think at least having your squad member's names always show from your hud is the most reasonable route. Because of this I found myself constantly checking my mini map for my squad.
-The pause menus and SL menus need to be simplified. There also needs to be a guide somewhere in control settings for SL's that don't know the controls, forget controls or  rememberwhich icon does what in the SL command menu.
-The inability to select gun attachments is a buzzkill. Sorry, but I don't think that it's fair or realistic to hold restrictions on gun attachments based off of player roles. I do understand restricting gun types based off of roles, but not letting me choose between irons or ACOG is a bit too unfair.

NOTE: While you may see my name on the 'Thank you' screen in the credits, or you may see an item, or an achievement with my name in it, I am not an employee of FobTi Interactive. I have just been friendly with the developer Tibor since he made Obludia, and he has thanked me for the support by making items, or achievements named after me in the game. :)
That said, I am a bit more friendly with the developer than most of the players that will buy this game so I will try to be more critical of the game than someone else because I have to be. Fortunately, I like the game so I don't have to be negative about it, or write a negative review.
Jet Set Knights (JSK) is the second game made by FobTi interactive, a "one-man" gaming studio and developer named Tibor Fobel. I have talked with Tibor for the last couple of years and gotten to know him in regards to his development and found him to be exactly what we want from Indie developers as gamers. Someone that makes games for the pure joy of being a game maker. He works hard to fix and change things he can for the gamers that play and buy his games, as well as making sure they are fun to play. He is also honest, which frankly seems to be lacking in the Indie gaming scene more and more these days. From Obludia to Jet Set Knights I have seen great improvement in not just his design skills, but in the artwork he has been able to make for his newest game. Tibor is a developer that I am happy to support.
JSK is a game that you can describe mostly as a Tower Defense sort of game that uses a 2D platforming style of screen with some slight RPG elements to level your skills. The entire level is on one screen in the side-scroller 2D style where the Tower Defense is you stopping enemies coming from the top down to stop them from getting your little Princess at the bottom! You play in several waves and each wave the enemies become more abundant and faster paced as you get closer to the end of the level and ultimately the level boss. Each level has a boss that you must fight at the end of 5+ waves to finish off that level and win. The bosses are fun and look good. I really loved the artwork on the bosses and you can see a few of them in the Store Page screenshots. After beating the level boss you can continue with the level for higher scores, but enemies become so fast it is very difficult to stay alive. :P
Depending on the difficulty level you start at (Easy, Medium, and Hard) your character starts with different stats for the RPG element of the game. Easy you get 5 HP (Can get hit 5 times before death), down to Hard where you only start with 3 hearts (HP). As you kill more enemies you gain XP and when you "Level Up" you get the choice to use 1 skill point in Attack, Health, Speed (How fast you can move), or Critical+. Attack is usually the best to use early, but at times you want to use HP because it offers the extra benefit of healing you to 100% health on top of giving you another heart so if you are about dead you definitely want to take that. Attack allows you to increase your power and how long it takes to kill enemies who have differing levels of health.
Besides stomping the enemies by doing a Mario-jump on their heads you are given an array of tools to stop them. Stomping on their heads is actually one of, if not the most effective ways on normal enemies to kill them while saving resources at the same time. When I first started playing I didn't realize you could so I ran out of arrows all the time and had to melee up close for extra danger. In the stages you get treasure chests you can open up that contain "ammo". You start with arrows you can shoot and each chest you open adds more ammo. After opening a certain amount of these you can unlock more weapons like fire arrows, ice arrows, thrown axes, ninja stars, etc. It adds a nice variety and you will strategize the ones you want to use most as you learn more.
On top of weapons you get even more power ups during stages. You can get boards that allow you to put up fences around your Princess to slow down any enemies trying to get to her. You absolutely want to do this because if you don't enemies will end your game very fast when they get down to her. There are metal bricks you get as well that allow you to set up turrets/orbs in certain spots on each level to help to clear out the enemies. On top of these you get other power ups that are random. For example, one that looks like a cat allows your princess to shoot projectiles above at enemies and help you out for a limited time. There are hearts to heal, books that blow up the screen to kill all the enemies on it, more powerful weapons you can use for a limited time, time stops, etc. These all help in making you stronger for short bursts and appear randomly so collecting them ASAP is almost always a smart idea, or save a very powerful one if you think it will be a big help later. Plus there are letters separate from the power ups which spell out "B-O-N-U-S" that give you a small mini-game that stops the level to allow you the chance to earn extra tokens for the Artifact-O-Matic!
The Artifact-O-Matic.  This is a slot machine outside the levels on the World Map in the 'Gambling House' that allows you to spin the tokens you earn in the game and earn powerful artifacts that you can equip to help you beat the levels. While I haven't been able to get many of these yet, there seem to be several different ones you can obtain and use to increase your power and dominate levels better. There is the choice on the mini-games screen with a Gameboy on there too that has 3 mini-games too that I guess you can unlock to allow you to play mini-games for extra tokens, or items too. Just a bunch of fun extra stuff to do outside the main game. While there are more secrets and unlockables in the game I don't want to spoil them all, or list them all so I will just leave it at that.
I am solely a single player gamer for most things so I have not yet tried this, but JSK does offer the ability to play local co-op for these levels and survive as long as you can. It also added in a Player vs. Player Local-MP option as well that you can mix it up in, but i have not tried it.
JSK is a very fast paced Tower Defense game that is just fun to play. The pixel graphic style is exactly the kind we expect from the 8-bit era games and looks great for the style of gameplay. The music is top notch and fits the game well. I would like to see more levels added eventually that have more variety in how they work. IF there is anything that FobTi needs to work on is map variety in his games. He has good concepts in the game design and weapons and items, but the maps tend to be very similar as you play through his games thus far and could use some more variety in the future. This game doesn't really have an overall story/point to it either so far, which it could add. Not sure how, but it needs to have some sort of "end", or reason for it. Might be nice to see some story elements, but the lore and story aren't necessary. It is a Tower Defense game so we don't need it, but Tibor has started he has some story/lore and may put it into a comic at some point rather than adding game story. Tibor is very open to suggestions so if there is anything people think would add more to the game he will take it into account if he thinks he can make it happen.
I'd recommend this to Tower Defense fans and those that like a bit of fast paced platforming thrown into the mix to make it more action-orientated tower defense than strategic. There are no pauses here to stop and think out your strategies. It is all on the fly and you must move quickly to stop enemies. I would recommend it for most people when it goes on sale, but I don't think the retail price is too high for it.
JSK includes Trading Cards, and WILL have achievements soon (There is one named after me so I definitely know they are coming. xD).

I'm a huge fan of Dragon Ball, and I've played a number of the games since Budokai. I bought this week one in excitement for the release. I've played the game to storyline completion, and completed almost half of the PQs so far. I've generally enjoyed it, but frustrations are building and I'm no longer certain this was a good purchasing decision.
PROS:
+Customer characterization is cool! You can play as multiple character races from the series, including Frieza-type aliens. Customization allows for specific builds which employ moves or skills from multiple DBZ characters, allowing for an interesting fusion of styles. There's a variety of cool costumes that call back to even the most obscure (such as an outfit Bulma wears on one Dragon Ball manga cover, Arale from Dr. Slump's hat, and the hats Goku and Krillin wear when they attend their first Budokai Tenkaichi).
+Control scheme is simpler and more approachable to those who may not be as experienced with the DB fighting games.
+There are new, original characters for the game's storyline, including the Supreme Kai of Time and Demon God Demigra.
+In the multiplayer lobby, you can goof around by doing hilarious character poses, like the Ginyu Force poses, or Great Saiyaman's entirely too elaborate poses.
+At its strong points, combat feels great, with the exaggerated sound effects, combos, and dramatic camera angles adding a lot of excitement, reminiscent of the show.
PROBLEMS WITH ONLINE PLAY:
Online play is a complicated, fickle beast. There's a lot of problems here.
-First, you have to play online unless your internet connection is off. There's no offline option within the game settings. It will always log you onto the servers. This can be aggravating when there's a lot of server downtime. It can take a long time for the game to boot because it spends a while connecting to the server. Even in single player lobby, if the servers go down, you'll be booted from play and have to log back in.
-Connections can be very unstable. Characters lag across maps and sometimes freeze in place, or enemies don't spawn in. Sometimes the quest will simply freeze upon completion, until one character forcibly closes the entire game. Often, one or more participants will not receive credit, experience, money, or items upon completion. While grinding for items with friends, this can be very frustrating. I am doubtful that this is entirely to blame on my internet connection speed, and feel that measures could've been taken to deal with the issue.
OTHER CONS:
-Item droprate is utterly brutal. Some equipment is purchasable for large sums of zeni in the in-game store. However, some of the more desirable equipment must be unlocked via Parallel Quest. The problem is that it's highly specific and randomized. Quests have secret requirements in order to unlock extra battles or equipment within them. There is very little information to go off of within the game as to what these requirements are (sometimes context or character relationships could provide insight). Sometimes, when you do fulfill these secret requirements, the battle finishes early anyway. And if you do complete the requirements, you still have a random chance of getting the item. This can be extremely time-consuming if there's a particular look or build you're trying to create for your character.
-The difficulty curve can be awkward at times. Computer AI can vary from relentless to completely ignorant. One battle, I might get stunlocked into a corner, another, I might be able to stand next to my opponent and freely charge to super saiyan without so much as a single glance in my direction.
-Some design elements feel cumbersome and purposeless. You are required to walk to whatever game option you want to play. While the idea of Tokitoki City is nice in concept, in execution, it results in players taking one to two minutes to select play options as opposed to seconds. While grinding for item drops, this can cause a lot of annoyance (though the distance is shorter to the PQ desk).
-Sometimes characters can become stuck on objects, forcing players to either end the game in the lobby, or accept a KO in matches.
-Some gameplay mechanics aren't explained to the player, resulting in some early game confusion.
I'm hoping that the developers will consider a number of the major issues, which have been vocalized numerous times by the community, and work to improve this game so that it can achieve its potential. For now, I would advise against most from purchase, though avid fans who are willing to look past problems may find themselves enjoying the highlights.

Toren is a brief, uneven game. Sometimes it shows flashes of brilliance, and others it feels extremely derivative.
The art in the game is sometimes beautiful, and sometimes your eye is drawn to what feels like are out of place modeling or textures that are much lower resolution than their surroundings making them pop out. Sometimes there are graphical errors with the main characters clothing textures.
The animation is fluid, and the controls for the most part feel spot on, but then sometimes such as jumping and when the camera is really touchy and trying to stay behind the character in the dream sequences, the controls falll apart, and feel floaty and unresponsive.
The mythology has the starts of interesting, but never really gets fleshed out, and in the telling is really confusing.
I think the game feels like a would-be spiritual successor to ICO (but not Shadows of the Colossus), that could have used more time in the cooker. It's uneven, and overall mediocre, but the game is still worth picking up for the flashes of brillliance it does have in it's short playtime.
Another note: I was able to beat the game twice and get all of the achievements in 3 hours, but ended up having to idle the game over night to get the rest of the trading cards for it, so keep that in mind when looking at my play time. It is a really short game, but the drop rate of the steam trading cards needs to be adjusted to reflect that.

From a gameplay perspective, this game is super fun.  It's kinda like Diablo meets Custom Robo.  You are given a mech that you are able to customize with a variety of weapons and armor, each with their own benefits and drawbacks.  I'm a bit early in the game so it's hard to say how deep the customization gets, but so far I've been happy with it and I'm constantly switching gear around based on what kinds of boosts or debuffs I get from a weapon/piece of armor.  I imagine as the game goes on, you'll have to be more thoughtful with what you put on your mech since there is a power limit, halting you from putting whatever you damn well please on your mech.  A bit prohibitive, but it's understandable.  The missions are pretty short, at least from what I've played so far (about 10-15 missions, Rank E-D).  The game has a ranking system and the replayability will come from S-Ranking every mission.  If you are looking for a game where you can customize a mech and slaugther a bunch of other mechs, then this is perfect for you.  The $15 price tag is also attractive.
In terms of presentation, the game runs and looks fine.  Weapon effects look cool and the sound effects give you a sense of impact.  The audio sounds a bit too loud overall, since the game is originally meant to be played on a handheld, but you can adjust the audio levels to your hearts desire.  I've had no frame drops in my time of playing so far, so they at least got that down well.  I imagine this game can be played on low-end computers well too since it's just a port of a PS Vita game.
Overall, it's a really fun game that certainly has a budget feel to it, but if you go in expecting that, you'll have a good time.  The most attractive thing about the game is being able to customize a mech, which this game does well.  It's sad that mech games are practically non-existant on PC, but this is a good game to scratch that mecha itch.  Only big complaint is that there is no multiplayer.  This game BEGS to be played with other people, especially since there is an in-game arena where you fight other mechs 1 on 1.  Perhaps that can be added in the future, but I doubt this game will get any post-launch support.
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Tl;dr: For a $15 mech game, it's fun as hell.

What do you get when you throw ICO, the Tower of Babel and a budget of about £15 into a big indie developer pot? This, apparently. Toren is a short little platformer that clearly favours style but manages to get a decent portion of substance in with it. You play as a girl running, jumping and stabbing her way through multiple lifetimes in pursuit of a particularly satanic dragon, in the hopes that doing so will make end the endless day scorching the world into a lifeless husk stop.
The first thing you will notice is that the graphics aren't pretty, in fact in some places they're downright ugly. Only some, though. I've always felt that atmosphere and a coherent style are better than bland hyperrealism, and for the most part the art direction makes up for the flat textures and uncanny-valley faces. There are some cutscenes in a sort of painted style that were freaking lovely though, and it's a shame there weren't a few more. The controls could be tighter, sometimes feeling like momentum is building from nothing, but only once did I die as a direct result of them. Still, for a platformer, they're serviceable at best. For the obvious lack of budget, I only found one actual glitch, involving clipping through the floor in a very specific spot after some very panicky swordplay. People have reported achievements not showing until after you exit the game, but the devs have confirmed this was intentional, so as not to break immersion.
I did have a good time with this. There are some very gorgeous-looking parts and the story leaves enough mystery and room for interpretation while still having clear goals and narrative. I loved the reincarnating, it's that rarest of things in "artsy" videogames: a good idea actually executed well. It's all held together with gameplay that's compelling enough to keep you moving forward. It won't be for everyone; the length in particular I imagine will be a sticking point for some people and if that sounds like you I'd wait for a sale. But it's a nice little thing put together with love and technical competance, and that's all I really want at the end of the day.

It's very important to keep in mind that Proteus is not a game. It is a relaxation toy. It's Dear Esther without the story or the dialogue or the 3D graphics -- that is to say, you walk around an island. You can change the season you're in by stepping into a swirling halo of lights; after you do that, you're basically done with Proteus.
If you have a setup that can really immerse you -- a large screen and good speakers, for instance -- Proteus is a great way to come home after a hard day of thinking and just relax.
This is not the greatest game in the world, this is just a tribute.

Kind of like a 320x200 video game rendering of "Koyaanisqatsi." Not just because its primary appeal is its visuals, but also because of its pretty neat, procedurally generated, Phillip Glass-esque score. The primary mechanic is exploration and the combination of the audio and visuals make it play more like a sort of extended tone poem than a "game," but there are interactive elements and new things to see and discover on different playthroughs.
Not sure if there's enough there to warrant many play throughs, but it is incredibly....relaxing. Its cumulative effect is a bit like popping a couple valium and listening to one of those self-hypnosis relaxation tapes (which wouldn't be a compliment if referring to most games, but in Proteus' case it is). In fact, it's so relaxing that I kind of find the demand to control it to be a bit of an impediment at times. Someone needs to make an "auto-wander" mod for it so I could turn it on and veg out when I'm stressed or just fall asleep to it.

Having played several Mario Kart games, I must admit that I enjoy the variety offered by this Sega alternative.  Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed offers customizable vehicles, three different vehicle modes for different terrains, and a large variety of racing modes.  The solo campaign features the expected World Tour, Grand Prix, and Time Attack modes.  Grand Prix and Time Attack are no different than a Mario Kart game, but World Tour has much variety. (Note, the last Mario Kart I played was Mario Kart Wii, so it is possible Mario Kart has since started offering this variety as well.)
All-Star Racing Transformed offers several different types of game modes in the World Tour campaign:
* Standard Race - 3 laps, use weapons to attack other racers
* Battle Race - at most 3 laps, use weapons to attack other racers, 3 hits eliminates a racer
* Boost Race - 3 laps, no weapons, lots of boost pads
* Boost Challenge - Race through a number of checkpoints before time runs out, time only counts down when you are NOT boosting
* Ring Challenge - Fly through a ring course before time runs out
* Traffic Attack - dodge through cars to reach checkpoints before time runs out
* Drift Challenge - drift through checkpoints along a set path, time only increases when you drift correctly
* Versus - 1v1 race, stay in the lead for a set amount of time or get far enough ahead to eliminate the opponent
* Sprint - solo race, beat the lap time of a ghost
* Pursuit - attack a massive tank that stays in front of you, dodge the tank's attacks, kill it before it kills you
Multiplayer retains only the Race, Battle Race, and Boost Race game modes, but it also offers two additional modes exclusive to multiplayer games:
* Battle Arena - drive around on a small open map using weapons to attack opponents, 3 hits eliminates a player
* Capture the Chao - pick up a Chao creature and bring it to a dropoff area to score, attacking the player with the Chao will cause the Chao to drop and another player can pick it up
Living up to the title, race cars will transform on different levels to account for changes in the course.  Levels feature a mixture of land, sea, and air racing, so you may find yourself driving a car, boat, or plane as you race to the finish.  If cars transforming wasn't enough, the race tracks will also change between laps, so you may find yourself flying in lap 3 even though you used a boat in laps 1 and 2.
In addition to the transformations, each driver also has several mods you can apply to the vehicle.  Mods are unlocked by leveling up a driver.  Drivers earn experience for each event they complete regardless of whether or not you win or lose, though you do get much more experience for winning.  The mods may affect each driver's vehicle differently, but in general they take a point away from one category and add it to a different category.  The mods are:
* Standard - default stats
* Balanced - usually takes a point off the highest stat and gives it to the lowest stat
* Handling - takes a point off Speed and adds it to Handling
* Acceleration - takes a point off Boost and adds it to Acceleration
* Speed - takes a point off Handling and adds it to Speed
* Boost - takes a point off Acceleration and adds it to Boost
* Console Mod - generally maxes out Speed and/or Boost at the expense of other stats (this mod must be unlocked in the World Tour campaign rather than by leveling up)
But how does the game actually play? Is it fun?
Short answer: YES!
Long answer:
It will take you a bit of time to get used to this game.  There are several tricks you'll need to learn to help you race faster, such as knowing how to get the starting boost and when to perform aerial acrobatics, but you will quickly get the hang of things.  The car is by far the easiest vehicle mode to control.  The boat and plane take a bit of getting used to, but none are terribly frustrating after a bit of practice.  There are also plenty of characters with different stats, so you'll certainly be able to find something that suits your play style.  (In fact, there's more than enough characters, many of which you will likely never use.)
I enjoyed playing my way through the campaign.  The difficulty curve increased at about the same rate as my skill, so the levels got harder as I got better.  There were a handful of tracks I had to play several times, but for the most part I was able to complete each level in 4 tries or less.
Multiplayer is where this game really shines, assuming you have friends to play with.  The game supports 4 player local play and up to 10 players online, which can be a mix of local and network.  The silliness and chaos of casual races with friends is great, but there is also a small competitive community if you're into that instead.
One point of complaint is that the game artificially increases the game time by trapping you in non-skippable menus after each race.  It takes 35 seconds to restart a level after you fail, 55 if you want to change characters or difficulty.  You will certainly be button mashing that :XBA: button to get through these screens as fast as possible, but this still amounts to over an hour of your life wasted in menus if you play through the campaign.
Another point of complaint is that the ability to fully customize races is missing.  I'd like the ability to specify which weapons are available, or change the rules of the race.  Maybe put on low gravity, faster cars, or some other crazy mix of custom rules.
My Game Completion info:
I beat all World Tour levels on Hard difficulty.  This unlocked a 6th cup and Expert mode.  I then beat all the levels in the 6th cup on Hard except the last level (which requires you to beat the entire game on Expert in order to unlock. No thanks!  I've had enough of this game artificially increasing game time.)
I also beat the first 5 Grand Prix cups on Hard difficulty.  This unlocks another 5 Grand Prix cups in mirror mode (which I ignored).

This is another success in the Lego series of game. The only one i had previously played before this one was the Star Wars saga game which i really enjoyed so i was glad to see they had expanded on a winning formula and managed to keep fun as the main feature of this game.
This game still has the wacky humour of previous games although has included the voces for characters instead of having mute characters. So overall i'd recommend this game to everyone especially if you enjoy the Lord Of The Rings films or books. It may be aimed towards a younger audience but even as an adult i really enjoyed it. It's a great game to just pick up and play when you want to relax and just play a fun game. It's a 9/10 for me.

Awesome game to play if you enjoy a tactical squad based multiplayer shooter with large scale battles, a heavy emphasis on teamwork and communication. Played it only for a few days during the Free Weekend and only played Advance and Secure (AAS) and as Squad Leader three times So i cannot speak for every aspect of this game, but from what i have played I would recommend it to anyone who is looking for more from a first person shooter and wants more squad interaction, teamwork and tactical thinking.
Your Gameplay involves and relies heavily upon:
Situational awarness
-Check your corners, keeping your ears open and listening. A hostile's foot steps, grenade hitting the ground and sound of either an enemy reloading, the click made from switching to fully auto on some weapons or swapping gear.
This will change you and your squad's effectivness in urban and close engagements. Listening for vehicles and shots in the distance, telling the differance between a AK and a M4 shot in the distance and sniper shots.
Relay information to your squad and squad leader. Getting the upper hand is key. Don't forget your enemy is also doing the same and you can get caught bandaging yourself, switching a weapon or reloading if no one in your squad is watching your back and you don't communicate that to them. Some situations and positions can become untenable past a point and you can end up on the defensive the rest of the match if strategic positions are not made against or taken from the enemy.
Careful, Decisive Planning and Good Communication
-As Squad Leader and as any of the other roles most of this also applies, things can get hectic fast when overwhelmed with coordinating with those around you Via Proxy Chat, those in your squad Via Squad Radio Chat, all the other Squad Leaders on your team Via the general 'Command Radio' Chat channel or contacting an individual Squad Leader directly Via their own seperate 'Command Radio' channel using the Num Pad Numbers coresponding to that Squad's Number as that Squad Leaders channel. To clarify more, one channel for all leaders to communicate on and one channel for each Squad Leader to communicate directly to on the Num Pad.
You will need to relay Compass Bearing's on Hostile Contacts (Infantry or Vehicle). Map grid locations on Hostile Contacts to Advance, Suppress or Flank, enemy mortar emplacements, locations for mortar strikes and locations of friendly forces. Failing to act and respond, quickly and decisively will have consquences for you, your squad or the team when trying to defend or capture an objective, possibly getting you, your squad or friendlies killed.
Squad lead also has the ablility to deploy weapon emplacements (Mortars, .50 Cal. Machine Guns) and defensive emplacements (Sandbag emplacements, Forwad Operating Bases, Indirect Fire Shelters and fortified wall structures etc.) These require supplies from your main base with supply runs in a logistic truck which can be attacked.
You Will Be Doing This Under Fire.

Infantry you may or may not see
Vehicles too far or too close
Machine Gun nests Friendly or Hostile
Mortars raining upon you or your Enemy
I highly recommend this game and if you're interested watch some videos online as there is alot more to this game than i alone can cover without experiencing it yourself with more to come. The sound design is so well done the battles feel alive and deadly my heart was racing a few times when things were tense. The shots in the distance and up close, the cracks of the bullets flying past your head and hitting the ground next to you, the explosions of vehicles and mortar strikes. Gunfire and explosions are loud, as they should be and communicating in a heavy fire fight can get difficult.
Great particle effects and sounds. You see and hear the dirt and gravel fall to the ground so realistically, from grenades, RPG's and mortars. Tracer rounds in the .50 Cal machine guns with bullet drop. Vehicle sounds are really good also the vehicles sound as they should. The diesel engine on some of the tracked Soviet era APC's are phenomenal. The diesel motor has a distinct rhythm to it making is sound like its old left over from the cold war, and the vehicles sound heavy duty.
The lighting and visual effects are also very well done with thought put into them thick plumes of black smoke off burning vehicles simulating the fuel burning pouring out this really dark cloud, columns of dust, dirt and debris from explosions. There are some maps during the sunset which are very pleasing to the eye and the lighing comes nicely through the trees. Shadows give you or enemies away
The battles are very intense, if shot a once you will bleed out to a incapacitated state if you do not bandage yourself immediately. If incapacitated you will require a medic to stablize then heal you. Enemies can be difficult to spot depending on your attention to detail, you're FOV settings and monitor set up. i played at 100, the max at 120 and have a 60HZ monitor, so keep it in mind when adjusting.
It is very team oriented, going alone without being stealthly is very risky. Suppressive fire is more important since you can die very easily, poking your head out or running to cover at the wrong time will get you killed either clipped by a stray bullet or picked off by a sniper. Cover, stance and orientation can change taking a bullet to the head or taking it to the chest and vice versa so keep it in mind.
I make the game sound very unforgiving which it can be when new, but you will adapt your playstyle and learn the mechanics fairly quickly. There is a rally point mechanic which allows a limited number of squad respawns in the field and only allows the Squad Leader to place one when one other squad member is present and only once the cool down has expired (few minutes) Forward Operating bases have unlimited respawns, but every death has a respawn timer. so there can be really long fire fights if neither squad kills the other's squad lead before they have a chance to put down a rally point or short ones if the you or other squad does. This also helps reduce but not get rid of long walks from the main base, so make it count. Firefights can get really big and can go on for a while fighting for an objective, taking different approches in the process, the tide can turn quickly if a team gets the upper hand. Vehicles also have respawn timers and can be repaired at base or in the field by building a repair and resupply point.
I didn't have any issues with bugs really but heard some people could not shoot through some vehicles to hit the driver this i encountered also. Some people fell through the map and some spots you could see through the map to the empty canvas the game world is painted on, and a server kicked everyone and I (18 players total) out of a match mid game for some time out reason, not sure what that was about. The game is still in alpha so i understand a few issues are going to be present and you'll be hard pressed to find even a finished game to be completely bug free.
There are some things i would like to be in or done differently however. Only the three basic stances, i hope they impliment one more inbetween stance between crouching and prone to lower your silouette and reduce sound while moving at the of cost movement speed. i found my self Crouching and leaning right to stay in some cover, not asking they change the crouch they have but add an additional stance inbetween. I don't understand digging a mine into a concrete bridge or road. Not knowing where in the body I was shot and where it came from made it hard to determine shot location. a visual dimming or sound cue utilizing surround headphones would be interesting. Increase respawn timer just a little more.
The game is Alpha so some things are still to come and isn't fully balanced yet and vehicles have just been put in.
I'm looking forward to what gets implemented in the future and the games release

The way the death-revive system currently works is that mild damage makes you bleed and anything above that puts you to black screen and to wait for a revive. Just... why? Why would you want your player to spend a big portion of their game in such a stunned state? I mean... in a real war you would already be presumed dead in such state. Just please, give the player a chance to look around them, crawl and maybe even give them a chance to shoot their pistol aswell. Or maybe give the medic a chance to carry away the wounded? This would also tackle the problem of people giving up too easily despite of medics being nearby.
At its current state, the death-revive system is more like punishing teamplay for making two people momentarily blind and useless because of the mistakes of one individual. As a medic I often felt that the right option was to say screw this and just to look for enemies to kill despite of all the wounded allies nearby.
