Mabinogi is a fantasy life MMO, with a lot of content aside from fighting that is much more interactive than most other MMOs. Also, it is NOT PAY-TO-WIN.
Hi. I urge you to strongly consider giving this game a try; you may just find it worth your time, and if not I won't stop you from turning away. If you don't care for some sections I made in this review, scroll past them. But - trust me that CHARACTER, COMBAT, and CONTENT are worth the read. Subsequently, I will try to the best of my ability to summarize different aspects of the game I have categorized this review into, in an effort to pique your interest in trying out MY FAVORITE GAME IN THE WHOLE WIDE WORLD.
1. INTRO: Mabinogi is an MMO game different from any you've ever played. If you plan to read on, throw out all you know old-school tab-targeting hotkey-mashing MMOs. If that's what you like, you DEFINITELY should try this game, because it'll be a very interesting experience for you. Mabinogi has no stupid beginner collecting/grinding quests, no slow leveling and skill-acquiring, no long exhausting distances to travel. In fact, suppress what you know about every MMO you have ever tried, because this game is just that different.
2. FLAWS: I'll get the bad and ugly out of the way first so they scare you away before and not after you spend all this time reading my review.
- This game is run by Nexon America, the same publishers of Combat Arms and Maplestory. Nexon users have reported bad experiences with customer support but it will be different for everyone.
- The game will go down for maintenance subjectedly, sometimes up to thrice a month, but Nexon will give a 10-minute warning for the scheduled ones which usually only last hours.
- Crashes are rare but not unheard of. Only people with personal shops lost items before in a crash, and Mabinogi's servers have only crashed once or twice in the past 6 years.
- Bugs are rampant in this engine like an infestation of Bethesda Games' code's bugs with a mutation of gun-powered butts that just spray♥♥♥♥♥♥everywhere and spit in your face to top it off. None are game-breaking, but some annoying bugs are seen in aspects like user interface.
- Players can experience NA server lag because they are not timezone-based. From the East Coast, my latency in Tarlach is generally smooth.
Still reading? I hope you are finding tolerance in these errors and will consider giving this game a chance. Read on.
3. CHARACTER: Your characters are classless, cloneless, and 100% customizable. You will never find another person exactly like you. You will choose from different eyes and hairstyles, colors for both, as well as age and gender. You can shape your character however you like - your first one even has access to ANY premium facial feature (disregard what the game says about giving premium features to your first character).
There is ZERO class selection. ZERO. Even after you select a talent, you are completely free to assign Ability Points to WHATEVER you wish along the way. Your skills train by actively using them and meeting requirements rather than by level. Spend AP (earned by leveling) to upgrade skills to the next rank. HOWEVER - you never run out of AP because of the rebirth system which I explain later in this review. Skills have 15 ranks each, and reward you with master titles when you complete the highest.
Different schools of combat can be focused or, if you choose, not focused: Bows, 3 kinds of Alchemy (quite similar to Fullmetal Alchemist itself, even), Magic, or even Bard, Puppetry, Gunner, and martial-arts-like Fighter. Three elemental types in the game add to the dynamic fighting system - Fire, Ice, and Lightning. There are also life skills, like tailoring, blacksmithing, and fishing.
A rebirth system allows you to reset to a current Level of 1 every few weeks (recently changed to every week), giving free regular access to more Ability Points to rank skills while keeping EVERYTHING about your character, while resetting only your age, current level (you maintain a total level), and if you choose, looks.
4. COMBAT: similar to a kind of Rock, Paper, Scissors. I would define it as strategy combat. It requires a degree of timing and reaction-based approach. Skills are loaded and executed.
5. COMMUNITY: There are guilds. Social interaction is a HUGE part of the experience of Mabinogi. Differences between any two can mean nothing at all. A friend window allows an email-like system. Gestures allow people to animate characters to fit their mood. Nothing at all can be transferred across the 4 servers, save friends and IM messages.
6. CONTENT: You can fashion yourself with a HUGE selection of clothing items and dyes, or work on Life skills. Lack of classes allows for free switching and hybrid builds fit to your own playstyle. You don't have to find a single monster to bash the entire game - hone a life skill instead and be a merchant. You even own your own free Homestead.
7. EVENTS: Nexon will add friendly (though oftentimes, very cheesy) events almost weekly where players participate in certain objectives to win rewards. None ever require pay-to-win or elite levels to take advantage above others.
8, PETS: though most are bought with real money, the game grants you two free permanent mounts as you complete the beginner quests. All pets fight for you, are shared among ALL characters, and have inventories. Many have unique abilities.
9. PvE: Enemies are found all across.
Grinding is nonexistent in Mabinogi; it is never a requirement. In fact, the game penalizes your experience-gain for fighting in overworld fields for extended periods.
Raids are in the form of field bosses which appear at certain times throughout a real-life week. Some will require upwards of 40 skilled Mabinogians to defeat, others may only require a few and have much less threat.
10. PvP: Fighting other players is another very open-ended aspect of Mabinogi. One method is dueling a friend 1v1 anywhere. The other is arenas. PvP rewards are not a huge part of this MMO.
11. STORY: The story is in installments called Generations. The interactive anime-based storyline is a sufficient length and is regularly updated. The mainstream story quests are completely optional, but they do delve your character deep into an enticing and dramatic plot.
There is just so much content in Mabinogi that I will never be able to sum it up in a review. Use
, the most complete community wiki you will find for the game - it will answer mostly ALL of your questions as you learn to play.

Played this over the free weekend and I really enjoyed it.
I gotta warn you that this game is not for everybody.  For one thing, funnily enough, I wouldn't classify it as a "shooter"; even though shooting is a big portion of the game, if you're in it just for the fighting, you're going to get bored when you have to drive (or even walk, if there's no rally points or FOBs set up) for quite a while.  Honestly, it feels like the main focus of the game isn't on the gunplay (even though it's really nice), but rather on the Squad-play.  Everything is focused around communication and coordination between you and your squad, and the squads work together, rather than you just fighting around with the other players on you team.  This is why having a microphone is a *MUST*.  Even though you can make it without a mic, you can also go through life with one leg on crutches, but you're going to feel hampered in everything you do.
I enjoy the fact that you can build defenses.  One game we set up an awesome sandbag and MG-nest perimiter around the objective we were defending, which was actually pretty cool.  Had the enemy not run out of tickets before they tried to assault our fortifications, I'm sure it would have been a fun little battle.
This honestly feels more like the game Rising Storm 2: Vietnam should have been - long moments of stillness, the sound of gunshots ringing out from a firefight between players about a mile out, the sounds getting louder as your transport gets you close, walking through your team's forward operating base and catching pieces of conversations other players are having through VOIP, you just a background character in their experience.  I'm not sure how the game manages to make it happen, but it allows players to create an atmosphere in their communication, teamwork and individual actions through the "dull" moments, so that when you do finally start exchanging fire at hostiles, it really is something that you dread and look forward to.
RS2 I think is a little too action-oriented, and the constant death in that game makes everything, especially trying to survive, a futile struggle; in Squad, even though it's very easy to get killed, it's also a bit harder to get hit - and if you go down, a medic can revive you to keep you in the fight.  At the same time, I appreciate that it is not on a level of autistic realism that ARMA is muddled with.  It'll take you a couple of hours to get the hang of Squad, but it's not overburdened with controls and commands and other crap.
I'd say, from my 8 hours of playing, the biggest issue was just how far it is from home base to the other points.  If your team doesn't have an FOB and your squad doesn't have a ralley point, and no one is running logistic truck runs, and your SL doesn't let you have access to a vehicle (or there isn't one available at spawn), you're going to be doing a LOT of walking.  However, if you get in a good squad who isn't afraid of helping out a scrub, it's quite a fun experience.
I don't think it's quite $40 worth at this point in time (again, a shooter where only 20 to 40 percent of your total experience will involve shooting at something is a hard sell to make to a player), but I'll definitely pick it up next time it goes on sale or I have a couple of extra bucks to spend on buying it full price (something I've only very rarely have done), because I definitely want to get back into the warzone.

I have a love-hate relationship with this game.
The Pros:
Fun & interesting vehicle building system
Fast-paced combat
Loads of unique and interesting weapons
The Cons:
Horrible Matchmaking - Matching people with only gray or blue tier weapons against those with purple should NEVER happen, yet it consistently does, meaning that it is next to impossible to win against them.
Janky Physics - Trying to drive in a straight line can be difficult at times. It feels like some maps should be ice themed, because you'll just slide around with little control if you have a fast vehicle.
Crafting Extortion - To craft parts, you need to spend in-game currency. Lots of it. For basic stuff. You can only get this currency by buying some with REAL money, or grinding the market by selling fuel, scrap, and crates. This borders on pay to win.
The XP System - Since the only way to get XP is to damage enemies, you will get next to nothing if you are ganked at the start of the match, which will happen frequently. You also receive no items after a match if you lose, which is infuriating if you are matched against players with gear much better that yours.
In Conclusion:
When this game performs as it should, it is amazing. When it doesn't however, it is an absolute disaster. The devs definitely need to fix the matchmaking, touch up the handling on certain maps, and revise the crafting system, but overall, this is definitely worth a try for a free download.

DragonBall XenoVerse is by far the best game they may have created in turns of their franchise, however, it is not the spotlight of putting it on the PC Master Race, but the fact that it lacked the true nature that of DragonBall Z. The game takes a turn to a completely different prespective similair to Another Road for PSP.
It uses a combination of these games:
- Dragon Ball Z: Tenkaichi Tag Team (PSP)
- Dragon Ball Z: Budokai Tenkaichi (1 not 2 or 3)
- Dragon Ball Z: Shin Budokai
The main aspects are from Tag team and Tenkaichi and removing alot from the previous games to make up for the graphics and high end processor power. Basically, everything in this game is merely cosmetic.
What is good about this game?
- Various selectable characters, including your own avatar!
- Custom Created Characters with their own stats.
- 3 Vs. 3 Gameplay battle. Somethign that DBZ has really had and needed.
- Gameplay mechanics and smoothness of game is well balanced for 60 FPS.
What isn't good about this game?
- Transformations once again, are limited, very limited (You can only carry 1 transformation, transformations are one-time execution and cannot charge Ki to sustain them. This is not how DBZ is).
- Skills are bound to one avatar, skills won't change on transformation so you end up having only 1 setup.
- 7 Slot System returns from Budokai series with downside. You have 7 slots to setup your moves and abilities, but are restricted to certain sections, including a transformation (4 Super, 2 Ultimates, 1 Evasive).
- No Saiyan Overdrive System, characters will reach a very low-limited power level, max Level of 50, 150 ATB Points.
- No secure online system, cheating is inevitable. 999 ATB stats on all attributes. Go figure.
- Repetitive Combat Strings with no Cancel/Trick Moves or strategy (You can continuously use the same attacks: XXXXY (repeat) till out of stamina or your opponent stops you.
If there is any hope of truely getting the DBZ feel out of the next game, these are the recommended changes that would improve it:
- Return Budokai or Budokai Tenkaichi style Battle Strings and System (Basic Attacks, Smash, Charged Smash, Ki Charging)
- Skill System to Raging Blast, Tenkachi 3, Budokai 3. Transformations should be separate from Move List, and characters should be leveled up higher in order to be able to achieve higher transformation systems.
- Restore Ki Charging (Not a Skill on a wasted slot)
- 8 Slot System (4 Supers, 4 Ultimates, of 2 Ultimates being Evasive, Defesive attacks or abilities) These slots should not take transformatons.
- Transformation Slots (4 Slots) since this game uses D-Pad, it can use of them directions for transformation menu and then use the (XYAB) buttons to choose your transformation, limiting characters to up to 4 transformations.
- Restore Overdrive system, lose your transformation if you get damaged too much without rest or counter attacks, a fatique meter ( or if stamina reaches 0 ) you lose your transformation. Allow transformations to boost your stats by training in those transformations instead of leveling up your base form.
In all the game is okay, but it not a comparison to what Tag Team was like, or Raging Blast 2. Better luck next time. Hope Dimps, or Namco Bandai make a better game this time.

Tales from the Borderlands is an episodic narrative driven Point & Click set in the insane world of Pandora. This is a rather interesting game as the Borderlands series is not known for its stories and is Telltale's first attempt to venture into video game IPs unlike their previous takes on famous TV shows like Game of Thrones or comics like The Walking Dead. We start off as a Hyperion employee named Rhys who is on his way to his boss’s office for a promotion only to find that his boss has been thrown out of an airlock and his nemesis has been made the new boss. Rhys has unfortunately been “promoted” to janitor and vows to get revenge. Luckily for him he managed to discover a multimillion deal and decided to steal it from under the new boss’s nose. In order to accomplish this Rhys and his best friend travel to Pandora and this is where our journey truly begins.
Upon landing they soon discover how strange and violent the people on that planet are and quickly get themselves into trouble. The unique thing to Telltale's take on Borderlands is that you are not some gun sling badass and has never seen anything more violent than fake finger gun fights in the office. He is very out of his element on this planet and much of the humor comes from his reactions to all the crazy events that occur to him. His only real talent is hacking and even then he is not very good at it. After a while we are introduced to the second character that we will control throughout this game called Fiona who is a native Pandorian and a scam artist. Through a strange turn of events both characters soon meet and try to survive together. Fiona may be a much tougher person than Rhys though she is no fighter so they usually deal with danger by running, hiding or talking their way out of it.
You will on rare occasions be able to control your character and solve a simple puzzle but the game mostly has you sitting and watching with the occasional dialogue choice. It works in its favor as the parts where you control the character are by far the worst since your character walks way too slow and has you solve extremely simple puzzles that make you think “Why did they even bother to put this in?”. Like other Telltale games this title is heavily reliant on Quick Time Events and will frequently throw some your way to make sure you are still paying attention. While you have control of a character you can access an inventory system that show you what items you have on you but it is completely useless and never used making it an unneeded gimmick. A nice little detail is that you can open some certain crates or steal from certain people to get money which you can then use to buy masks or give your car some style in certain scenarios. Both are completely just cosmetic and are gone from the game before you can blink but it's a rather nice touch.
The story is pretty funny but is also shockingly engaging, tragic and mysterious. You see the story is being told by your two characters as some unknown man kidnaps them and demands to know about what they have found in their travels. Who he is and what he wants is a real mystery for most of the game and he comes off as a really cool character. Cool characters is what this game has in spades, nearly everyone you meet is memorable in some way or another since everyone on Pandora seems to be balls to the wall insane. Old characters from the Borderlands series also make an appearance here and there like Scooter and a few of the Vault Hunters. Vault Hunters are exactly what the name says for those unfamiliar with the series. Even if you are not familiar with the Borderlands franchise the games barely have any stories to them so you will get the gist of it in no time. All you need to know is that Vaults are said to have great riches and everyone wants to enter one. Only thing you will really miss out on is the cameos of old character as you will likely have no idea who they are.
Graphics retain that comic book look of Borderlands and looks very true to its source material. Seeing the world of Pandora through the eyes of someone who can't fight suddenly makes you realize what a horrible place that planet is. It helps you sympathize with the characters as well as capture a nice blend of thinking you are going to die and chuckling to yourself in disbelief as your character is saved by a stroke of luck or even pulls off something awesome in a few cases. As I mentioned before this title has a great blend of storytelling methods other than humor and has some shockingly powerful moments. It knows exactly when to be serious, how to present the illusion of choice and when to pull out the dubstep vs space ninja death race battles. The ending left it open for a season 2 though it didn't feel like a cliff hanger was satisfied and was done in a far better way than their previous Game of Thrones game. Tales of a Borderlands is in my opinion Telltale's finest work yet and I would highly recommend it to anyone that enjoys the genre even if they are not a fan of the source material.

This is a great basis for a future development, but as it stands at the moment, i didn't find it a great experience.
The game itself is so clunky, neither the platforming or fighting mechanics work well, it's too easy to accidentally fall off something and the checkpoints feel really far apart because it takes so long and so much effort to get anywhere, so you get frustrated. It's also never very clear what's going on or what you're supposed to be doing, so i spent even more time just wondering around.
The major problem i had was the "dreams" being optional though. I'm willing to forgive a game a lot of sins if it has good aesthetic and a great story. I think this could have both of them, but i spent the entire game going "Huh? Who's that dude? What's going on here?" because i missed the very first optional dream, as they weren't explained, and later in the game that particular dream statue is unuseable. Each dream gives you part of the back story, and without it, you miss a huge chunk of plot, so i was annoyed by how easy they were to not see, and by the fact that the first one at least isn't compulsory.
Missing a dream also means you actually miss out on a hefty amount of gameplay; it's a short game, and each dream is a few mins of new content, so they're sort of screwing themselves by making them optional as well.
Overall i found that the music was nice, the palatte was pretty and there's  a lot of potential here, but really, unless you've totally run out of something to play, i would probably give this one a miss.

This is a summary of my review video, which I encourage you to watch if you are looking for a more in-depth review.
First off let me state, Yes to this game, but only if it is 50%+ on sale.
Toren is a third person platformer-esque explorational adventure. The graphics fit well with the artistic expression of the game, despite not being the highest quality. The sound, story, and concepts are esoteric, and require patience more than skill or knowledge to complete. As the movements of the character feel sluggish, and the platforming of the game can best be described as guided.
The game is balanced off of learning by failure, rather than learning by testing the limits of your environment. You almost need to fail most of the time in order to move forward. They have integrated a very thorough checkpoint system, however, so you do not lose much progress when you die. For me, I did die very often and have to reload more times than I enjoy.
The environment is abstract, leaving you with more questions than answers, and leaves you confused more than not. The ending does wrap up the story nicely, but when I think about my time in the game, it didn't draw me in enough to want to know more. This made my progression through the story very grating.
The art style was beautiful, the gameplay was a bit clunky, and the story was unclear and confusing until the end. The game relies very heavily on patience to make it through the puzzles and challenges, and you have to be okay with multiple reloads as you progress in order to enjoy it. I would say this would be worth getting if it was on a decent sale. It works, but just barely, and designed to slow the player down as much as possible. A very high level of patients is needed.

When Proteus first came out, there was a lot of controversy over whether or not it counts as a game. Because if you don't think about it, there's nothing to do, no overarching story, no buttons to press, just one decently sized possibly alien island.
I absolutely believe this counts as a game. More specifically, a child's game. This is how wee babes see the world: as something weird and beautiful that NEEDS to be explored. In Proteus, your entire goal is to do whatever. You interact with the world as a child does: by running at things and seeing what they do. This game will be a million times better once Oculus is made usable, and a million times more if we ever get haptic gloves out of them. The idea is total immersion into a brand new environment and learning how it exists. So no, it's not a classical game, but that is in no way a problem.

Let me just start off by saying, I appreciate this game for exisiting. There's a certain charm to be found in games like this that don't exist anywhere else. Charm that exists in the game's stunning environmental visuals, and soundtrack. Games like Ico, or Shadow of the Colossus seems to have had some sort of impact on how this game came into fruition, and because of that I can say I'd rather live in a world where this game was made, than not.
With that out of the way, I need to address some issues I have with the game overall. While the visuals are beautiful, character models seem to have not had the same attention to detail put into them as everything else. Character animations feel rough, as do the cutscenes, and a lot of the time, the main character had an expression on her face that I can only describe as goofy. Also, the way the story is presented could have used some work as well. There's seems to be a lot of interesting lore hidden throughout the world to better explain everything for those willing to dig deeper, but I myself couldn't really find anything to latch onto, and that's due in part to the shortness of the game.
Concepts for puzzle solving are introduced through tutorial segments, but are rarely ever used again, and that's a shame because there were plenty of opportunities for them to branch out beyond what the game had. Combat felt sluggish, hitting enemies never felt that satisfying, and platforming felt really floaty. Sound effects could have also used some more work, since I got tired of hearing that dragon's screech consistantly.
Despite all this though, I still found the game worth buying at a sale price. There was a lot here that I really enjoyed, and despite my minor gripe about the length of the game, the hidden backstory does encorage multiple playthroughs, that wouldn't be a chore to go through due to the length of the game. I don't hate this game at all, and I do highly recommend checking it out. It's one of the better indie games I've played this year, and I'd love to see this company go and make something else to showcase their talent even further. But for 10 dollars, I'd suggest waiting for some sort of price drop like I did.

When you first make a character in Hero Siege and begin on Act I, you'll find it difficult. You'll find the game frustrating. But, once you overcome the restlessness that comes along with starting a new game and find yourself settled with the game, prepare to become fully infatutated with Hero Siege. Hero Siege has a lot of great points, as well as bad, which you can easily find out either by reading reviews on the game or buying it and finding out wether you dislike/like the game there. Don't let the reviews sway your mind to only take one look at the game and either buy or ignore the game. See for yourself thoroughly, wether or not you want the game, because Hero Siege isn't your average game.
As I said before, Hero Siege has its good and bad points, the things that determine its quality. Some good things about Hero Siege is that it twists RPG elements in a good way. For example, normally in quests for RPGs, you'd have to travel through multiple environments, defeat a couple of enemies, or retrieve something important to the quest giver in order to receive a reward that you already knew you'd get (for the most part). But, in Hero Siege, you'll never know what you'll get. Maybe some new armour, maybe a buttload of coins. (I find the mystery in that enticing.) Your reward varies, wether or not you did something difficult. Adding on to this, a lot of quests in RPGs have you running around and traversing multiple stages/environments, which again, is different from Hero Siege, where your quest and everything needed to fulfill it is right on one screen from your quest-giver to your objective(s) in the quest.
As I said before, though, Hero Siege also has bad things about it. For example, it's hard to get into at the start, as I said before. Trying to play with friends is a pain, and if you run on a toaster and find out that the game only allows the FPS to go up to 60, you'd die by the pain that is lag. As well as the fact of all the bugs that involve relics and the stages that can knock you into a gate that you will never be able to leave.
But y'know, Hero Siege is a perfectly good hack 'n slash in my opinion, though I have almost no experience with games like these outside of the game itself. Besides, all these reasons that represent Hero Siege's "quality" doesn't really matter all that much because it doesn't matter wether in some peoples' eyes it's a good game or not. What you think of the game is what matters. I recommend this game because that shows what I think of Hero Siege.

A game that shouldn't be good, but is.
First, some basic points:
Graphics:  Very poor.  The best that can be said about them is that they are functional.  In fact, they would be considered poor in the days of 8-bit computing.  Developers seem to compete to see who can produce the worst graphics in this genre so I'm not surprised.  But I am disappointed.
Sound: Atrocious.  The worst soundtrack I've ever heard.  Instead of going for an ambient, mood-enhancing backing sound, we have repetitive made-for-tv quality tripe.  Apparently you can buy the soundtrack seperately. "Expect plenty of copies to be available," as the saying goes.
Theme: wild-west meets sci-fi, supposedly.  It bombed for the excellent Firefly (leading to its cancellation in season one), and Cowboys and Aliens was a dreadful movie.  Yet, for some reason, the theme of cowboys in space gets revived time and again despite being proven many times to be a bad idea.  What's really strange is that the pioneering West was driven by trade, capitalism and greed - whereas Rimword is arguably more Communist than Capitalist.  An odd, bad choice of theme.
Gameplay: Gnomoria-style.
Everything I've listed makes it look like an unexceptional game and first impressions are not good.  But if you turn the music off it suddenly gets a whole lot better.  The top down approach is far better than the isometry of Gnomoria, and the awful graphics do at least allow you to grasp quickly what is happening.
The gameplay has a moreish quality to it, like Gnomoria, but the graphics are easier on the eye and clearly the developers have learned a lot from similar games that have come before.  The GUI is exceptionally streamlined, tricky things like roofing are cleverly handled, and the options for creating a challenge are varied and work well.  Also, there is no tunnelling, with exploration going 'wide' across the planet, not underground.  This makes keeping track of things much easier.
In short, it gets more things right than wrong.  The sound may be unforgiveably bad, but there is the option to turn the music off.    Use that option.  You won't regret it.  You can't do much about the cowboy theme, but the good news is that (other than Cowboy hats) the theme is underused.  If you just think of them as regular colonists and not cowboys'n'cowgirls you'll enjoy the game much more.
I like it.  Overpriced and over-hyped, perhaps, but undeniably a good game.

EVE Online or as I call it: Star Trek on Steroids that just ripped your house a new doorway. This daunting giant of a game has been around the internet for as long as most people can recall and this beast still continues to keep tearing at boundaries.
The basic premise of this game is "You are a space pilot, you are in space, you're pretty rad now." but to say that's where it ends would be insulting as there are too many things to even list in a mere review meant for a brief read for some form of idea.
A more accurate description is that you're a space pilot in a constantly changing galaxy that litterally evolves and changes based on what the community itself are doing within it: Sectors can be claimed or lost for factions, mine deposits can be exausted in certain areas, pirates can come for you when you least expect it, you can be a bounty hunter that hunts down other players or be the bounty yourself, making yourself feared throughout the galaxy!
That alone was enough for me to buy into this and yet, more new features are constantly being added to this (already huge) giant such as building your own Colony within a sector or planet, hacking ships to get treasures and even linked play with Dust 314 to assist players fighting on planets with orbital bombardments.
The downside is that since there is so much to this game to even consider doing or even do, it's very mindblowing to any newcomers to EVE Online, putting them off as a whole. Fortunatly, the tutorial sets you off to some basics to help you get some form of idea what you could be doing. Skipping the tutorial altogether however feels very non optional and will not only leave you very confused as to what you should be doing, but make EVE a very boring game in the long run since you'll have nothing to start off with.
If the tutorial didn't help you, there are several players that will gladly mentor you (which to be honest, actually saved me from running screaming from this game and never looking back, so thank you brilliant mentors!) and help you get onto your way with whatever you want to focus on.
All in all if you're willing to put the time and effort into this game, it begins to get very interesting as well as rewarding, such as using in game currency to rebuy your subs rather than using real money instead. If not owning this game, then at least try it just once.

I played Age of Empires 2 when it first released back in 1999. Along with its predecessor, AOE 2 was one of the titles that laid the ground work for RTS games that can still be seen to this day. Being so old, you'd think that it would be a clunky mess by todays standards. That the absence of features found in latter day titles would make the game feel obsolete.
Amazingly enough, this is not the case.
Age of Empires 2 remains one of the very best RTS titles, deftly balancing city building, economics and army management without sacrificing the depth of either. I'm honestly amazed that most strategy games lack specific controls like formations and unit behavior settings when this one did it way back when.
AOE 2 HD doesn't seem to add much to the original package, unless you count the non-essential DLC's. However, the simple fact is that AOE 2 doesn't -need- much added to it beyond the ability to function on modern systems. As such, this is a must buy for any RTS fans.
Regarding the DLC's; they...aren't bad, but aren't really that big a deal either. I suppose if you are a long time fan, it will hardly ruin anything for you. Though if you're just starting out, you miss nothing by just getting the base game.

Stick Fight is....a game where, you guessed it, stick figures fight. Although it may seem like something right out of a 2011 Pivot animation, Stick Fight is much more than that. Out of the 3.6 hours I currently have in the game, I have to say it's been an absolute blast. PROS:
*Fun game with a diverse set of weapons and maps
*Multiplayer so you can play with your friends
*Hours of replay value
*Devs still continue to pour love into the game with constant updates
*$4.99 for such a great game is an absolute steal.
CONS:
*Lag spikes are bound to happen but they aren't extremly common
*When you aren't playing with a friend, it can sometimes get frusturating when people are dozens of hours ahead of you in skill since there is no matchmaking and lag usually has a part in that too
*Can sometimes get repetitive but only when played for more than an hour and a half in one sitting with the same people.
Final notes: Stick Fight is an amazing game that I would recommend to anyone who is looking for an action packed fun game that is full of laughs. (also pretty cheap lol)

If your tired of all the MMOs that are similar to World of Warcraft this is the game for you. So much to do to suit any game style.

Unlike other Asian MMOs where it is filled with fanbase of big boobs, panty shots, etc. for the male/lesbian taste, and mainly focused on combat. This is a fun MMORPG to try out for at least 3 days (or your money back).
When you first start, you may feel overwhelmed and excited to try out as many skills as you can. It is highly recommended that you try out each skill at least a few times before leveling it from Novic to F (if it requires 0 AP then go ahead) because you will not get those back. Eventually you'll figure out which talent you want to invest in, take your time on that.
One thing I really like is that the clothing/equipment doesn’t always look the same in color and may not have the same stats either, if created by tailoring and/or blacksmithing, same for some weapons. This game really focuses on teamwork and is very welcoming to casual players as well. Another thing I really enjoy the most is how some of the NPC's break the 4th wall at times, or that some of the enemy's you meet will wear funny disguises. Lastely, weapons and equipment are sort of irrelevant in damage and defense. Talents are what really helps you grow whether be combat or non-combat talents. Level, Age, and Race also play as a factor for stat increase. Can also earn money not only by questing or grinding, but by part-time jobs or commerce as well! If you play your cards right, you could earn 10k+ in no time!
There are a few flaws/annoyances though: Can only make one character (Only bright side is that with your first character you can pick all the choices, normal and premium, for customizing, however will have to purchase another character card via cash shop, depending on type price varies, or make an alliance with either Elves or Giants to get a free card of that race). There is no advance warning that you’re using a beginner inventory package till level 30, where you’re able to use the full bank inventory, but the right half will be locked after level 30 and anything stored in there will be stuck unless you get the Inventory Plus Service from the Cash Shop for $8 for 30 days. The inventory on your character may get easily filled if you’re taking on too many talents. When buying a pattern or a blueprint for crafting clothe, weapon, armor, you don’t know what materials will be needed till after you purchase and start to use it. Best to use the wiki for this, it’ll save you up on gold.
Recommend doing 2-3 life skill talents that require frequent inventory space like Tailoring, Medicine, and Cooking. It is nice to have at least one combat talent too like Close Combat (aka Warrior), Lance, Magic, etc. Say no more than two combat talents though if you wish to do any non-combat talents, and vise versa.
On the server I go to, Alexina, the community is friendly and helpful to newbies (however there are exceptions.) I have rarely seen any players that gloat/brag/show off about their W/L record, about how strong they are, or about their equipment and skills. This makes the game fun and comfortable to play in. Overall, who needs skill when you can have fun? That’s what the game is really emphasizing, fun!
The only piece of fanbase you’ll get the best of is at the start after making your first character. Enjoy the bouncy boobs while you can, because that’ll probably be the only time you’ll get to see anything jiggle on a woman!

Mabinogi is one of the most befuddling games I've had the pleasure of playing. It advertises endless possibilities and mountains of content, when in reality the main things you'll be doing will be menial tasks like milking cows, running shadow missions over and over again for a material you accidentally wasted in the forging process, and showing off your oversized pet collection. The basic combat has a rock-paper-scissors-esque counters, but there's many new styles that render the original sword-and-board playstyle almost moot. Dungeons can range from a challenging romp through small puzzles and waves of enemies to boring clear-the-room gameplay with a boss with an insta-kill move you can't reasonably defend yourself from. Without a good party, tedium and frustration insue, but once you find an active guild, you'll pick up the ins and outs in no time at all. Small fry at your level can kill you just as quickly as you can kill them, and bosses require a couple of players (or luck, in the soloist's case) and a deep understanding of your chosen skill tree to best. Armor and weapons do almost nothing in the wrong hands, which is a refreshing take on games of its genre, and the majority of your combat strength comes from not upgrades and gear, but your character's own experience. The rebirth system allows your character to continue growing without a level cap, allowing long-time players to hit harder with an unupgraded stick than a newbie could with the best gear available. While the grind IS rewarding in the long run, it's the longest run you'll ever take. The majority of the player-base is WAY high up in level, so you'd better start with a couple of friends if you want to get anywhere. Overall, it's not a bad game, and has its moments of fun, but it's older than most of the people who play Nexon games and hasn't aged gracefully. If you're looking for an RPG and life simulator, I highly suggest that you follow the flavor of the month, because despite frequent updates Mabinogi falls short in too many categories to hold your attention.

I bought this game over 3 years ago on a promise and a lot of hyperbole about what the developers wanted to achieve. The product is not yet finished and it will be a little while longer before we have a full single player campaign. However, what is there is very good, by no means perfect, but very good none the less, and I have no hesitation in recommending it in its current state.
Whats good:
* Lots of different game modes, with the main game being team based PvP, but also a 4 player Coop story mode vs bots, and various other co-op player vs bots modes.
* The AI on the bots is fun to play against and they offer a genuine challenge, and have on more than one occasion made me jump.
* Very focussed gameplay, there are only 2 weapons and limited ammo in each clip, so every shot counts
* Great community of people playing, there is quite a lot of chatter on the servers with players, and people are generally quite nice, funny, helpful.
* Quick loading times to get into games
* Great respawn idea, basically when you die you have to wait 2 mins before respawn, but if your team captures zones you get to respawn earlier. This makes the game quite tactical and differentiates it over your usual COD, counterstrike type gameplay.
* The game can be tough for beginners, but experienced players can be quite helpful, so stick at it and it will come to you
* The developers are occasionally found playing with/against you, this gives the feeling that they also enjoy playing the game and adds an extra bit of fun when they do.
* Day/night mode on maps; the night mode makes things especially interesting, how often do you use the flashlight to see where you are going vs giving your position away. The positional sound of footsteps also can give you away / help you find people.
* A bunch of other things I can't be arsed to type.
Whats bad:
* Despite selling a lot of copies of the game, and there being quite a lot of servers, only 1 or 2 of the main ones tend to fill up. However, once you are in at the right time of day the games are fun, in fact I have had quite a few 2v2 or 4v4 games that were amazing.
* Lag. This to me is the games biggest issue, and can be quite frustrating at times, however, again with experience you can compensate for it by firing ahead of target. If there is one thing that needs some more TLC its the lag compensation and reducing overall lag when connecting to servers.
* I play a lot of counterstrike and miss not being able to melee people, i would take anything over nothing, even if you had to charge melee up before striking. The prestige of being able to sneak up on someone and stab them in the back and embarass them would make this game twice as good.
* Not much else other than its not finished, but like I said this is still a very good and polished game
Overall if want something a bit different then this game might be for you, also you can test some of the early stuff out on their website before committing:

Like many others have said, this game is so far removed from the tile-based, MM: Battle Network reboot that it originally promised to be back in 2012. I wanted to provide constructive critiscism upon playing the 2015 version of the Early Access launch but there was nothing I could give other than "Go back to the original Kickstarter demo format."
With Kickstarter, there's a 50/50 chance the game you're backing could be like Shovel Knight, which became a surprise megalomanical hit or this, which slowly degenerated it's development over time and caused both the fans and the development team to give up on it.
There's nothing I can really review about this game that hasn't been said. It's less tactical and more real time focused, a button-masher with confusing and sometimes difficult gameplay. The first demo from the kickstarter and subsequent demos were real-time tactical gameplay but were more rewarding to play based on the limited tile spaces, even with my obvious bugs. Not all games become like this, but that's the risk you take. I don't regret my decision in backing this, seeing as that was 5 years ago; I just want another MM: BattleNetwork game, someday.

Tales from the Borderlands is an episodic point-and-click adventure based on Borderlands series. Everything that drives you crazy or make you smile from previous games, or even you’re not Borderlands fan. The adventure spin-off itself contains great elements of scene, humor, violence, and characters.
The game presents strong characters and development even tons of supported characters will play major roles in storyline regardless on your decisions. I do love Fiona and Rhys. They’re funny and conflicted many times, but they have self-interest and purpose on their goals which add different taste on story.
Each dialogue and decision is well-crafted and written which can lead you to an unexpected outcome. Thanks to Telltale games for implementation on great storytelling, twisted plots, and how it fits well in Borderlands’ universe.

The action scenes mostly involve on pressing direction button and short quick-time events. It’s fast and full of chaos. It’s actually pretty fun to watch although some are unnecessary and overused.

However, I feel like the last episode is bit rushed in term of tight sequence. There is not much difference on choosing Vault team. Also, I’m trying to get close to point of interesting and the cutscene just interrupt when player reach certain area. The placement of script sometimes ruins player self-exploration. I also expect Fiona’s cash could play more roles on choices and inventory system could be manually used for purpose.
Tales from The Borderlands becomes one of my great Pandora tour. Not because of its title, but it has mixed feelings of experience and unforgettable taste of what Borderlands should be.

This game is a lot of fun. I play mainly by myself because none of my friends will get it, but I love the challenge. The campaign is pretty tough, but nothing a single person couldn't handle. The game looks great but still has its kinks. I don't know if this is already a feature, but I hope they put in the scaling feature to the co-op missions. By that I mean that the more people that are in the group, the more enemies you encounter. I've played all the solo missions so far and was impressed; I can't wait to see what else they add. I have yet to play multiplayer, but I hear great things. I also did hear that the online only has one game mode right now and that it gets repetitve.
The weapons are well done as well. You get two SMGs, the first it seams is meant for closer range, meaning the sight doesnt zoom in as much and it doesnt do as much damage. The second is more as a longer range SMG, meaning the sight zooms in much more than the first and does a larger chunck of damage, making it almost like a sniper rifle, but still a SMG. The only other things that I would like to see would be a silencer added to the weapons. There is a toggle for a light and a laser and they are great but I would like to see a silencer and maybe a pistol as well. There are some times when you should be stealthy and the to SMGs that you have are pretty loud and attract attention. There are also some time that the enemies get a little close and zooming in on the first smg just puts you too close.
There are also some cool features like taking off your helment which gets rid of your hud, which makes it a lot harder to play not knowing when and enemie is down or how many bullets you have left. One of the other featuers I really like is that when you are damaged your hud goes down and you hearing is impared, making it harder for you to make the kill. There is also a suicide button, I'm not 100% sure why you would need this, but I found out about it the hard way trying out the buttons and had to restart the whole level. That's the other thing, if you die during the campaign you have to restart the entire thing, granted it's not that long as of now, but its a little fustrating. But the game is overall really nice, would 100% recommend it to someone. Great job guys and keep up the awesome work. (as of update 14)

Loved it.
Main criticisms would be production-wise mainly, it's just unpolished. Clipping, collision detection, floaty platforming, what little of the combat there is lacks much feedback. But I feel the lack of polish is excused considering like 30 people in total worked on the game (including composer, producers) and with the variety of visuals on offer here. On the level of Zeno Clash 2. Much like that game, also South American developers (Swordtales is Brazilian, ACE Team is Chilean) so props to seeing more games from that continent.
If those don't bother you so much, check it out for a really interesting coming-of-age dark fantasy experience. It's short but complete, around 3 hours. Perfect for one sitting. There is oodles of poeticism and surrealism involving ashen children, blood, seasons, and celestial bodies. Basically, men's ambition and arrogance has failed them, so a girl is the only one who can save it all while being guided by a mage, but her childhood will have to be sacrificed. Seasons and her age changes, as she makes a tree tower to the top. Celestial bodies get involved. Reminded me fondly of Tale of Princess Kaguya. There's only about 3 characters involved: a girl, a soldier, and a dragon. It's a pretty grim and lonely affair
, overall.
The music by Vinicius Kleinsorgen is memorably excellent.
If you're up for something more sombre from an action-adventure game in the vein of Team Ico with the dark surrealism of something like Alice Madness Returns, 70s psychedelia, and a cool female protagonist in a memorable tale, give it a shot. Worth it just for the visuals.

Out of all the Dragon Ball games I have played, Xenoverse is probably my favorite.  Story wise it takes place in the future of the series, having you travel around time correcting errors in the time stream. The game features character creation, its pretty detailed compared to what I was expecting, and features 5 separate races.  There is a good deal of gear and tons of ability's to put on your character as well. Most of the gear and abilities are acquired via side quests, but there are shops to purchase, items, gear and skills at as well.  You can party up, or solo most quests.
Xenoverse is a game I really love, but it is not without its flaws.One big downside to the game is cheating, cheating is real and its a problem (super stats anyone)? This coupled with unbalanced skills and gear (it feels like every patch something new breaks in some op way) makes PvP public games pretty un-fun.  To top it off It seems to me that PvP is dead most of the time anyway, so this is probably not a game you will want to get if your a "hard core" fighting game fan, or want a DBZ game for the PvP aspects.
When the game released it had terrible server issues, and im glad now that those kinks have been worked out they can work on balancing and patching the other known bugs players often compalin about.  I just hope, some time in the future they give the game anticheat, because as it stands I find this to be a pretty unacceptable level of cheaters in the game.
Overall though the game has a story similar to the game Dragon Ball Online, and the fighting feels pretty unique and unlike most fighting games out there, as you wont find any combos you need to remember, or anything like that. Its a simpler take of a fighting game, coupled with full 3d movement and Rpg elements just makes this a blast to play, especially if you have friends who can play to!

Most of what you are reading is basically "MANA UPDATE AND ITEM WIPE RUINED IT". Now this consistency might sound circlejerky and immature at first examination. But it is completely true, and it is why a game I used to play for multiple hours at a time, I can now only muster 15-20 minutes of before I drop it for at least a month. It hurts that a game that I was once addicted too, that I've bought all the DLC for, now is completely unsatisfying. Please don't let the "Very Positive" label fool you, those positive reviews are outdated.
Early game:
Basically a top down fast hack slash with RPG elements that took a lot of design choices from The Binding of Isaac (I highly recommend TBOI, go play any version of that instead, it is what you are looking for if you like a game like this.) You would fight five waves and a boss in areas, and after five areas you would move on to an act boss and finally the next act. Dungeons and shops have the chance to spawn after each wave in each area. (This hasn't changed)
Each character has a skill tree and stats to apply. Among the character tree are both passive and active skills with level requirements. Active skills could always be activated whenever off cooldown, encouraging expirimentation with how they combo together and how best to use them in sequence. The skills are binded a bit akwardly, but can be gotten used to, taking up 1234 slots and not slots closer to the WASD buttons like Q, E, R, and F, or something similar.
Honestly the game took some grinding, as even though skill and stat points applied are permanent, they serve more to augment which of your characters stats or skills does end up more prominent than others. Relics found in dungeons, bought in shops, or picked up at the end of areas heavily help your character, giving certain passive or active skills, or even just certain stat boosts. The actual combat was pretty fun in a lot of ways, so the difficulty due to health/armor constraints disappeared the longer you play or the farther you get. An inventory with items [still constricted to your current run I think?] was introduced. It didn't have too much depth, but it was just starting and there were some items that made getting skills above your level requirement possible, so it was pretty nice. It doesn't pause the game for it though, so you have to be fast. It is made easy by the side by side comparison of the currrent and new item, and the simplicity of the choice of either replacing or dropping.
Definitely wasn't perfect, and didn't have the greatest balance, but it still managed to be fun, at least for me, so w/e. :) Multiplayer was in development, quite buggy, but it was exciting to think that online co-op was coming.
Changes:
I had dropped the game for a bit due to other games grabbing my attention (Dota 2, TF2, Half-Life series, etc.), nothing I mentioned before really forced me away. But the combination of all this new stuff is ....eh.
Okay, I'm definitely being repetitive with how it isn't as enjoyable, but it is a main part of why I liked this so much. The balancing is awkward, the controls are a bit weird, and the grinding has always been a bit of tedium. But there was also the satisfying times of sequencing or spamming spells, and finding more and more relics to majorly augment my run kept me hooked despite it not being a "great game". This was a guilty pleasure of mine. But I now I feel with these changes I've been pushed back into the grinding, and it will be even harder for me to find enjoyment in it to the same extent due to the limitations of the new game. I mean, I haven't even had personal experience with the apparently horrible staff. (All I know is that from the time I followed the creator's twitter he was often quite bratty) Play something else. Save yourself the time.

Mabinogi my favorite MMORPG of all time, Mabinogi is a game with plenty of places to explore, tons of free content.
Mabingoi’s plot is actually a bunch of optional stories you can be in. It can range from saving a goddess to helping Shakespeare complete his plays.
Mabinogi has 3 races you can play as, Human, Elf and Giant. I recommend Human as your starter race unless you’re okay with only having on free character card. The Human allows one to unlock the other the classes for free, each race also has its advantages and disadvantages. Elf for example of the least amount of "str" or Strength in the game but have the largest amount of Mana. Giants on the other hand are more powerful in "str" but have less of Mana amount. Humans are in the middle when it comes to this.
But enough about the races the thing that makes Mabingoi different among MMORPG is the amount of skills you can learn and the things you can do with them.
In Mabingoi the skill list goes as follows;
Combat
Magic
Life
Alchemy
Fighter
Music
Puppetry
There are other skills in these skills such as life has making clothes in it along with Transformation Mastery which allows one to become an animal, such as a baby chick or a snake. Another example would be the music skill which is one of my favorites due to its ability to play any song you want. If you want to play the Portal theme song you can or even your own song. The Music skill works is putting in symbols and rest into a scroll with three sections.
Melody
Harmony 1
Harmony 2
Now let’s say you have no knowledge of composition not to worry there are plenty of pre-written scripts around the internet and most users don't mind making a copy of a song for you.
The game also has a skill rank system that goes as follows.
Novice
F
E
D
C
B
A
9
8
7
6
5
4
3
2
1
These levels are boosted by using a skill and raising it with AP. AP can be gained by leveling up or during a game event if AP is one of the prizes.
Another important feature of Mabinogi is Rebirth. A player ages one year a week in real time. You can start at age 10 to 17. When you start at age 17 you can go up to age 20 and rebirth for free each time you become age 20 resetting your level and not you skill ranks. If you rebirth and you had rank A music playing for example it would still be rank A in your next life. Rebirths allow you to gain AP faster so it’s very useful.
The last part of the review I have to bring up is the amount of free content. I've played this game since 2009 and I have to say everything in the shop is optional. It may speed things up a little but almost everything you can buy in the shop can also be sold for in game money by other users. The biggest item that is in the shop but cannot be sold by users is pets. But don't worry two pets are free to each player. a horse and a eagle. In Mabinogi some pets can actually fly places. The eagle is one of them.
That’s pretty much all I have to say about Mabingoi. If you feel overwhelmed its okay Mabinogi is a complex game but once you get the hang of it, it can be a real fun game. I recommend trying it.

Early backer here. Backed on Kickstarter based on the pitch in the middle of 2013. Played the alphas, liked where it was going. Seriously, look at the difference:
Tons of radio silence throughout this, of course. There was limited mention about why things were taking so long, what was going on with the team, etc. Eventually I just forgot about it.
Then, suddenly, they went to Early Access. Man, was I excited - I thought the alpha must have progressed enough to warrant releasing it on Steam! But... alas... it wasn't the same game pitched at all. It didn't feel the same, the battlefields weren't structured the same way, my dreams of playing this on a touch interface were basically shattered.
What happened? Everyone, including the dev, said to give it time. Fair enough. So, after August 20th, 2015, I waited. I figured, well, if things need to be overhauled, that'll take a few months, right? Three? Why stop there? Let's wait 5, just to give it extra time.
Man, what a let down. I know it's early access still, but this game's two years past the original deadline. It feels like a flash game, it runs like a flash game.
Activating the "grid" to see movement literally puts hex outlines in a checkerboard pattern on a square grid, and the player can only move in the four cardinal directions. The controls for keyboard are rather poor. The best part of the game, the animations, are choppy and have a limited amount of frames each (it's like they were animated on fours rather than twos or ones) and the sprites themselves are low detail. It's hard to get into the game when it's so clunky, but the majority of it seems to be moving from battle to battle with little to do inbetween. The combat itself is tedious to the point that I'd rather just go do chores.
I can't recommend this game. I'll probably let it sit in my library until it's out of early access (if that happens), but it's on my "remove from account without refund because it's that bad" list.

This is one of those games where, if you practice enough to get good, you can make a lot of progress. Then, you inevitably lose to something foolish. finally, when you start back at the beginning, the enemies at this point are so different in regards to how accurate they are and how fast they can attack. it's almost impossible to go from the silver tier back down to bronze and make any progress after. So basically, unless you are already in a good mood or have infinite patience, this game will be fun-right up until you make the smallest error. Then you lose a limb, which takes away any upgrades that you've already purchased that utilize that limb. If you survive that round, then to get your limbs and upgrades back you must forfeit your next upgrade to purchase a clone.
These are just issues I've noticed playing. It seems to me that too much emphasis is placed on the importance of purchasing clones, rather than upgrades that you can then learn to use to survive longer. My recommendation to the programming team; maybe repair the player's robot between matches? or maybe just replace 1 missing limb?
I very much like how balanced the gameplay is and that the game runs very smoothly, and would definitely recommend it to anyone who likes arena-style gameplay; just make sure that you're in a good mood, because every mistake is punished severely...

Disclaimer: I'm a kickstarter backer so the low play time count on Steam does not reflect  actual game time since I have been playing the alpha builds released prior to Steam.
TLDR Game Description: Are you aware of the megaman exe series before? If you are, this plays a lot like it, if you aren't the units here move in real time along a grid, and you move on the grid to dodge enemy attacks and launch your own attacks. The game mechanics are extremely addicting as it is reflex and tactically based, there are lots of times you can die but you will want to retry it.
Yeah so, just a background C-Wars was actually a game pitched in kickstarter more than 2 years ago, the dev team underwent severe issues both personally and financially and as a result the game spent time in development hell and entered early access by the skin of its teeth...this is the reason why the game has a lot of negative reviews when it was first launched it was really closer to a tech demo than an actual game.
FORTUNATELY, the dev team went into super saiyan mode and started releasing daily updates since then, right now I can say it can be positively compared to other EA games in terms of actual content, and consequently is now worth the EA price. For the price of a cup of coffee you get beautiful pixel art, ok music and fun and frenetic gameplay. I suggest you buy it now because the price will likely increase.
I mean at the end of the day the game is receiving daily updates, patches, bug fixes and various quality of life improvements so it will definitely be worth your purchase. Buy it now and encourage them to improve the game even more. Plus, it is highly original this is the first megaman exe style game I've seen anywhere apart from the original megaman exe games themselves.

(Be aware this game is early alpha, and thus I'm reviewing my impressions on the game as of November 8, 2014.)
Interstellar Marines is a Co-Op Tactical FPS. It pits you and 3 other teammates who are, you guess it, interstellar marines, against defective robots in a battle to survive to the end by means of elimination, escaping, or simply surviving. Or, you can also go against other players in a control point-style battle.
This game actually has a good amount of realism and atmosphere which blend very well for a game like this. The game has a real dark atmosphere to it, feels genuinely creepy and lonely with only your friends by your side. The maps, for the most part, are like an abandoned and broken facility. Very dark, and your main light source would be flickering lights or your own flashlight. It really brings immersion into the game, which is very helpful. The animations of the marines too are very well done, especially in first person. You actually see your arms move as you look around, see your own feet, and so on. Small detail, but very welcome.
Speaking of realism, that's one of the best parts of the game. Whenever you take damage, your hearing is impaired (which is important in this game), your HUD disappears until you heal, and team damage/killing is also real. The guns aren't all that powerful either, but that's a good thing. The robots you face are very powerful, and can down you in seconds. You only have two guns: One for short range, and one for long range. Neither have that much ammo in it's clip (Probably enough for 3-4 robots if you're accurate), or have amazing accuracy, so you need to be precise and careful; Spraying and gunning your way through just won't succeed.
Teamwork is heavily emphasized here. It's only four of you, and because the robots are so powerful, you're likely to go down. The only way you can survive is if your teammates revive you in your 15 seconds of last breaths. The aforementioned guns are weak with only one person, so if hoards of robots come, you all need to use your ammo and shoot tactically.
There's currently 5 game modes as of this review, and they all have nice variety to the game. Elimination is killing all the robots in the area, Escape is moving to the top of the facility while surviving from the bots, Survivial is activiating several objectives and then escaping (with robots.), and Stronghold is the PvP game mode, 2 teams trying to capture all points in the area. The other mode is a campaign mission, titled The Neurogen Incident. It appears to be story oriented, but I cannot currently play it as it crashes my game.
All in all, Marines is an incredible team based tactical shooter, especially for being early access! And I would really recommend this to anybody who wants some good times with their friends, using teamwork to achieve the goal in a dark and desolate enviornment.

The game itself is a story, and perhaps you have to really concentrate to get the context, but as you play as Toren you see her grow from an infant to adult as she scales a tree, growing inside a tall tower. Unfortunately for me, there isn’t a lot to say in terms of replay value. On our completion of the game we saw that we didn’t complete a section of a puzzle, so technically we didn’t 100% complete it. the only other thing I'm a bit dissapointed at is that you cant play Co-Op on the story mode. which seems a bit silly really considering you can play all the parallel quests together which are pretty much the entirety of the story mode anyway just with certain things changed to it. there seems to be no reason i can see why they could'nty of just added in an online co-op mode for the story.

All in all its a good game and has a lot of replay value , The combat is fun and the Super/Ultime skills really do make you feel empowered when you land them just right.
Unique twist on the story too which i really think works well and is delivered great , but again I think they really missed a trick here with Multiplayer Story.

If you enjoy getting attatched to your characters and leading them on an adventure this game might be for you. I had already long since beaten this game by the time this playthrough came about but I had a relativley good colony going, we had this golden retriever auto named 'Hope'. Cheesey as hell, I know. But she had gotten into a fight with a wolf a few weeks back in-game, lost all of her legs and even her tail. But I couldn't let her die, so we kept her in her bed and brought her food, despite her contributing nothing. Even when food got low, we kept her there and struggled.
The attacks had been rough as of late and had no hope of slowing down. I decided it was best to move our base, we had few fighters and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ weaponry. We got the majority of the base made but I was suffering some pretty heavy mental debuffs. A man-hunter pack came. It was about fifteen turtles. This doesn't sound too bad until you consider I had one fighter at this point with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hunting rifle and only two turrets at the entrance (which they had swarmed already) that were nearly broken. I had enough food to stay inside and wait them out but a storm came and lightning struck my old base which still had a few resources in it and my food supply. Hope also hadn't been moved over yet due to the constant mental breaks. Fire started to spread.
I got the quickest runner and the best shot and lined them up at the narrow corridor. I couldn't let Hope die, because I feared my whole colony would fall with her if I did. (so much cheese yo) I turned on the turrets and opened the doors, Hope's owner sprinting narrowly past the turtles of death, the room filling with blood as he sprinted off to the burning ruin of the base. Heat started to build up in the wooden structure, sending the immobile Hope into a heat stroke. Grayson busted through one of the walls and heaved her out while the battle of the bunker raged on, explosions sounding in the distance. He sat outside of the ruined base, scavenging food to feed her before she starved to death. The turtles had been defeated at that point, my turrets were done for and my fighter was in the thrown together hospital. He brought Hope back to the settlement and we slowly started to recover.
Then another ♥♥♥♥ing raid came. There had to be atleast seven men, all relativley well armed. My colony was beaten down and broken at this point, but we made strong walls and kept a 24/7 hour watch repairing them, but people were slowly going mad and we could only scavenge so much meat from the turtle corpses. It looked like it was all going to go downhill...
A wanderer had entered the area. She was butt-naked and was a hell of a shot. I had her pick over the old battlefields scattered around the map from seasons of war with neighboring settlements. She found a sniper rifle in mint condition and lined herself up with the raiders who started to make their way through the wall now that most of my colony was wandering around in a daze or attacking one another. The first shot was a headshot that pulled the rest of the men away from the walls and into a firefight with her. She picked them off one by one, kiting in and out of their range while dodging every one of their shots. The naked sniper prooved too much for them as they started to desperately flee. Only one survived.
Weeks later a plague ran through the colony and slowly started to kill everyone off. Both my doctors had it bad and had to be in bed for a majority of their time. Hope died early, everyone else followed until my bunker was turned into a tomb for the dying settlers.
I reccomend playing this game on the 'hardcore' mode, no reloading saves. While it can be very cheap and annoying at times, actually surviving when there are no redos in one of the most gratifying things. When you just reload the save it cheapens the whole experience. I did that on my first playthrough and won the game, and it wasn't nearly as fun as all the many times that I had failed.
TLDR: A very entertaining sandbox game that can tell a number of stories from epic adventures to tragic endings. Play on the 'hardcore' mode and don't savescum, it spoils the experience.

Before reading this, I'd like to point out that I am very much aware of the negative response the game has gotten since its October patch (The reviews that have been deemed 'Most Helpful' are negative all the way up to the 26th review), and I understand the backlash, anddd... I don't at the same time. I don't know what the game was before its October patch, and I don't know what existed in that patch that caused such a huge backlash. Because of this, this review is for the present-day game only. It won't be biased on previous versions.
So I will start with a very major thing for future consumers. If you are considering buying this game to play with friends, I highly discourage it. This game is intended for multiplayer purposes, and Panic Art Studios has urged that with its 4 Pack.  Despite this, the game's multiplayer is abysmal. The gameplay is absolutely fine. The problem is that the Multiplayer functions are very unorganized and don't work most of the time.
There are a few ways to join other players in Multiplayer, all of which do not work without port-forwarding. If you do not want to port-forward to play with your friends, then skip ahead to the Singleplayer section of the review.
Firstly, the option to join your friends via Steam is disabled, so it isn't even an option to begin with. Secondly, you can join someone else's server in the server list, but most of the time, no servers will come up even if they exist. Plus, there is no way to refresh the Server List. Third, you can join via someone else's IP. DO NOT DO THIS. Without port-forwarding, once you enter someone's IP in this section, it will post that IP into the PUBLIC CHAT. So unless you have port-forwarded, or you are joining someone else's game that you trust, I suggest you do not do this.
Now, if this review was to address the multiplayer side of the game, this would certainly be a negative review. However, behind all of the multiplayer issues is a genuinely entertaining gameplay experience. If you want to buy the game to play with your friends, don't buy it. But if you're looking for a game that you wouldn't mind playing by yourself, then at least bring this into consideration.
I could go as far as to say that the gameplay was phenominal. Sure, I did encounter the occasional bug here and there, but it was thrilling, it was challenging, and it was fun. Most video games in the past few years have tended to play it safe and make their games easier, so "more people can enjoy it." In theory this is fine, but it does end up excluding those gamers that want a challenge. The game does not wait around to challenge you. Once you start, you are thrown into combat and you are on your feet just like that. This may seem frustrating at first, especially since an explanation of controls is never given, but after a maximum of 15 minutes, you can pick up on the controls rather easily. I suppose by not having that explanation, it allows gamers to figure out the situation by themselves, and the resulting levels you defeat are all the more rewarding.
I don't know what was added in the October patch that could've caused such a ruckus, but I think it was something Mana-related, and if that's the case, then I wouldn't necessarily see the problem with it. From what I played, mana isn't a necessity to play the game. It certainly helps out, but you're not going to die over and over if you choose not to use it. It might become more of use in the long run, but you definitely would get tons of entertainment value out of the game beforehand.
I have heard, however, that after some time, the game does start handing out items that aren't balanced, and can make the game really easy, but by the time this happens, you'll already have tons of hours given into the game, if you are to get that far, and I think those hours would in fact be worth your time.
All in all, the game isn't without its flaws, but I feel the other reviews have been too picky with them that they've forgotten the core game itself. It's not a great game, but it's not a bad game either. A price of $6.49 is debatable, but the game has gone on sale as far as 90% off, so if you want to try out the game, wait for it to go on sale.
In summary, if you're looking for a game to play with friends, do not buy this game. If you're looking for a single-player game where you can kill a few hours, then I would definitely recommend it. And even though the key multiplayer issues have yet to be acted upon after... 2 years apparently, I'd ask of gamers to simply keep being patient, as it's not the end of the world if they don't. And besides, the game isn't abandoned. They're still adding new content to this date, so the possibility of the game consisting of a great multiplayer experience to coincide with the single player campaign is very much there.

Mabinogi is one of my all-time favorite MMORPGs. If you spent countless hours playing RuneScape or Harvest Moon back in the day, you'll probably like this too.
Grinding by endlessly fighting monsters isn't necessary in this game, though the dungeons and fields offer the opportunity. Instead, much of your experience will come from quests and skill building. Part-time jobs offered by the shopkeepers of Erinn are a helpful way to gain exp, gold, and crafting supplies. Each character in this world is unique, so doing quests is a good way to build friendships.

There is a huge selection of skills, and you are free to build as many as you like. This includes, but is not limited to, fishing, cooking, tailoring, carpentry, metalworking, transformation, alchemy, music playing, swordfighting, archery, and magic. Practicing your trade(s) contributes to your skill level and your overall level. This allows you to use new techniques and recipes.
Your character ages at the rate of 1 year for every 1 real-life week. If your level and age get too high for your taste, you can be reborn as your younger self (or a completely new person with a purchasable character card). You keep your skills and items, but resetting your level allows you to try new quests and gain AP faster to promote skill growth. Your character grows and changes weight as you get older and vary your diet and activity, making rebirth all the more refreshing.
Overall, Mabinogi is a great MMO because it offers enough variety to last for countless hours of playtime. Even if the cutesy anime style graphics aren't to your taste, Mabinogi is worth a try if you long for a quality crafting/exploration MMO.
