As someone who is put off by anything related to anime due to it being something i've never really got into nor liked, I am rather happy to say I enjoyed this game even if you have limited knowledge of the franchise itself.
The story is basic yet engaging, to sum it up quickly, you'll play as a custom character of your choice (Human, Namekian, Majin, Saiyan or frieza's race) and have to help trunks, a saiyan from the franchise, by going back into past events of the dragon ball universe and fixing them. An example of this would be (Spoiler Spoiler Spoiler) Raditz at the start of the saiyan saga, instead of the usually weak raditz people know he's taken on a much stronger form and nobody knows why, you have to go and help goku and piccolo fight the now stronger raditz and make sure it ends in the way it did originally, with goku and raditz getting hit by piccolo's beam.
After story missions are completed, you slowly unlock side-missions relating to the story missions you did, an example of this would be to kill saibermen who were working with raditz, these give you experiance, mission rewards and a ranking from D-S (As far as I can tell)
Your character is fully customisable, with most of the moves used in dragon ball available, such as the famous Kamehameha and the galick gun and some more lesser used ones. When you gain enough experiance, you will level up and be able add points into your Ki amount, Health, Stamina amount, basic attack, super attack or super blast, which in turn makes the stat of it higher and boosts it. So it's very possible to make a character that uses a full close combat loadout and still have it as a viable tactic. On top of this, you can buy, find, or earn custom clothing in order to bost stats, such as Lord Slugs garb, or Turles's battlesuit, a wide range of clothing is available to suit your characters cosmetic and stat needs.
The combat itsef is very satisfying especially when you use your own custom character, it's very easy to pull off a combo even with limited understanding of the mechanics, whether it be shooting a kamehameha x10 or beating someone to a pulp in close range, it feels very responsive and fluid compared so some of the previous games (I'm talking about you, Battle of Z) The keyboard controlls are just as viable as using a gamepad, so people without one need not worry.
If I were to pick some negative aspects that push the game down for me, it would be the servers (Now mostly fixed) which disconnect you randomly, meaning you have to wait to log back in. And a lack of some of the movie characters and lack of character clothing, but it's still made up by what is available. Another problem i've found is that some special attacks are down right over or underpowered, the father and son kamehamea does the tiniest bit more damage than a normal one, while taking three Ki bars, while the blue swirl used by burter can deal nearly 3/4 damage of someones HP if they get in the whirlewind at the start, and this has a large AOE, so potentially you could destroy the whole team with one move.
Overall i'd give it a solid 7.5 out of 10, if it were to be pushed up to an 8 or a 9, the moves would have to be balanced out a bit more, and the servers would have to be working better, I would reccomend this to fans of the show who want a good game, but to those not into the game, it might be better to wait for some of the problems to be fixed, though I'd imagine they'd still have a lot of fun playing this.

The most fun DBZ game I've ever played, and one that finally made it to PC without me having to get PS2 iso's of the old Budokai games and play them on an emulator.
PROS:
-Create your own character and have them interact with actual set pieces of the DBZ universe (FINALLY).
-The fighting is good, pretty simple to pull off some sweet combo's on enemies with little effort, but takes a while to master and can be problematic at times.
-Super Saiyan/Vegeta/Kaioken tranformations! And any clothing options and skills you find can be equipped by your own character. Want to be a Namekian and fire off Kamehameha blasts? You can here!
-RPG elements (leveling up makes you feel like you're actually increasing your power level throughout the game, because YOU ARE. You can tell by being able to play one of the earlier PQ's as a level 70+ and just own them in a few moves).
-A ton of content to get lost into for hours after completing the main game (but also during) known as Parallel Quests.
-Loot drops (also a CON, see below).
-Graphics match the show pretty much spot on, and the sound effects do as well (though strangely enough, some things do not have any audible playback in some stages/attacks).
-You can have series favorites train you and teach you their moves, and they even commentate on the score screen after a PQ, telling you how happy/meh/disappointed they are with your performance!
CONS:
-Loot drops are ENTIRELY RANDOM and not really based off of your final score/rating at the end of a PQ (you could get a Z rating but get absolutely no loot afterwards). This requires you to farm PQ's to get items which can take forever, espeically if you're playing a very difficult/long PQ, only to have it drop nothing good, requiring you to play it over and over again until you get the item you want, which is extremely frustrating (at least to me).
-Difficulty can range from simple to punishing in some PQ's (mostly depending on your level, but this can be a con if you're trying to farm a PQ and get good loot).
-No option to preview outfits, accessories, etc on your character before buying them (which means you could drop 100,000 zeni on an item that sounds cool, but then you equip it on your character and realize you don't like it. Sorry, you're out 100,000 zeni).
-Servers are currently unreliable. They are getting better, but why am I getting disconnected during a single player lobby??
-Dragonballs. Why am I fighting Time Patrollers to get these? And farming them is pretty simple, though some characters will stop dropping the dragon balls, granted they even show up in the PQ (I can't get the Five Star ball for some reason, no matter which PQ I play with the randomly spawning Time Patroller. It's gotta be an issue on my end, but I've spent a while trying to get it and for some reason it will not drop no matter what I do).
Overall, I would recommend this game for DBZ fans, and still recommend it to newcomers of the series. It's a blast to play, especailly with friends online (it makes farming PQ's much more fun and easy).
8/10, would farm quests for Trunks outfit/Super Saiyan/10X Big Bang Kamehameha/Dragonballs again.

Looking at the steam reviews I am honestly shocked at the poor reception this game has recieved.  Much of the dissapointment has to do with the admittedly bad launch which came with a bug preventing anyone from playing, instead players were stuck in the "searching for players" screen and thus thought "this game is dead." And well, due to that its player base is now really suffering.  However, this game is fantastic! The only Issue i have had so far is with the small playerbase, but I have always been able to find a good game to join in spite of this.  And now on to the real review.
If you don't know what to think of Deformers at first glance you aren't alone, so try and imagine this: Deformers plays as though Super Smash Brothers and Quake multiplayer had a baby.  The game is constantly fast paced and provides you with a variety of options to go about your objectives with.  If you want to take a mroe direct approach to combat you might play the Striker class and headbutt your foes to oblivion, or you might want to spend your time giving your opponents the good ol'♥♥♥♥♥♥block with the Guardian and kill them with your cube counter.  Much like in the 2016 Doom, you can only regain any substancial amount of hp by killing opponents and therefore encouraging you to carefully engage your opponents if you are looking to come back from a deficit.
As for content, there are three modes of play, which is a little lacking, but for me the hidden depth of the gameplay more than make up for that.
In my book this game makes an easy 9/10 because if I give it a 10/10 people will call me a liar.  I highly reccommend this game to any casual or hardcore player!
If you have any further questions about the game feel free to hit me up with a message.  I would love to see this game grow and (de)form into something great!

Although it is "possible" to play this game for free, most players cannot afford to play for free with in-game currency.  If you think you are going to be one of the few playing for free, get ready when you discover how much time/effort is required to do that.  Get a real job if you are going to play this game and give up that fantasy of playing for free.
The good: Immersive, large galaxy, always something new to try out.
The BAD:
- new players are heavily targetted by veterans who want easy gains.  New players frequently lose everything they have and go broke due to ganks by 5+ year veterans of the game.  The developers not only allow this, but encourage it.
- 3rd person flight controls only
- The "player controlled economy" is a half lie: the devs can and do intervene in the economy of the game. Although player production does effect the economy, CCP has "adjusted" in game prices often.  Plex prices and supply, for example, have been manipulated by devs in the past and are subject to manipulation at any time.  The half truth is CCP usually allows player supply to drive the economy more than any direct price/supply manipulation by the devs.
-1 player per ship, no matter how big that ship is in game.  Absolutely no chance at multi-player crewed ships or boarding due to the limits of the game design.
- There are only 2 modes: 3rd person space flight or you are in your room in a station spinning your ships.  If you want more, wait for Star Citizen like the rest of us. ;)
- If you don't Pay 2 Win, it will take you a very, very, VERY long time to not be gank bait for veteran players in this game.
Play at your own risk.
If you like space combat and exploration, pass on purchasing EvE Online and check out Star Citizen instead.
P.S.  Oh yeah, I forgot to mention: scamming and griefing are allowed and heavily encouraged in this game. Don't cry when it happens... repeatedly.  I tried to warn you. ;)

EDIT: Changed to thumbs down because of a convinient bug of not rewarding any scrap in big black scorpions anymore.
TLDR: It's a fun little game I recommend trying for a while. After a while the grind skyrockets into comedy levels. So hold on to your wallet, this ain't worth it. I'll probably ditch it too soon enough.
To be honest, if you put some thought into designing your own vehicle, you will get good results. So don't be a t,wat, slap armor on the places you get hit the most, use non explosive components as armor as well as junk. Put your explosive parts under the cabin (if you loose the cabin first, you're dead anyway), so they aren't likely to get shot up. If you're getting flipped over on the sides often, widen the chasis, don't overdo it with the wheels (4 to 8 max) and so on. It's not simple, but it's no rocket science either.
Even with the grind, you can easily grind tons of scrap in big black scorpions brawl (like, 10 scrap per kill even if you loose and you get between 10-20 scrap per entire match in normal play), that is until they nerf it into oblivion. The problem is that in any other mode you are essentially rubbing your genitals on a cheese grate to get anything of value.
Atm Im pushing into 5.5K+ and the only two things that really bother me are the autoaim MGs and pretty much all of the drones as they have been recently buffed with double damage, these things take zero effort to use while outputting insane DPS.
Everything else is manageable.
Regarding seal clubbing, you're gonna get that in any game that does not have hard limits on overtiering. It was present in both Robocraft and Junk League (Stopped playing both a while ago so I have no idea about the state atm).
Regarding P2W aspect, yeah it's present. But beyond that I don't have much to say, after playing so many F2P games that are blatantly P2W this hardly surprises me. Not to mention Gaijin is known to run games into the ground with decisions focused on short term monetary gains at the expense of consumer trust and the game itself. But then again, that story is far too common with F2P games.
Overall, vehicle building is nice and the limited available parts, engine power, number of wheels, energy levels, weight do present a challenge when designing a vehicle.
It runs really well, 144fps (1080p) on a now 4 year old rig, though its a good idea to turn down some GPU intensive options.
Balance, well that is going to be the most popular topic in any PvP game and this is no exception. Seal clubbing seens particularly bad here as people not only try to bring purple weapons into lower tiers, but they bring drones and autoaim MGs of all things, essentially being the ultimate scu,mbags.
The grind is extraordinary once you begin looking into purple items (white > blue > purple > yellow > orange). I can imagine that grinding for a legendary is a titanic undertaking on its own.
Over all, I recommend this for people to try out. But I do not think it is worth spending any money as the grind will only get worse past the blue level and thats not even the middle of the road. The fact that Gaijin runs the show doesn't exactly radiate trust.

KI is a really solid 2D fighter that Iron Galaxy did a terrific job with, creating an incredibly unique combo system that is very simple to pick up yet has enough depth to satisfy people familiar with the genre.
+6 button control scheme identical to Street Fighter/Skullgirls (3x punch/3x kick)
+Basic combo flowchart of hitconfirm -> opener -> auto double -> linker -> auto double -> ender which can change on a character by character basis but remains rather constant throughout the cast.
+The combo breaker is easily the biggest hit or miss feature about the game solely because this game will nearly always at some point give the player being hit to break out of the combo if they correctly guess the strength of the move the other player is using (i.e if I use Jago M auto doubles, if you press MP+MK within a small window you'll be let out of my combo). However, this system is offset by a state called "lockout" where if you've already guessed wrong on a combo break, the other player has their freedom with you like a traditional combo for a little bit. It's a great risk/reward system imo.
+Character variety is all over the place. Very solid roster at this point with most playstyles being catered to.
+In depth tutorial covers everything from basic mechanics to real match situations.
+Netcode is arguably the best out of any modern fighter.
+Exhibition has crossplay capability with Windows 10 and Xbox One versions.
+A super rare fighting game with actual single player content! Wild, right?
-Ranked has no crossplay (WHY???) and is relatively dead once you hit Gold or Killer.
-Playing with a specific user on Xbox One or Win10 is a total ♥♥♥♥♥how and I've never gotten it to work successfully.
9/10, it's a good game

Clone Drone in the Danger Zone is an arena fighter game where you're pitted against AI in an arena filled with enemies and traps. While at first it seems simple, the combination of the different enemies soon turns it into a battle of quick reactions and tactical use of your available weapons. The story mode provides a good tutorial into the game by being moderately difficult, abeit rather short with only 2 chapters (more to come). The main chunk of the gameplay comes from challenge mode and endless mode, with twitch mode being obviously something that only twitch streamers would sink time into, though it is definitely a fun mode as well.
Endless mode is basically just the player versus wave after wave of robots, following the same structure as the story mode. After each wave you return to your lobby and use a skill point to upgrade your robot. The maps come in groups of bronze, silver, gold, diamond and titanium with each map either being one shared between them all with an increase in enemy tier or a map unique to that difficulty. The enemies slowly progress as the game goes on to increase the variety and while it is more common to see the tier 3 and 4 enemies towards titanium, lower tiers can still appear as well to sneak in a cheeky killing blow while your guard is down. One of the best parts of this mode is the combination of the enemies which forms a formidable force to fight against. For example, a single Mark 3 Sword Robot might be easy to handle on it's own, but add any archer bot to the mix and suddenly you can have an arrow that you dodged deflected into your back by the sword robot. Another example of this was a kick bot knocking me into the swing of a hammer, perfectly positioning me for the killing blow. The interaction between the enemies results in random and interesting fights each time you play.
The second time sink mode is Challenge Mode. This requires the player to follow handicaps such as using the hammer or bow only, as well as other ones such as random (clone always) upgrade challenge where the upgrade is randomly selected for you, forcing you to (respawn a lot) change your playstyle according to (how many clones you got) what skills you were given. It's a fun mode and it even rewards you with bonus abilities that can be used in endless mode as well as a cool statue in your lobby area.

The content gets updated regularly so that it feels like you have something significant to come back to whenever you see this game has a patch. With the recent addition of photo mode it's also a blast just to try and show off to get a cool looking photo. Overall this is a fantastic game that is well worth the money and time.

This game has been labeled as an DIablo-style FPS, and I can't really think of a better way to describe it - it just says it all!
You start out choosing a class for your avatar, progress through story, earning XP, levels and climbing up the ability tree.
There are no saves to take into account, because a respawn system is in place, taking Your mind of that, and making sure that You just enjoy the game! You still need tactics and proper situation assessment, so it's not a "forgive-all" difficulty - You will still be punished for dying and enemies will respawn after time and regenerate lost hit health.
Each game has random loot, so no two games are exactly the same. It adds a nice touch and makes You think about how to (re-)distribute skill points for the current situation.
When starting out, just take Your time and if You ever feel frustrated, just do some research about some game mechanics/advanced settings. It's very well worth the time for this game :)
I do recommend this game wholeheartedly to anyone, not just the FPS loving crowd :)

“Only you can change the path of faith.”
is an Action-Adventure, Puzzle Platformer, developed by Brazilian-based developer Swordtales & published by Versus Evil.
, Dutch for tower, focuses its gaze on the misadventures of Moonchild, the plot’s female protagonist. Her journey has her ascending a tower to restore some semblance of balance to the universe, all the while re-discovering the nature of her past.
With respect to the gameplay mechanics,
doesn’t conspire to deliver an enjoyable experience. The puzzles are simple, generic & do not feel rewarding once solved. The platforming elements are equally as generic & can be downright buggy. The combat, while rare in the game, is extremely unsatisfying. There are combat glitches which when encountered merited a suicide in order to progress. The camera & controls didn’t feel fluid even while playing with a controller – the game’s suggested input device.
The art style is a flattering backdrop to the story. The game does look downright gorgeous at times, featuring varying colorful environments. Though, there were a number of graphical glitches, including flickering textures. The soundtrack is composed of 23 unique tracks & is fittingly soothing.
is peppered with symbolism, mysticism & poetry so much so that much of it fails to enhance the actual plot of the story. You will encounter story-integral mysticism which pulls from several major religious themes. Much of the poetry is divulged through cut-scenes which cannot be skipped & much of it borders on clichéd one-liners.
In conclusion,
doesn’t seem to have a solitary idea of what it wants to be. It’s a combination of poorly developed platforming, puzzle & combat elements with a unique art style, slapped on what could have very well been a great story. However,
is certainly different & worth a look if seeking a title with a heavy mystical bias without the expectation of anything genre defining.

Dragonball Xenoverse is a typical DBZ fighting game with a vast array of characters & it's own unique character creator that puts YOU in the DBZ timeline.  There is a story, albeit short & cheesy, as well as several side missions (over 50 in total) that allow you to play with friends or strangers online.  There is also a PVP element, however if you've come to play this game for it's PVP you'll be sadly disappointed since the majority of the community has left the game's arena barren & void of any activity.  To put it bluntly, the PVP in this game is not very good.
This game shines most in it's customization & the co-op quests.  The downside to all of this is their network is still in disarray & you will most likely experience lag in any form of online play.  The lag can also break missions & cause them to glitch out becoming unfinishable. The combat is typical of most other DBZ fighters.  You punch people, blast them, & cast crazy super powers of destruction that can anihilate civilizations.  The downside to all this is the destruction element is lacking when compared to previous DBZ fighters.  You can't blow up the planets like you could in Budokai Tenkaichi 2, & you can't destroy very many buildings.  The only buildings you can destroy are the smaller ones that seem out of place in a giant city scape.
The graphics are pretty much a copy/paste set up from older DBZ titles as well as from the Asian only DBZ MMO, with some added glow effects that are more annoying than they're worth.  I had to turn them down just because they made everything too bright & glowy.  You won't need a super rig to run this game at least & since there is a big lack of DBZ games on PC that may be a good thing for everyone who wants one.
The worst or best part about this game is it's RNG system.  Let me explain exactly why this system is both good & bad. Ahem, first of all the game uses a typical RNG element for loot drops.  It uses this same element for Super/Ultimates.  Now, the part that's different & that people seem to be upset about is in order to get the 'best' items/skills in the game each mission has a prerequisite that you must fulfill in order to trigger the event to claim them.  HOWEVER, fulfilling the prerequisite only gives you a 'chance' for that event to occur.  You see where I'm going with this?  You have to fulfill requirements, then you get an RNG event that may or may not happen, THEN you have RNG again on what items will drop.  In short, RNG within RNG within RNG.  It's really terrible & it is a cheap tactic to lengthen the game when it's really not that long to begin with.  You can complete the main story & all the side missions in about 20 or 30 hours, less so if you're used to playing DBZ fighting games.  However, collecting everything in the game will take you hundreds of hours IF you're lucky with this games terrible RNG system.
The plus side to all of this is that the game is overall fun & playing missions over & over again may be tedious & at times frustrating because of it's RNG system you will not ever get bored of the combat while doing said missions.  The combat is a joy & very fun, especially if you have a friend or two to play with you.  You ever sandwich an opponent between 2 kamehameha beams?  Well, me & a buddy did & when we did we couldn't stop talking about how cool it was.
The game's voice acting ranges from great to down right bad.  There are moments where the voice acting seems like they did it in one take, while others are done very well.  These bad segments are few & far between, thankfully. The voice cast has people from the actual show as well as people from DBZ Abridged (Which is a great online series that I highly reccoment watching whether you're a DBZ fan or not).  There's even an easter egg from that show put in the game.
Overall this is a decent single player game with good RPG elements & a good character creator that will give you around 30 or so hours of fun DBZ gameplay goodness, or more if you decide you wanna grind & unlock everything in the game as well as earning the highest rank on every mission.  The online element lags when you group with random people, but works fairly well when you group with friends through Steam.  The group play is a joy if you don't experience any lag but very rarely did I ever get games with no lag.  The PVP is filled with cheap exploitations & some powers in this game give you a feeling that it was just added on as an extra feature since there is no real balance set up for it.
I can only recommend this game for anyone who enjoy's anime fighting games or just wants a DBZ game for PC.  Anyone else may want to steer clear of it's RNG within RNG style dungeon crawl.

I'll put it simply: for 5$, you'll certainly get your money's worth. The game provides a lot of fun for very little risk. However, in my opinion you really should only get it if you have friends also willing to buy the game to play it (or can play locally, which I highly recommend). Playing online quick match is fun, but playing with friends is where the game becomes absolutley phenomenal.
Pros to the game:
The controls are simplistic, yet the stick figures have a ragdoll aspect which causes them to be difficult to maneuver. This is intentional, and creates the perception of real struggle to every battle, as the player not only combats their opponents but also their own ability to control their stick figure. I'd recommend every player use a controller, even though it is harder to control/aim than a keyboard and mouse, because this adds to the intended effect of the game. The problem with mouse and keyboard which I find is it takes one of the more challenging aspects - aiming - and turns it into a trivial matter of simply clicking on your enemy.
The battles are quick paced. Time flies by as one fight transfers to the next fight and so on.
Score isn't kept track of (unless you play local, in which case there is one level which announces current standings). I find this to be a huge benefit. Games like Duck Game get exhausting because gradually one player emerges as the victor over the course of several games and everybody not in the lead is painstakingly aware of it. Contrastingly, in Stick Fight one only remembers who won the previous fight, denoted simply by the presence of a crown. This allows for players to get lost in the present, forgetting deflating aspects like who is winning overall.
The game has a ton of variety for being so simple. Many overall level themes, plus dozens of level designs, combined with the randomness of which weapons happen to spawn makes each match feel like its own experience. My friends and I constantly reflect on specific matches with sentences like "Remember that one time..." and such. However, this random variety isn't fully fleshed out, something I address in the cons.
Cons to the game:
De-sync. The first flaw you will notice is the connectivity issues you will inevitably encounter if you are playing over internet (one of the reasons why local is advisable). However, the fast paced aspect combined with the lack of keeping score over internet makes up for this inherent flaw.
Levels which inhibit randomness and thus variability. This my critique to the creators of this game. Some of the levels have very cool concepts - such as one where you have to fight while avoiding falling spike platforms, or in a pit with snakes slowly seeping in. On the surface these are fantastic concepts, because they add a unique pressure to the game. However, many of the levels that would normally be fun are static. The gun spawns and player spawns are fixed, and over the course of 20 games this begins to devolve into rudimentary repetitive games. My friends and I agree these are the worst levels, because eventually each player learns his or her own way of traversing the level, which kills the variety of the gameplay. This could be infinitely better if random gun drops were enabled for all maps, or better yet player spawns were random! Even if they kept the same spawns, but made is so that a certain player didn't always spawn in the same place (i.e. blue might spawn where red normally would) this would make the game ALOT better.

You wake up in an ocean... How did you get there ? No one knows... In the distance you see an island. You decide to swim towards it. Once you've arrived you see one of the most colorful environments you've ever seen. There are trees, flowers, lakes, bushes, the sun is shining; it just feels so good to be there. It... it feels right. You decide the explore the island a bit. The trees start making noises. Not the annoying or natural kind, but a relaxing kind. You walk on. As you walk on the flowers and bushes start making sounds as well. You realize it's a symphony, a symphony created for you.
A few metres away you spot a group of creatures. You have no idea what sort of creature as it's one you've never ever seen before. You approach them, but... they get scared and run away. While running away, they start making sounds. It's a lovely sound. And even though there are scared you decide to follow them. After following them for a while, enjoying the sounds they create, you start to wander off again.
You head into a different direction. The sun is setting and it's getting dark. Somehow, you're not scared. Even when it's dark the island still looks magical. There are fireflies and stars in the sky. There are even different animals now. You see some white spots that look like insects or flies, you're not sure. There's a whole swarm of them. As somebody who hasnt gotten to play a DBZ fighting game since DBZ: Budokai 2 on Gamecube, being able to finally pick up a next gen DBZ title, and on steam of all places is just perfect for me. I've been a Dragonball Z fan for as long as I can remember, and whether you are a fan or not, I think this game will be a fun and satisfying experience for everybody. The game is able to run very smoothly even on my laptop, and I rarely ever have any issues with playing it.
The only game in my library that I've played longer than this title is Skyrim, and that's saying a lot. There are plenty of things to do in this game, so it'll keep you busy for hours upon hours. The game has full controller support, so and the controls are thankfully very easy to learn, as instead of having to pull off annoying combos, you can just use the trigger buttons to access your Super and Ultimate moves provided you have enough energy to use them. I have had some issues with the game responding to my button presses and a little bit of input lag, but that might just be my computer or the graphics settings.
This game looks pretty, plays well, and is all and all a very fun game to pick up and play. My main criticisms are that sometimes the RNG is terrible and it makes trying to find masters or gathering Dragon Balls or getting certain item drops from quests rather tedious, which can sometimes make playing them feel like a chore. Another thing I would have liked to see was an option in the clothing and accessory shops to preview what you're buying. You dont get to see anything but the name and stats of the clothes you buy, so you either have to look it up online, or buy it blindly. If you dont happen to like it, your only choice is to just deal with it or sell it back for half of what you paid for it. Some quests are also almost unfairly hard, and some of those quests are ones you must get from NPC's, so you may not bring support characters or finish the quest online with a friend until you beat it once by yourself. It wouldnt be so bad if it werent for the fact that some of these involve characters that like to spam their super attacks so much you cant even move and get comboed from full health until you die, one of these quests being one where you have to fight at least 15 characters by yourself to complete it.
Complains aside, this is a really fun game, and an interesting take on the story in the DBZ universe, and I'd recommend it to anyone, especially a DBZ fan.

I have more than 100 hours into the game.  I have received my money’s worth.
That said, this game has the potential to be great, but it’s just not there yet.  First, it has a very steep learning curve and even once you learn to play it, there are just things that don’t make sense.  Let me be clear, not mysterious, just flat do not make sense.
Second, it is not truly a sandbox game ... you are required to do things in a specific order and within a certain time frame or the AI will simply just defeat you.  It is sandbox only in that the game allows you to ignore the required steps so the AI can destroy you.
And that is part of the problem with the game.  It is a one-man development team and he seems to believe it is the task of the AI to beat you, rather than just making it challenging so you can try different things.  And his supporters will flat tell you in the forums "It’s fun to lose."
Personally, I don't find spending hours developing a colony, just to have the AI slam you with some event or catastrophe that results in the loss of all that work, fun.  Rather, I find it damned annoying.
You can certainly cheat and continue to reload saved games ... but that is not my idea of a "game".
Third, this game is HEAVILY focused on a "morale" system.  And just like with every other game that uses morale as part of the challenge, you reach a point where you just can’t satisfy your colonists … they start killing each other, killing your animals, burning your buildings/crops and just going on a walk-about they never return from.
The developer explains this in a round about way as a lessoning value derived from enterainment as the colonists get used to whatever you have offered them … but there’s only like 5 things you have at your disposal to offer them … even I can only watch one TV at a time, and yes, it does get boring.   I suppose you could put a plant or statue every 5 feet in your colony, but this again would be an example of it not really being a sandbox game ... but more a puzzle game.
Finally, the developer believes there was never a drug made (required here) the citizenry doesn’t get addicted to.  So the drugs you are required to research, grow, and manufacture, become a frustrating micromanagement scenario where you need to let them have access to them, but don’t let them have access too long, and make sure you keep them locked away, but don't forget they need it, and … /sigh.
So what turns out, at first, to be promising and refreshing new builder game, evolves into a click-fest that just becomes an exercise in frustration.
And yes, his rabid supporters, and there are many, will be in your face telling you, “IT’S ALPHA!”  Yes, it is … for more than a year now.   “It’s Alpha” has become the badge of immunity and cover for developers when their games are criticized.
I would wait until its released as a finished product and then wait for the reviews on that game.  Since developers seem to frequently ruin promising games as they approach release.  Or worse, never finish it for release.
This is just one man's opinion.

A great real time strategy game. The premise is to move out to various cities and rescue surviors by placing a "go here" mark that your helicopter arrives at every so often to pick up survivors. The game is seen entirely from a bird eyes view giving you full awareness of where the survivors are and where the zombies are coming from. Over time you earn various mercenaries and items to help. Snipers, soldiers, barricades, cannons, mines, nukes, and more. These can all be leveled up over time. Saving scientists allow you to buy various extra upgrades. You might save every survivor from a city, or maybe become overwhelmed and lose. You simply move from city to city saving as much as possible. The game is a race to see who can get enough points first. You get points for saving people, clearing cities, etc. The zombies get points for eating people, taking over cities, etc. Whoever reaches the point goal wins, so the game has a board game feel. NOW GET OUT THERE AND BEAT THE ZAMBIES!

There is a review somewhere on here were a fellow talks about how terrible the game is because of the aiming system. He says that he aims right at the bad guy and the shot misses and when he aims of to the side of the bad guy the bullet hits him. Do to this he says, the game is crap. This guy forgot a very important aspect of the game; it's a First Person Shooter-RPG not just a fps. In a regular fps, your guns are powerful the only thing standing between you and killing your enemy is how good you aim. In a FPS-RPG your guns have stats. You could have the best aim in the world but if your gun sucks, you're gonna get mauled down faster than a turkey on thanksgiving. On the other hand if your aim sucks but you have a powerful gun just run up to the guy and blast him and if you get swarmed by a bunch enemies no problem because in this game, it's all about the guns. And second winds, the best aspect of this game.
Normally if your get shot down in a game you die and have to restart the level or whatever, but in this game if your shield and health bar deplete to zero you have a chance to kill and enemy before you bleed to death and catch a Second Wind in which your shield regenerates and you can go on killing baddies. This single element gives you the freedom to play the game anyway you like. You can run and gun, or stealth kill or both whatever. Just make sure you have a good gun and a good shield ALWAYS or your second wind rampages will be short lived.
Death is the difference between losing money and not losing money. When you die you respawn at a checkpoint and get charged a fee which is a percentage of the amount of money you have so, if you low on cash it's possible to respawn for like 3 bucks. Don't worry about having to kill the same baddies over again because in this game, when you kill an enemy in an area but another one kills you, when you respawn the enemies you killed WON'T Be there anymore. Let me say that again, enemies you killed already will not respawn when you die. They will only comeback when you exit the game and reload or in some cases, when you return to the area at a later time. This is great because even if a second wind can't save you then just walk back and take out what bad guys are left.
One important thing though, the health bars of guys you didn't kill will regenerate when you respawn, so if you're fighting a boss and die, he will be at full health when you return. You need to have at least some strategy in this game though because a run and gun will NOT always work. Especially with bosses. Using Second Winds is a strategy in its self that can be very effective and an extremely fun way to play, but if you do not use it properly you will lose money FAST and/or get repeatedly killed by gang lords.
That begin said don't worry too much about boss fights, they are a fun aspect of the game because you can approach the battle anyway you like. The boss battles are as challenging as you make then. Exploit the bosses attack range and spam yours or fight him legitimately in a head to head arena using the proper dodge, cover and aim techniques; either way boss killing is satisfying.
You have a lot of control on how you play the game with the skills, guns, approaches, ect you discover. I won't ruin it all for you and leave you to figure them out for yourself. All in all, this is probably the best game I have played do to the fact that you can play the game however you want to. In short, Get. This. Game.

While I can see some appeal here in the attempt to tell a good story, and the attempt to look pretty in the process, the constant crawling pace, combined with a mash of low-res textures, buggy movement/jumping, and absolutely no guidance as to what's happening, why, and what you should do about it, Toren reaches for the stars and falls down into the abyss in almost every aspect with the only exception being it's fantastic modelling.
Toren is an abstract, 3D story game, with about 2 hours of game play if you don't throw down your controller (or moon forbid, using a keyboard and mouse) in frustration from missing a jump because the camera angle decided to wildly change mid-air, or you miss safety by a hairs-breath and the game forces you to go back 2-3min of slow backtracking.
If the movement speed was increased, and cutscenes were skippable, you could probably finish this game in about 20minutes without trying too hard. Alas, even the invisible ball-and-chain wrapped around Toren's ankle doesn't provide much for gameplay like many other story-based platformers. All you have to soak in is moving objects clipping each other, blurry rocks next to highly detailed stairs, while your camera spins jumps and judders going from too-slow to too-fast in a few seconds.
Perhaps if this game had a team of people building it and some sort of quality control, instead of seeming like one art student's University project, it might have been better.

This game deserves a review because its awesome!  You can play all night if you are not careful, its one of those “just one more move” type games.
The idea of a story teller AI really fits- because your colony does have a story. The colonists contribute to the story in so many ways, with their personalities, social interactions, sculpture creations reflecting their own story, etc. But that's not all!  You contribute of course, you have the freedom to create, to expand, to fight, so much.
Even the graphics have their own sort of cool charm and style. There is a good sense of humor here too in many places.
The con is that because there are so many possibilities, this game could experience "feature creep" and just keep adding patches and new things.  At some point they should limit the scope and make what they have carved out awesome. Also the interface could use some more improvements, like what is that blob, sandstone or granite?  etc.  Maybe a hotkey to show text over every space or resource on teh screen on/off.

My nurse ran out to rescue the ranger-- and at the same the ranger's long lost brother escaped 2 raiders nearby and fled to my colony!  Two of five of my colonists were knocked out by the muffalo, then the raiders show up and start lighting fires!  They destroy half my supplies, all my medicine, and burn down half my warehouse.  One attempts to kidnap my nurse and the ranger's long lost brother, naked, grabbing a pistol off my dead doctor, chases after him and saves the nurse.  Then he returns to kill the other pyro raider inside my colony's walls, put out the fire, cut down some herbal root to revive the nurse (so she can tend to the 3 other wounded colonists). This game is outstanding in the depth of it's character creation, and for a game capitalizing on a franchise that has ceased to be relevant, I'm glad so much work was put into this game. The animation is smooth, the difficulty is very balanced, and there was a surprising amount of depth put into the settings for the PC version. Full disclosure: I came into this game expecting to be disappointed by another attempt by a company at capitalizing on a rapidly fading franchise before it died.
What I got was a very fun game, and that is saying a lot as I don't like fighting games in general. I'm also not very good at them. The only two complaints I have are the combat system, which has depth, but the depth is overshadowed by the unbalanced attack types. There are WAY more energy attacks than physical attacks in this game, and that makes a creating a character that gets up close and personal a bit difficult, but not impossible. The second problem I have is the story mode, which goes from being on par with a normal DBZ episode to being an incredibly bad self-insert Mary-Sue fanfiction in the blink of an eye. There is one point where the player character actually helps Goku push an enemy back because he doesn't have enough energy left to maintain a Spirit Bomb. That's right, you get behind the Spirit Bomb and push it forward to overpower the enemy that is trying to push it back. There are several parts of the main story that are like this and I found myself groaning audibly while watching them.
This being said, this game is a fighting game, and the fighting mechanics are good. If you are playing this game for the story, you are looking in the wrong direction. If you want to have fun being an OP energy shooting alien, then this is the game for you. Goku Simulator 2015 is the top fighting game for those that want to bring their Deviant Art OCs (please don't steal) to live.

To call Proteus a game would be selling it short. Much like Dear Esther, Proteus isn't so much a game, as it is an art piece. Unlike Dear Esther though, each viewing is different, your islands are randomly generated. The graphics and sound are all perfectly simplistic and work oh so well in tandem. The only interactions are your movements and discoveries through the beautifully pixelated world. The sound especially is the draw, changing to different soothing tones based off your surroundings and season. While it's possible to see everything in a single island, you'll want to keep coming back to view it in a different setting. If you find something that takes your breath away, you can share the postcard (F9 ingame) with friends to let them explore the same island. If you're at all interested in interactive art, Proteus is a must play.

Or, you may find yourself hated by many, and being driven out of the EVE universe. However, most don't reach this level, and many quit before giving the game a chance. I recently purchased an x-box 1 controller and have been trying to cover controller controls on games with my reviews, but for this one apparently it doesn't like my xbox 1 controller. I just grabbed an x-box controller, I didn't know some games don't like 'em. I even tried downloading a button mapper which would emulate a regular x-box controller... no dice.
In the end it was too much work, and I just concluded I'll get better with a keyboard and mouse, the problem is you don't know all the buttons unless you read a guide or somehow guess each button.
Here's the basic's to get you started: Space is Drift, arrow keys will direct you, Shift to accelerate (P.S. your pinky-finger will hate you after a few races), and E to fire a weapon. You can also flip using WASD but I forget about the flips because I'm a baddy mcbad-face.
If you want to save some time, check out any of the top rated Sonic and All-Stars Racing Transformed beginer's guides located here:
There are three game play types in Sonic All stars racing transformed
There are three game types: Career, Match Making, and Custom Game.
For the Career you play against the AI, having easy, medium, and hard difficulty NPC's. In world tour there are 5 worlds and roughly 8 levels each world, plus character unlocks. In Grand Prix there are 5 cups, and 4 races per cup, lastly there's a lot of levels in time attack and single race mode
Regarding Match making, you can play online in three game modes: Race, Arena, and Lucky Dip, there are also respective stats, win loss ratio, games played wins, and ratings, for all you junkies who aren't desensitized yet.
Custom Game is exclusively for multiplayer, you can play local co-op, if you have enough controllers plugged in, you can play with up to 4 friends locally
and online you can play with your online friends.
Okay, so we've talked about the types of game modes, and pretty well spelled out there's a lot of different levels to keep you busy for some time... How does the game FEEL?
Well, it feels like a Mario Kart Game, but with Sonic Characters and Danica Patrick.
You race along a course, the course will sometimes change on the last lap of a race, you pick up items, some will boost you, some will you aim and throw, others help the last place scrublord like me while playing online
I'm not the best person to speak to when it comes to potential that a racing game has because I'm not particularly skilled at them to begin with, but I could easily see this game being the type of game you play with a group of friends like many of us used to do back in our Mario Kart Days on the N64.
What I'm trying to say is; I liked it. I'll play it more, I'm not good at it, but I don't feel like I need to be good at something to enjoy it.
Hopefully this review has been either entertaining, informative, or inspiring. My name's Atratzu and I approve this review.

You can work around this by adding a line or two to one of the config files (see PCGamingWiki for details) and then pressing a button once every time you enter a game or enter/exit a vehicle to set the FOV to a much better value.
If you are willing to work around (or live with) the technical flaws, it is in my mind the best of the Borderlands games. The DLCs are pretty decent. One of them allows you to fight large mechs, which is cool. The swamp DLC is rather dull and repetitive unless you really enjoy zombies, but you might as well pick up the GOTY edition anyway.

Great game!
In short (if you didnt see the trailer/read the description) its a puzzle game where you combine movement, hiding, buttonpressing and trapmaking to proceed in the levels. Its not really a platformer, but you do need to take your character around the map to reach physical objectives.
You are quite free to kill your way through it all, play it entirely non-lethal or try and ghost the levels, it only affects your rating which really didnt seem to have any impact at all on the rest of the game. As a side note: i got A as the lowest rating in the missions so maybe something happen when you get B's or C's.
Its not superlong, maybe 3h long in total if you take it slow like me, I have played it in total 4½ hours and I've been achievement hunting (have 5 left now!) the rest of the time.
Depending on how you wanna play it, it gets harder. Ghosting is of course the hardest but if you like playing it fast and loose and kicking down doors (technically you only get this for the last mission, but you can replay the earlier ones with all abilities if you want) you can finish a level in under a minute if you know what youre doing.
Its fun and can be a bit tricky if you aim for non-lethal, ghosting, etc. But if you screw up you only rewind a few seconds and youre back to it and can continue like it never happened, works superwell!
Movement and jumping works great, you can stick to the walls or climb in the ceiling, this is a great tool to let you plan how you wanna do the mission.
Puzzles are quite straight forward in the beginning, but gets more complex when closed circuits (color coded circuits) gets introduced.
The music is great and fits very well in the theme of the game.
Bugwise I have had no crashes, but one achievement have so far eluded me ONLY  because of bugs. Minor, but still annoying. :)
Can recommend to people who like a bit of sneaking around and puzzle games.

Easily one of the most over-rated games I have ever played. A Fallout clone meets uninspired WoW RPG interface that lacks serious polish. I didn't mind the cell shading but question it's effectiveness in a post apocalyptic-like setting. Everything is just brown and bland including the enemies.
The clunky and erratic aiming controls on the console make over-powered general mobs incredibly frustrating. Enemy AI seems to exploit these poor controls by straffing and sprinting all over while they posses near perfect aim. Axe wielding mobs are insanely ridiculous as they can heave axes from miles away with dead on accuracy (even over huge boulders or cover) all while you struggle with the aim of a sniper rifle.
As an FPS this game is pretty weak compared to other offerings out there. Even with sensitivity turned way up the aim is always poor. Weapons have erratic aim. Some shots will land crits while other perfectly aimed shots miss or register next to no damage. Explosives can go off at enemy or even your own feet dealing little to no damage then a grenade 10 feet away can kill you or a mob. Weapons are also pretty bland with just different stats.
Basically I never felt like I was progressing in this game. Most RPGs allow players to reach a point where they develop their stats enough to manipulate the game engine and make playthrough either easier or more enjoyable. Borderlands always has the player feeling like he is horribly underpowered and no amount of leveling really matters. It's all luck based on which weapons you find. The sotry is kind of vague and most quests are just random fetch quests or bounty missions. I never really had a full understanding of what I was doing. I gather the single player story is short but after 8 hours of just monotonous grinding I won't be finishing this title. There are way better games to play and the release of Borderlands 2 will not be seeing me as a customer. Even as a budget title I would give this a miss.

*note:  "-" is not a minus sign, just a dash sign to signify that I am organizing this review on a point-by-point basis, instead of pros & cons.
- Reminded me personally of a cinematic Dark Souls.
- This game is very heavily story-driven, with numerous cutscenes, lots of lore, pretty cool quotes and dialogue, and lots of obscurity. For some, these varying points could be plusses or minuses.
- I did expect there to be more action-esque gameplay where you fight enemies, but there is only one enemy of which you were really intended to fight (I also expected there to be more enemies to fight.) You fight this enemy a few times, and each time involves some sort of "puzzle," or at least something else that you must do besides hack n' slash.
- You are expected to die a few times, I would say.
- I was able to do one run-through of the game in about 2 hours
Ultimately, I am simply content with my purchase. I'd say I can recommend this game, but be aware of the points I made above, particularly the fact that I, and many others, finished the game at least once with 2 - 5 hours of gameplay, and that it is very cinematic with not very much action.

This game, for that price? No. And when I say "No," What I really mean is "Nooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo!"

There are three modes to play, and you'll be waiting for a very long time to get into a lobby for any of them, and that's when the game isn't crashing.

Get the game through the code and means stated in other reviews, but DO NOT spend $30 on it. You can get infinitely more for that price.

NOTE: At the time of writing this, I've only played about 30 mins worth of the game, so keep that in mind.
Toren is about the story of a young girl named Moonchild, who is the last hope for mankind. As the story explains, Man sought to end its battle with Time by building a tower, Toren, to the sky and capturing the Moon. The Sun didn't take too kindly to this. It's now up to Moonchild to defeat the Dragon and restore things.
Toren is a platformer with little action early on. There is some light puzzle solving (if you could call it that), but mostly it's atmospheric. Again, I've not played much & where I left off, I was in a fight with the Dragon that I lost.
You play as Moonchild in three stages; as a baby/toddler, as a young child & then as an adolescent. Early on, you're going to be mostly playing in the young child form, but alternating as the story/memories progress.
:
- Toren is absolutely beautiful. Similar to Life is Strange, the art style is a bit off but in a charming way. While it looks polygonal, you feel like that was the direction, rather than because they couldn't afford (or had the skillset) to make it look more crisp. I dunno how to exactly word it other than it feels right. The colors are vibrant when they want to be & dull when they're supposed to. It's very amazing how starkly it contrats & gets it right.
- The story, so far, is very good. I like that, while it is a rather played out plot, the story itself is quite unique. Plus the storytelling itself is well done. I'm hooked on it.
- The "puzzles" (again, so far) haven't been too difficult. People might think, "Why is that a good thing?" and, I think, this game may be more suited for a younger audience. That doesn't mean everyone won't enjoy some of it.
- The music is incredible. I love it. It's so soothing and joyful to listen to, but it also gets pretty good when combat is going on, too. Overall, a very good score.
:
- The biggest gripe I have with the game, so far, is the combat. While there is very little that I've experienced, I'm not a fan of standing still when I swing my sword. Maybe it's because of the form I'm in, but I'm hoping that this changes later on, in her adolescent form.
- When the narrator is talking, sometimes the background music will completely drain him out. Now, I get that he's speaking in tongues (I don't think it's actually Brazilian), but I would have rather heard him speak this language, than just the background music.
- The jumping animation looks bad. You hover more than anything.
- Collision issues. Walked up a flight of stairs and I couldn't proceed to the platform until I took a step back, then forward. Nothing was in my way to hinder me.
:
I'd give this game about a 7 out of 10. I think what it does right, it really does right. The minor things that hold it back - like the collision issues - are nothing a patch or two can't fix. But there are a few design flaws that really make you scratch your head.
At its current price, $10 USD, I would say it's definitely worth buying but understand that it is flawed (like any other game, I know). For what it brings to the table, I honestly have enjoyed my little time with it.

In this game you mine, build, craft, grow crops, breed animals, trade, form caravans, explore, fight, quest, research, slave-trade, do surgery, harvest organs, capture prisoners, "get some lovin'" (sometimes "x2," which, for a man my age, can be considered impressive) and the best part is: everything is well done, all of it works just fine and, as far as I can tell, the game is bug-free.
Your characters also interact socially with each other. They can become rivals, friends, lovers, or married (they can't have children though, at least not yet) so... there's also some The Sims to it... or rather some Big Brother--since some of them are pyromaniacs, drug addicts, alcoholics, lazy, psychopats or just plain A-holes.
Two things in particular are worth mentioning:
1 - Each of your characters' individual body parts can be damaged sepparately, and you can install prosthetics/bionic implants on them to substitute damaged limbs or otherwise just improve some of their weaknesses.
2 - The combat is fairly strategic and rather fun for a game like this. There's ranged and melee combat, and cover-usage. You can also unleash your animals upon your foes.
You roll the stats of 3 randomized characters to start the game with, then choose a starting location on a random-generated planet, build your base, buy/capture/rescue more people, raise their stats, research, trade, fight, craft/find/buy some gear, and have fun while you try to send your colonists back into space.
- Although the game is good, the price is rather steep for an EA, one-dev game.
- Not necessarily a con, but... I really don't get all the "story-driven game" stuff. I guess you can try to do a "farmers-only colony," a tribe of slave-trading cyborgs, focus on drug-dealing or whatever, but there's no real point in doing so. All skills/trades are useful, and you'll do much better just using all of them and playing always pretty much the same way.
You can choose one out of 3 "story-tellers" (databanks from which the random events that will happen during the game will be extracted) when you start a new colony-- and I've only played with the easiest one, true-- but said "events," at least at the moment, are just random raids on your base, materials falling from space, random people joining your colony... calling it a "story-driven" game sounds like a bit of a stretch to me.
Do not play in permadeath-mode (although it's the way "the game is intended to be played") until you know what you are doing. There are things you gotta try out to see if/how they work and, if they don't, there's a good chance you'll lose too much (or everything) and have to start over.

First and foremost I want to praise the outstanding soundtrack and art direction. They are a quite amazing feat, coming from a small unknown studio. If you like art games like Ico or Journey, you should feel right at home.
However, the gameplay could use a little more variety as some mechanics are very simple and the puzzles take almost no effort to finish. The combat would also benefit of some fine tuning as well as there are few enemies and you can just avoid them if you so wish. The boss battles, on the other hand, are very creative and fun, especially the final one. This is a game that starts out slow and just gets better as you progress through it.

First off, Deformers has 3 modes, Deathmatch, Team Deathmatch, and Form Goal, which is essentially Rocket League. There's no tutorial in the game, so learning about the different classes, and how to do different abilites is non-existent.
That alone can be annoying, especially when a game starts and for some reason it's 4p on 2p, pretty much, you not knowing how to play, makes it 4 on 1.
Then comes the framerate, Its not a solid 60 or higher, even with setting the minimum FPS to 90 in options, and the maximum turned off, the FPS counter while playing fluctuates between 30 - 50 FPS. It also fluctuates way too often for no apparent reason. Yet I can jump into another game like DOOM and that game has no issues with keeping a solid FPS of 60+. (Which means it's a game issue, not a hardware issue).
Why this game came off of of Early Access and decided to release despite broken is beyond me, but it's quite apparent why Gamestop is giving this away for free. Also in that same logic, I feel bad for anyone who paid $30.00 for it..There isn't $30 worth of content in the game, and the fact that microtransactions are present without the content is horrifying. Save your money...

Proteus is more of a work of art than a game. Every new game (there is no saving, everytime you play is a new game) is a relaxing walk through new a dreamlike retro game style musical landscape.
If you've ever set out in games like Skyrim, Minecraft or Fallout 3 to just explore the world, you'll probably enjoy playing this. If you are too busy playing the game to ever do that, you'll probably feel like everyting that makes games fun is missing from this.
No Checkpoints, Campaign restarts on any difficulty.

I'll put it simply: for 5$, you'll certainly get your money's worth. The game provides a lot of fun for very little risk. However, in my opinion you really should only get it if you have friends also willing to buy the game to play it (or can play locally, which I highly recommend). Playing online quick match is fun, but playing with friends is where the game becomes absolutley phenomenal.
Pros to the game:
The controls are simplistic, yet the stick figures have a ragdoll aspect which causes them to be difficult to maneuver. This is intentional, and creates the perception of real struggle to every battle, as the player not only combats their opponents but also their own ability to control their stick figure. I'd recommend every player use a controller, even though it is harder to control/aim than a keyboard and mouse, because this adds to the intended effect of the game. The problem with mouse and keyboard which I find is it takes one of the more challenging aspects - aiming - and turns it into a trivial matter of simply clicking on your enemy.
The battles are quick paced. Time flies by as one fight transfers to the next fight and so on.
Score isn't kept track of (unless you play local, in which case there is one level which announces current standings). I find this to be a huge benefit. Games like Duck Game get exhausting because gradually one player emerges as the victor over the course of several games and everybody not in the lead is painstakingly aware of it. Contrastingly, in Stick Fight one only remembers who won the previous fight, denoted simply by the presence of a crown. This allows for players to get lost in the present, forgetting deflating aspects like who is winning overall.
The game has a ton of variety for being so simple. Many overall level themes, plus dozens of level designs, combined with the randomness of which weapons happen to spawn makes each match feel like its own experience. My friends and I constantly reflect on specific matches with sentences like "Remember that one time..." and such. However, this random variety isn't fully fleshed out, something I address in the cons.
Cons to the game:
De-sync. The first flaw you will notice is the connectivity issues you will inevitably encounter if you are playing over internet (one of the reasons why local is advisable). However, the fast paced aspect combined with the lack of keeping score over internet makes up for this inherent flaw.
Levels which inhibit randomness and thus variability. This my critique to the creators of this game. Some of the levels have very cool concepts - such as one where you have to fight while avoiding falling spike platforms, or in a pit with snakes slowly seeping in. On the surface these are fantastic concepts, because they add a unique pressure to the game. However, many of the levels that would normally be fun are static. The gun spawns and player spawns are fixed, and over the course of 20 games this begins to devolve into rudimentary repetitive games. My friends and I agree these are the worst levels, because eventually each player learns his or her own way of traversing the level, which kills the variety of the gameplay. This could be infinitely better if random gun drops were enabled for all maps, or better yet player spawns were random! Even if they kept the same spawns, but made is so that a certain player didn't always spawn in the same place (i.e. blue might spawn where red normally would) this would make the game ALOT better.

Atom Zombie Smasher is a strategy game where you defeat the zombie invasion by repelling  or destroying hordes of zombies as they close in on the survivors you're trying to rescue.
The game has an overworld campaign, where you try to prevent the zombies from spreading out of control, and the city section, where you kill lots of zombies. The overworld plays a bit like Risk. The city sections play very differently depending on what weapons you have available, and this is random. If you have artillery and snipers, it's not too hard to annihilate the zombies quickly. If you have roadblocks and bait, then you need to get everyone out quickly.
I've definitely enjoyed it so far. The biggest flaws are its weak tutorial and the fact that a bad choice of random weapons might force you to concede a map. But, the strategy's good and it's fun to play. I haven't tried the local co-op yet... seems fun though.
If you like strategy games, I think this is worth picking up, but your milage may vary.

Ok, there are some bad reviews.  However if you look at the big picture, I think they are unjustified. This game is definitely worth the price of admission!
First, this isn't a huge developing house pushing out games and running with the cash after the release.
This is a small ( 2-3 man ) dedicated team working on sharing their passion with the public.
Second, for the price and replay value, you would be very hard pressed to find a better game.  My logged time ( probably twice what is shown since I play off-line more -- limited internet ) is proof that I keep coming back for more.
Third, bug resolution, they do get fixed.  Some may gripe about this and that ( I have done some myself in the heat of the moment - I think we all get a little hot headed when something in a game changes how we play it ) but things do get fixed and changed.
The ultimate things to consider are these....
Do you have someone or someway to give feedback? -->  Yes
Will someone on the other end actually listen to and consider the feedback? -->  Yes
Will said feedback be implemented if enough people agree? -->  Yes
Does the Development Team  actually care about their product and you? -->  Yes
If the answers are  Yes   to the above ( In this case they really are!  Honest Abe! ) then you have found a true GEM!

Toren is a beautiful game. So much detail is packed into every nook and cranny of a scene. You can see the dust, feel the breeze of the wind, and that something strange is going on. Musically everything is superb in Toren as well. The orchestral music heightens moments in engaging fashion, What Toren reminds me of is an art piece. Beautiful to look at but functionality is simple and not complicated.
The puzzle elements tend to repeat themselves. From pouring of salt, to basic platforming. Combat is almost non-existent. The story is presented in the form of poetry and ambiguous cut scenes. I have beaten Toren and still don't understand what the game was all about. That isn't a bad thing though. Toren is a game that is open to interpretation and for the participant to define.
If you don't mind feeling lost and not having all the answers. Even when the game is done, then Toren's story is masterfully told. However some might be put off by its atypical story. The game may repeat certain puzzle elements but none of them over stay their welcome. Toren is a short game. Taking anywhere from 3 to 4 hours at most. Less, if you follow the games queues and never stray from the path. However there is secrets to be found. Even though you constantly feel as if you are being pushed forward. Toren is a game worth experiencing. Just enjoy the ride and don't worry about understanding everything. Like Art.

As the name suggest this game is a joy to play. That is when it's not making you want to put your fist through the screen. The platforming controls are simple but perfect. There's enough variation to keep it interesting and the level design is fantastic, so much so that I can't think of a single boring or uninteresting level. To compliment the simplistic controls ESJ boasts a simple yet beautiful art style with bright colours and stark contrast that makes every level visual interesting as you make your way over blocks and enemies to the tune of the masterfully done techno soundtrack.
Though it is accessible and easy to pick up and play, it is rather difficult to master and the later levels in particular will present a good challenge to even the most experienced platformer players. And as if that wasn't enough there's an abundance of optional challenge levels to try your patience.
Overall the game is fantastic. The gameplay, visuals and music all work together to present a tough but fair challenge, with plenty of replay value in the form of collectables.

for this game just being released, it's absolutely insane.
forget what other people in the reviews say about content, would you say rocket league is starved of content? hell no!
that's because rocket league is built on replay value, getting better, mastering, and ♥♥♥♥ing up absolutely everyone in your path.
---
GENERAL GAMEPLAY ;
deformers is a third person, movement and physics based arena brawler. it's built around two gamemodes (for now)
the first gamemode is deathmatch, or team deathmatch. you know how it works, you use a dash mechanic to ram people off the map, or just bop the living hell out of them until they explode.
it's packed with powerups (that actually work, and feel rewarding) and vibrant, interactive maps where you can learn your environment to bamboozle your enemies. this one's my favorite, i've absolutely loved jumping in with a friend and providing fun communication to team up and squish people to oblivion.
the second gamemode, for lack of a better term, is rocket league. but hold up, because it's not JUST rocket league, it's rocket league with hilarious character, physics, and far smoother gameplay. you roll, grab, toss, lob, your way to victory in a team versus team arena, the game from the stands doesn't look like it's too complicated, but it really is jam packed with advanced mechanics where you can, if mastered, throw the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of everything and feel like a genius.
technical wise, the game runs smooth, it's fast paced, fluid, you never skip a second of being able to interact with it. nothing feels on a grid, even the menus are this jiggly, fun experience.
---
CUSTOMIZATION ;
people talk a lot of♥♥♥♥♥♥on customization mechanics, people make fun of unlocking hats, but let me tell you, this game does it so beautifully. the variety is SHOCKING, there's literally SO MUCH YOU CAN UNLOCK? i almost cried when i first visited those menus.
HATS, GLASSES, BACKPACKS, SOUND PACKS, SPRAYS ETC. ALL UNLOCKABLE WITHOUT DROPPING A PENNY.
dude, there is h u n d r e d s of items.
---
SUMMARY ;
dude, it's REALLY, REALLY, good. thirty dollars? honestly, with the production quality and development + fine tuning, i'd feel awful asking for anything less.
every once in a while, something will come into your life where you wake up, think about it, go throughout your day thinking about it, and when you lay your head on that cold pillow, you still feel jitters in your fingers thinking about it.
deformers is that game, don't be hesitant, don't second guess, it really is wonderful. if you like fast paced, high skill cap, fun, physics brawlers that'll have you ♥♥♥♥ing crying laughing, you'd be a♥♥♥♥♥♥to ask for any game other than deformers.

I don't usually do this type of stuff but I feel like Toren deserves it because it's weird. I say weird because I don't know why I liked it.
I completed the game in about two hours, two very good hours mind you, and even now that I've finished it I don't know what it was I just played. Toren is supposed to be a Adventure, platform something dead baby, and it is, except for the dead baby, that I can say for certain. You do some simplistic puzzles that aren't to hard to figure out and they get more clever the further you get into the game. Some puzzles I overlooked that made them somewhat harder, like having to draw a symbol on the ground in pitch black darkness, thing was that I didn't notice was that you could get a god damn torch :/
But the platforming and puzzles are solid and fun and you get this very Indie feel as you play the game, character is clipping through everything for one. But aside that I really enjoyed the gameplay and thought it was fun.
And that must be the reason I liked the game because it was the thing I didn't expect to enjoy, thus it surprised me. Why I bought the game was not because of some gameplay video, it was because of the story. I don't facking know what the story was, I really don't. I'm more confident in guessing the contents of my friends balls then I am starting to guess the story of this game. Now, this isn't necessarily a bad thing, it's a good thing, it adds replayability if anything. So I may not have understood what happened in my first run through the game, but maybe the second time will yield some results or the third. It's intresting for a game to add replayability through story rather then unlockables or new gear and the like. It could also get boring as you are forced to to the same exact thing over and over again, but since the game is so short I don't see that as a problem.
Last thing I want to mention it that I really liked the character model, or what they did with it. The character is going through "stages" of human life (Baby, child, teenager, adult) and the model changes when I happens which I find really cool, especially the last one (I have a thing for capes!).
All in all, a very enjoyable experience, I'd rather have two really good hours of gameplay and story then having to play ninety hours of things I don't want to do just to reach the end, I'm looking at you Dragon Age Inquisition!

Killer Instinct is the revival of a long-gone fighting game series spanning back to the SNES, and finally comes to steam! The series is well known for being a conventional fighting game, with more of a push towards high combo strings and being as flashy as possible. One of the main features to create this remains, in the auto-double system - allowing the player to input certain buttons in sequence to perform longer combos semi-automatically. In order to suit the game more to the common person, they have also added an optional feature, called the "Combo Assist" mode, which allows the player to simply press a button alone to help them in their combos, instead of entering complex motions. However, the player will still have to enter special move inputs to start combos. The comboing system in KI3 has been set into specific segments of the combo for the player to remember. They start of their combos with an Opener, which will link into an auto-double, then they can either input a linker move (which will then lead into another auto-double) or they can end their combo with an ender move, which will deal the most damage, and will take away all potential damage through the combo. You can also link a linker to a linker to an ender, but you will have to keep the combo short enough so that the enemy does not break out of it, due to another system which measures the amount of damage given in a combo.
This is all backed up by an incredible soundtrack produced by Mick Gordon, Celldweller and Atlas Plug, all presented in the battle through a dynamic music system, with all the songs eventually reaching their culmination in a huge automatic ULTRA COMBO. You cannot forget the awesome work by the announcers in the different announcer packs which are unlockable, all providing the correct amounts of screams and shouts to get anyone pumping.
The visuals are nothing to sniff at either, with 3D models through the characters and the background stages being at a consistent texture quality that won't break your immersion at any time.
