My hours are inflated due to frequent AFK's, but I'd peg my hours around 350. This game is amazing. I'd call it probably the closest spiritual successor to Dwarf fortress, that despite lacking the multiple z-levels, has all of the "fun" that DF promises. The creators are updating constantly with new stuff like Caravans, Quests, and the ability to have more than one settlement (if your computer can handle it). The modding community is vibrant and allows you to transform this game into a lovecraftian tale, a technocratic paradise, or cannabalistic dictatorship.
Of course, the game is still in Early Access which means it's always evolving and considered "unfinished." That being said, this game is more complete than some full releases you will see in the Steam catalogue. The devs make significant updates every few months which will blow up your mods for a period of time. But I encourage playing the vanilla game at least once to completion to appreciate the original intent of the game. I do not have bugs occur very often, I honestly struggle to think of one at this time.
When you start up, you can either choose to read up guides or go in blind, whatever style floats your boat. But remember that losing is part of the fun - the community actively shares the tales of their triumphs and tragedies:
-I had my first major colony collapse because all of my huskies became raging alcoholics who vomited everywhere and wouldn't fight or haul. The colonists died to a raid, and the dogs lived out the last of their days getting rip roaring drunk.
-I operated on an individual to give them bionic arms, legs, spine, and organs. During fights he was a flash on the battlefield who could annhilate an army alone without a scratch. He died from a javelin in the head because I forgot to make everyone helmets. His wife went insane with grief, drugged herself  into a stupor, and ended up in the hospital. Nobody else was trained for combat at his level besides his wife. We died to a mob of wolves, his wife being torn apart in her hospital bed.
-After seasons of trying to create a respectable colony selling poorly crafted clothing, I moved to becoming drug kingpins. I started mass producing drugs, selling them for massive profits, outfitting every colonist with guns and advanced bionics. Walls could be built in an instant, one individual punched a scyther to death, massive raids would die before even hitting my kill box. I turned the colony into a depot, taking in new refugees daily and sending periodic ships of colonists to space. It only ended after a developer update that added the caravans.
Anyway, if you're still reading, just buy the game. It's worth the 30$ regardless of how you play because of the multiple "storytellers" that randomly choose events of varying threat levels. You can play on base building mode with minimal threats, or back breaking hard mode. It's your rimworld, your rules. Don't let your dreams be dreams, just do it!

Astray is a horror game that takes you to the Museum of the Supernatural at night. While the game has its share of bugs and oddities, I really enjoyed it.
Pros:
-Story: While the story wasn't incredibly well fleshed out, I thought it was reasonably creative and did a decent job of explaining what was going on.
-Environments: The environments in Astray aren't very detailed, but they get the job done. I especially liked the art style in the Atlantis exhibit.
Cons:
-Notes: Outside of the notes contained within some of the puzzles, most of the notes were pretty useless. I get that they were telling some foundational aspects of the story, but a lot of them were just not necessary. That being said, I did really like the
. As well, the UI for viewing the notes was absolutely awful aesthetically.
-Puzzles: The solutions to most of the puzzles in Astray were painfully obvious, to the point where some almost felt tedious.
-Flashlight Batteries: I honestly believe this game would have been way better without ever needing to find flashlight batteries. I found myself on several occasions in a pitch black area of the game waiting for a few minutes in a corner for my flashlight battery to "recharge" enough for me to find the door I was supposed to go through. This really broke immersion for me and if I wasn't already intrigued by the story by that point, I would have quit the game and not looked back.
-Dynamite:
That was pretty annoying.
-Invisible Walls: For the most part, the game lets you roam pretty free around the environment - however, towards the end of the game, there were a few invisible walls I found infuriating. In these areas, I was left confused as the game didn't give me any indication of why the invisible walls existed, given that the locations of the invisible walls appeared to be the most logical routes to proceed through their respective areas in the game.
Though some areas of the game were confusing and annoying, they don't remove the fact that Astray is an interesting and fun game. Don't play Astray expecting an AAA-quality game, but If you like a indie horror game with a decent story, grab it when it's on sale and you'll probably be impressed.

Updated 1/30/2015
Keeps coming together every update. It is starting to have that excellent charm that I mention more so than before; and almost makes me feel like I am playing a spiritual successor to the old Rogue Spear series; which is great. In case you guys aren't as ancient as I am; Rogue Spear was a old Tactical FPS where you would go on missions to destroy, protect, survive, rescue, etc. This game shares some of those aspects with its more post-modern/sci-fi tactical style.
I can't wait to see it grow more. The Starcrown Aerospace mission is a cool stealth-based one, which is demonstrating the versatility of the gameplay options. Right now it seems to focus on android murdering, but I would imagine in the near future they will start incorporating live missions where you are sent to fight real enemies. Also, I have notice some performance optimizations in the game.
Original stuff:
So far this game seems to be going in a great direction. The ambitious developers have been updating in good iterations and the background is looking very excellent. This game is essentially a Science-Fiction FPS where you are a Marine that goes to.. space! Common theme right? Well, this game does it different. You aren't some Halo Spartan or Warhammer Space Marine. You aren't some overpowered super-armored exo-suit marine that has access to giant guns and can punch enemies through a wall. You are a ordinary soldier who is trained for elite operations in space and ground.
This game puts a nice emphasis on augmented reality technology, such as implementing a visor that indicates your objectives, ammo, used items, etc. This may compare to other Sci-fi Marine flicks, with the exception that it is in such a way where the technology IS apart of your helmet, and not some typical video game user interface. Take off the visor and you will notice there is nothing. No recticule, no ammo type, no indicators for equipment, no objective points, NOTHING. Just your gun and it's trustworthy Iron Sight.
Right now as of Early Access, there are several features players can experience. While it isn't near to completion yet, it definately shows progress and I feel like these Developers are NOT out to dissapoint anyone. One thing I would like to see with this game is a little more of a team-based orientation when playing in competitive matches. It seems like no one really sticks as a team and it becomes a solo-festival of shooting. I don't have a big problem with it, but I have a problem if teamplay isn't encouraged.
What really gets this game my thumbs up right now is the whole immersive experience. The Ambient sound effects while on board a space station with the lights out makes you feel like a real soldier sent to investigate a dead space station. The eerie sound of hostile robots and their locomotion has you glued to the iron sight to check all areas. The Helmet is on, the gun is loaded, the objectives are displayed and the flashlight is on. Ok, time to figure out how to proceed to the objective.
This game just seems so much in that realm, and I would love it to continue being so. I just hope not all the levels are going to consist of pitch-black environments with 100% flashlight usage. The game should demand all sorts of scenarios. I do like the darkness, but I want a balance of dark and light. Missions in places where facilities have power and missions where places have no power and it is dark. Balance is everything when it comes to mission consistency.
Things I expect and would like when the game goes gold:
1. Peak performance optimizations
2. Plentiful amount of multiplayer and singleplayer missions.
3. Adherence to realistic player movement and team-oriented gameplay.
4. Adherence to that immersive charm that I mentioned.
5. Variety of equipment and weapons.

One of the major complaints of people wjo played the originals was that every character kinda played the same. This time, the devs tried to add some depth to the gameplay by making character more unique. For example: Saberwulf is now a rushdown heavy character who haves a bad time dealing with projectiles, while Tusk is now a very slow but high damaging character; and some chars like Kan Ra and Glacius are kind of like Dhalsim from Street Fighter, that is: good at mid range pokes and setups. The most balanced all around char and the most suitable for beginners is Jago, who plays kinda like Ryu with his fireball and shoryuken zoning and also has the standard Killer Instinct combos.
The combo system seems to be kinda hard in the begining, but it’s actually pretty straightforward: you beging your combo with some special move, then you follow up with a regular attack (weak, medium or strong) and keep combining normal and special attacks until the combo gauge starts to reach the red line, then you perform a special attack with the heavy button to finish the combo. While taking damage, the opponent might guess which normal attacks you’re using as likers and the press the same buttons to perform a Ccccc-combo breaker. If he makes the wrong guess, he gets locked in the combo.
There is also an autocombo system, which allows you to mash buttons randomly and the CPU will perform the combos for you. But I strongly recommend you to turn off dat schit, cause you will never actually learn the game if you use it and also it will lead you nowhere online.

As for the visuals, the game looks pretty good, even in a crappy PC like mine. I liked the new look of characters like Saberwulf and Orchid, but the new look of T.J. Combo and Glacius are kinda off. Fortunately, the game has tons of customization features for you char, one of them being the “classic skin”, suited for oldtimers. Another good thing about the customizations in this game is that they can all be earned through playing the game.

I've been hype af for this game since it was first announced as a launch title for the Xbox One.  The original Killer Instinct (or the SNES port of it, anyway) was one of the fighting games I always played with my cousin every time we got to hang out together.  It was always a requirement.  So I SO was ready and willing to board the hype/nostalgia train and get into the new version.  Season one was given to me as a gift from my brother-in-law, and I later snagged season two when it was free on XBLG.  As such, I didn't have the season three characters.  Now that the game's finished, however, and Killer Instinct has FINALLY come to Steam (I wasn't about to update to Windows 10 just to play the PC port of KI 'cuz screw dat) with all the content unlocked (give or take the things you have to earn, anyway) for $40.  The only way I could be happier is if I finally got to play it with my cousin again, like old times.
Now:
Now that I've got the hype and nostalgia out of the way, the game lives up to, and surpasses all expectations.  Killer Instinct has always had a unique, and simplistic combo flowchart (or you can play Sadira and play the up, down game if your execution's good enough), so the game, generally speaking, isn't that difficult, executionally.  Emphasis on executionally.  The real difficulty of the game comes from getting into your opponent's head, and making the right reads.
Combo and Counter Breakers:
In the older games, all you needed to do a combo breaker was the required special move input at the right time, so combo breaking was fairly easy.  In this game, they added a healthy level of risk to them.  Here, you have to press two buttons of the same strength as the button your opponent is currently hitting you with, and in time, you can learn to recognize or predict them, though you'll mostly be guessing at first.  However, if you guess wrong, you'll get locked out for a short period of time, during which you'll take extra damage and can't try combo breaking again.  Another thing to keep in mind about the risk of combo breakers is once your opponent figures out when you're going to break their combo, they can perform a counter breaker.  If they guessed that you were going to break the combo, and you don't, it just ends their combo prematurely, but if they did guess right, they can start a new combo from that point, in addition to the one they were already doing.  The KV (knockdown value) meter gets reset and you have to take a second combo on top of the initial one, and the damage skyrockets.
Final Thoughs:
This game is all about footsies, and risk and reward. I'm not one to write reviews, but this game deserves it, especially considering all the negative attention it's been receiving lately. I can't tell you how many reviews I've seen with less than a day's worth of playtime complaining about features the user hasn't taken the time to learn. Let me start by addressing everyone's biggest issue: the idea that this game is "pay-to-win." From a glance, I had the same impression, but the game was enjoyable enough for me to push past that idea. If you are able to reach even just the scrap requirement for the week and sell that, it will net you nearly 200 credits. This is enough for about four blue (rare) items in the game, or to buy the workbench slots everyone has such a problem with. Buy fifteen of them - trust me, it's worth it.
Congratulations, now you can craft your own blues. You will find that this is much more profitable than selling your scrap in the long run. Using just the weekly amount of scrap, you can craft six blues. This will net you 273 credits, considering the cost for six discounted workbench slots, and assuming you sell all six of them. Hey, that's 73 more than last week. From here, the profits only increase more.
Assuming you saved up for a while, and now you've got one of your extra factions to level five, you can craft purples! Hoorah! "But the purple workbench slots cost so much.." I hear you saying. Assuming you sold your scrap the first week and sold blues the second, you should have enough. This is assuming you didn't go on a crazy spending spree. Remember how I told you that you can craft six "free" blues a week? Great, because purples take six blues to craft. All of a sudden, you're only on your third week and you've already got a purple. Now you can craft a new one every week, until it's time to renew your workbench slots (or you choose to join a new faction). Awesome! Time to join the seal club too, right?!
Wrong. Even if I slap the strongest purple weapon I have on a noob truck, I'm going to have way less armor than anyone in that tier. Potentially none, depending on how low you go. All it takes is one or two well placed shots from the beginner cannon and suddenly the guy with the purple is either dead or missing their gun. The powerscore system in the game does a pretty good job keeping people in the tier that they're supposed to be in, and balancing when they're not. There is no "seal club" unless you perceive it that way.
With all this being said, the game IS in fact a grind, but only as much as you'd like it to be. It's possible to gain the weekly scrap requirement with about an hour spent every day. Efficient leveling can be done at the same rate by making use of the daily XP bonus, gaining about a level a day. This is faster in the beginning levels, and slower towards late game. Even once you're crafting purples, there will be plenty of stuff to be saught after. This is a progression-based game. It's pay-to-progress, end of story. I can't buy any one (or ten) item(s) and by the power of my wallet be stronger than everyone else. That's not how this game works. If I have a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ op truck, everyone else in my game will have one too, assuming they aren't horrible at building.
Instead of crying about the game being pay to win after only nine hours of playing, give it a fair chance. Actually try to LEARN the game's mechanics and market. The game rewards those who learn it just as much as those who support the devs, if not more (You get the same **** for free!). To anyone who's hesitant to play the game because of the reviews, give it a shot and form your own opinion. Try following my advice, and if you enjoy the game, then great! If not, at least you tried it, and maybe it will give you some insight on the pay-to-progress system everyone is so against.
TL;DR - Game is pay-to-progress, not pay-to-win. Powerscore limits twink builds heavily. It's a grind, but no worse than most games. With just 3 weeks playing (roughly) an hour a day, you can start crafting purples. Give the game a chance.

This game is an amazing blend of MMORPG and Fighting game. I had not played any Dragon Ball games before this one, because they did not offer anything except playing as the main characters, and I already know this is far and away the best Dragon Ball game of all time. The controls are simple enough to pick up if you have never played fighting games before and there is much less of an emphasis on rythem in the playstyle than other games. I only have two complaints:
1) super saiyan is too powerful when an AI is allowed to be one for an entire fight. Yes, there are ways to stay super saiyan indefinitely in a fight, but what I am talking about is the NPC enemy comes into the fight as a super saiyan and then does not have to do anything to maintain their super saiyan state. So, they can infinitely spam ultra and super attacks. In a one on one setting, this is manageable. However, there are missions later in the game that require you to endure 3 super saiyans at once all by yourself. This is the part that is not fun to deal with.
2) The loot is too randomized. I understand that making some of the loot exclusively and randomly drop in missions gives an extra challenge to players who want to complete the collections. However, When it is possible to play the same mission for 5 hours straight (while completing it every 5 minutes) and not get the one item you need to complete a mission for a mentor (Vegeta *cough* cough*), then the loot collection phase of the game becomes considerably less fun. People can get the 7 dragonballs in a total of 2 hours on average, so more than 5 hours for one item means that there is something seriously wrong with the RNG for the loot in the game. In this one instance, it is too much like an MMORPG.
Perhaps if the loot unlocked at the stores if you got a certain rank on the missions, then this would be a simple fix to the problem, because players would still need to grind quests for money to buy the loot they want/need. Or maybe if getting certain ranks on the missions guranteed certain item drops, then this could solve the dilemma of having nothing to show for quest grinding after several hours.
All in all, I love the game. The story is interesting, the gameplay is phenomenal and easy to learn. And the hub world provides a wonderful environment to interact the game outside of a menu.
Pro tip: the game won't have that blindingly shiny look to it if you turn the game's brightness all the way down. I actually play with both my game and computer brightness as low as possible, but just the game's brightness being turned down got rid of the solar flare effect.

Probably about 30% of the time I tried to start the game I was forced to use Task Manager to force close the unresponsive loading screen. Servers never load. This is possibly the best Kart racer I have ever played.  Having grown up as a SEGA fanboy, this is the SEGA answer to Mario Kart that I always wanted and the PC version definitely gives Mario Kart 8 a run for its money! It's also a great livingroom PC/HTPC game, as it supports up to 4 players on a single screen (local splitscreen.)
The tracks are varied and well designed, with plenty of shortcuts and bonuses which reward skilled players.  Being a huge SEGA fan from back in the day, I really appreciated the call-backs and themes the levels offered (Golden Axe, Shinobi, Skies of Arcadia, and more!)
As far as difficulty is concerned, this game is no cakewalk.  There is a learning curve involved in teaching yourself how to drift, how to boost, and how to stack boosts in order to be competitive, but the game greatly rewards you for building your skill.  Beware: The A.I is absolutely cutthroat and they won't show you any mercy while you're still getting used to things.  While at first they seem to be absolutely unfair, they can be overcome with practice and skill as well as knowledge of the track.  They do not rubber-band to the player like Mario Kart's opponents do in older entries.  There are items which you can use to attack/sabotage other drivers just like in Mario Kart, however they play less of an important role in SASRT, as you will not find yourself getting item-spammed at inopportune times if you're good enough to get ahead of the pack.
The tracks themselves can change lap-to-lap and new situations may require a new type of vehicle.  That's where the "transformed" part of the game's name comes in.  Each vehicle is capable of transforming from a car to a boat to a plane and back again, depending on the level's terrain.  The transformations are automatic (so you don't have to worry about having the wrong vehicle type at the wrong time) and they add a great variety to the overall gameplay.  There is a learning curve involved in learning the different handling of each vehicle type (especially the planes), but they are not difficult to get a hang of.
Each character has unique stats and abilities and they can be leveled up through racing and completing events/challenges.  When leveling up, you can unlock 'mods' which drastically alter your character's stats and can be helpful on certain courses (for example, the handling mod will boost cart handling and can help on an icy stage with lots of turns.)
Another huge advantage that this game has over Mario Kart is its Single Player campaign.  While Mario Kart only really offers a Grand Prix and Time Trial mode for its single player experience, SASRT offers both of those plus a "World Tour" mode in which players must complete a wide variety of events (races, drift challenges, boost challenges, combat race challenges, etc) to earn stars which can be used to unlock additional characters as well as stat/kart upgrades.  If you want, you can even play local multiplayer in World Tour mode (up to 4 players) and everyone can take on the challenge simultaneously. I found that I got a good 30 hours of gameplay out of World Tour so far and I haven't even 100% finished it yet; there's lots of content to be had!
I highly recommend this game to any fans of racers, Sonic, and SEGA franchises of old.  You won't find a better Mario Kart alternative on PC (short of emulation.)

I am going to attempt to explain why folks believe this game is pay-to-win, and why it truly is not.  I currently have over 300 hours invested according to Steam.  I believe this can be some kind of indicator that I have played enough to truly understand this game and I hope that some of you will disregard these filthy reviews this game is getting and go ahead and give it a try.
First and foremost, you cannot truly buy an advantage over other players.  Every item in this game has a power score.  If you simply pay real money and slap the best equipment on your car, your power score will go up and you will be fighting against other players with a similar power score.  You simply can’t buy the best stuff and then go destroy noob players with it.
Second, as a starting player you are able to acquire "Scrap" from completing starter raids and winning in PVP battles.  The game allows you to collect 2800 of these per week.  This cap is good in my opinion, as it helps keep the market stable.  Scrap is used to craft weapons and other items in the game.  When you eventually build a car over the 3000 power score, you can then start obtaining "Wire" each week as well.  Eventually when you get over 4000 power score, you can then collect "Electronics."  You are allowed to collect 2800 per week for each resource.
With that said, the scrap alone sells for about 67.00 coins per 1000.  That is just under 200 coins per week from the scrap alone.  Wire is currently selling for about 90 coins for 1000, which would be just under 300 coins per week from selling the wire.  And electronics are selling for about the same price as wire.
What I am getting at, is that as a new player you should sell the items you farm for.  If you play even somewhat regularly you can net over 500 coins per week from the resources alone.  All rare items sell for about 50 coins, and the epic items sell for about 400.  Getting good gear in this game is very obtainable without throwing money at the game.
Now for selling items, here is the thing that most new players do not understand and could cost them a great deal of coins.  In your storage inventory, you have the option to simply right click a piece of equipment and select "Sell".  This will sell the item to a player whom has placed a buy order.  It is more effective to select the "Trade" option and then place the item on the broker for your desired price instead of just selling it quickly to the highest bidder.  You will make a lot more money this way.
For anyone considering this game, please do not take all these negative reviews to heart.  Most of these players have very few hours recorded and thus, do not truly understand the game.  This game is great in every aspect and the building of your own craft is very unique and appealing to most.  You can pay to progress faster, however again, you will be playing against others with similar power scores.
Definitely a fun little game.  I've only played it through once, but he did a great job on it.  Looking forward to more.

If you want something to play that'll pass the time or crave a game with the classic RPG feeling to it, then Hero Siege is the perfect game for you. It's, in my opinion, a fantastic little gem of a game. Gameplay wise it feels as though the developer stuffed Diablo’s more reserved brother into a blender with The Binding of Issac, and added in a pinch of Killing Floor for good measure. In more sensible terms, it’s got a great number of rogue-like and RPG elements to it. There are a number of different levels, ranging from forests to snowy tundras, deserts and many more. At the end of each of these levels you can collect random pieces of loot, or relics as they’re called, which grant you varying stats and abilities. These relics come in four different flavours; weapon enhancing ones, which, as the name suggests, enhances your weapon giving it extra powers. For example an item called the Basilisk's Tooth makes it so that you have a 2% chance to turn enemies to stone. There are also passive relics as well, which improve your character’s skills. One example is the Cactus, which periodically spawns a cactus on the nearest enemy. The third relic type is active, which, after pressing the use key, will activate the effect of the relic. The Candy Crusher, one example of an active relic, launches candy in a ring around the player that explodes on landing. And the last relic type is orbiting, which float around the player and help during fights. One example is the Almighty Fedora which rapidly shoots projectiles.
All these and many more can be obtained by progressing through the game, and surviving the large waves of enemies the game throws at you.
Talking about enemies, there are a large number of different types. Ranging from axe throwing skeletons to towering yeti-like beasts. Also there are several “elite” type enemies that have particular skills that happen once they die. For example creating a large laser that spins in a circle or an X shaped explosion, which both appear where the “elite” was slain.
There are also a number of RPG elements in the game too. For one, there are unique skill trees for each class, providing varying passive and active abilities, depending on which class you choose out of the possible seven, or ten (depending on whether you own the DLC). They also all have their own sort of personalities and quotes as well.
Graphically the game looks a lot like your typical indie, rogue-like affair. But it fits nicely. The characters are easily distinguishable from each other and the varying levels all look pixel pretty with their individual themes and settings.
Overall the game feels enjoyable to play. The classes and their skills vary enough for the game to be replayed time and time again. Not to mention the seemingly endless number of experience levels you can rack up on a single class. The enemies vary in difficultly, depending on the level, and the boss battles, for the most part, feel fairly satisfying once they eventually kick the bucket.
To Conclude, I’d say that Hero Siege is worth a play, whether it’s a rogue-like or an RPG you're after, or just a quick bit of fun. It’s a satisfying game to play and well worth a go. Good Day!

EvE Online is an interesting and truly unique MMO. With it's passive skill system, the game moves away from the need to always be online and always be working towards a goal. Anything on a schedule beyond simply updating your skill queue is something you decide on investing in or not.
Since it's originaly incarnation in 2004, the game has improved steadily. From moving to DirectX9 and retiring it's old DirectX8 engine (with rumors of DX11 and tesselation coming in the future), to improvements in tutorials and reacting to player feedback, CCP proves they are willing to work with the game on the notion that it's shared by the playerbase.
All ships in EvE Online tend to have a role that the ship excels at. In one case you may have a frigate that you'd assume to be not worth your time, but they serve a vital role in fleet fights and have numerous advantages over bigger, heavier ships.
EvE Online does require a monthly fee, but it is possible, if you get yourself established well enough, to pay for your subscription by buying in-game representations of 30-days for your account. However, like all items in EvE, they are subject to scams, thefts, destruction and so on which means that you'll have to be on your toes when dealing with trades and transport.
EvE Online is hands-down my favorite MMO. Others have tried, but none have come close to the sense that you, as the player, get to carve out not only what's going on in the universe, but what your place is in it.

Ignoring the obvious main reason as to why people decide to buy this game ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°), there's some really solid beat 'em up gameplay here that I really enjoyed. The story is pretty good, I was actively interested through my playthrough of it and was suprised to see some pretty emotional moments. All 22 characters in this game have interesting personalities as well as unique fighting styles, and it was very enjoyable learning how to play all of them. There's a fair amount of content in this game to sink your teeth into, taking me about 35 hours to get all the achivements and 100% it. The music is also excellent.
My one complaint would be the content other than the main story can get pretty boring, however it isn't a major issue as you could only play the main story and still get around 28 hours from this game. Something I also want to mention is that playing with a keyboard and mouse is significantly less fun than playing with a controller. I spent hours changing the keyboard and mouse controls and getting used to them, but I still couldn't stand them. TLDR;  This is an amazing game worth every penny.  This is a must buy game.
This is a colony building game where you manage a colony of people you gather through various means to survive until one of a few things happens.  Either you build a ship and escape the planet via research, somehow manage to travel from one end ot the planet to the other to a ship that is already built to escape, or you die.  These are the game's end goals for a win condition.
So you start with whatever number of folks you set in your scenario (or you choose the default scenarios and go from there) and land on the planet.  You can prioritize how different colonists will perform work using either some weird♥♥♥♥♥check system, or (and my preferred method) using a scale from 1-4, 1 being the highest priority, and 4 being lowest.  You can leave the specific task blank to have the colonist not actually do a certain task.
Generally speaking you will build a base, make bedrooms/workshops/a freezer to ensure you can get work done to make money and items you will need to survive.  Over time you will encounter various issues where you'll use various weapons or technologies to thwart whatever comes your way.  Got a bunch of jerks wanting to raid your base, but they arent going to attach immediatly?  No problem!  MORTARS AWAY! Got raiders coming to kill you immediatly?  No problem, Improvised Turrets (if you have them) and use guns to solve your problems.  Are the enemy too strong?  Well shoot, now you're dead. Time to restart!
The best thing about this game is you can set up where you set up shop (temperate forest for easier time growing food/not too harsh temperatures, deserts if you're all like screw growing crap, meat all the way, frozen tundras because you hate yourself).  You can also set difficulties based on actual difficulty, and also choose a storyteller.  Cassandra Classic makes the situations get harder and harder as time goes on and will NOT be as easy as say Phoebe Chillax.  Both storytellers will follow the same general line of difficulty curve, just one goes through the curve faster vs. the other takes it slower.  Then there is Randy Random, who will send whatever he feels like whenever he pleases.  Because reasons.
But seriously, this is an amazing game with tons of depth, customization on automating tasks, plenty of obstacles to get in your way, and many playstyles to take up based on preference.  I tend to play Phoebe Chillax and build my base to withstand giant raids, and then take my time getting a ship built.  I know others out there really dig the somewhat new caravan system where you try and wander the planet to a ship to get you out.
Get this game.  It's so worth the money for the replayability.  Oh, and I forgot one thing...There are mods to this game.  I play vanilla, but I hear mods are pretty swell!

Borderlands is the cult classic loot shooter, where the main goal is to kill stuff and collect guns and guns and even more guns.
Borderlands takes place on a planet of Pandora where danger lurks around every corner, we play as the vault hunters who came to Pandora seeking a vault, a place that contains fortunes. You can pick from four different characters Brick, Roland, Lilith and Mordecai
The game is an RPG infused FPS. You run around killing stuff and looting chest for better equipment. The game is very fun and getting better equipment is also incredibly fun. The four characters you choose from have different abilities. Brick has berserk mode where he punches stuff and in rage mode regains health, Mordecai releases his pet Bloodwing which is a one hit kill on a random enemy in the battlefield or damages bosses, Roland puts down a turret which kills anything it sees and Lilith goes into phaselock mode where she goes invisible and after that releases a shockwave which kills or damages anyone around them. Each character is awesome but it's best to use the one to suit your play style the best.
Graphics are awesome. The cell shaded look is awesome and even though some of the textures are mediocre this game is very appealing. The environments are very bland since all of them are deserts. I'm still very glad that the change from realistic to cell shaded happened.
Audio is mediocre, I like some of the soundtrack but overall it's very bland. The gun sounds are awesome and everything but a lot of it is re used and some of the sound effects are quite bad.  Overall very mediocre sound design
The game can get quite tough at certain points, some of the enemies are higher levels than you and will kill you in seconds. Your best option is to do every side quest to level so the later sections in the game aren't as tough.
Level design is alright for the most part but some of the maps in the later sections of the game get really confusing. Overall it's okay for the most part.
The main game itself took me 18 hours to complete everything with every side quest, with all the dlc it took me around 30 hours. The game also has tons of replay value, you can play Ultimate Vault Hunter and True Hunter which are more difficult versions of the game and you can also try the different characters and not to mention you can always play the game with friends which is a lot of fun.
The game has one big problem. It's incredibly buggy. I've had many problems playing the game and DLC and constantly look for solutions to the problems I was having. Some of the issues were quests not showing up, I couldn't turn in quests. get stuck in the environments and fall through the levels. Overall there's nothing too game breaking and with enough time you could find a fix for the problems.
Borderlands is a must play for everyone. To date this is one of my favorite games of all time. This game is incredibly fun and funny too. This is incredibly fun game and even despite the issues this is a must play for everyone. My suggestion is get the main game and skip the DLC's cause they're not very good but if you want more then sure go ahead and buy it but I suggest saving your money for Borderlands 2. This is a must play for everyone. I give Borderlands a 9/10

EVE Online is an MMO for those who like number crunching - and complexity. The learning curve is extremely steep - as you customize your spaceship right down to CPU and Power consumption and only get to even hit a target in space - if you abide by the 'optimal range' of your currently equipped weapon (yes different weapons have different ranges) - and yes - it makes a difference whether you are trying to hit your opponent while moving or while sitting ducks. Eve Online sports an incredible open world - where combat is not your only destiny. There are several ways to get by in the universe, whether it is through trading, hauling (the transport of items between systems), mining or combat. Highly addictive, but again - highly complex!

Astray is one of those games I think would have been better without an actual monster chasing after you and killing you. Those sections where you were more or less forced to interact with the monster felt not very frightening at first, and after that it just felt like a chore.

Killer Instinct finally makes its way to the PC where it belongs...STEAM!
Single player wise, there is also a boat load of content available and those that don't want to play multiplayer can occupy themselves with Shadow Lords mode or even just a normal arcade mode against the PC. What makes KI truely exceptional for me is that fact that the game has a feature called "Combo Assist" which you can enable. If you're struggling to execute combos in fighting games (like I do) then this feature is awesome. Okay, some people or hardcore KI players do frown upon those that do use it, but trust me, there is nothing more satisfying than executing a combo in style and feel like a bad♥♥♥♥♥at the same time without needing to have the muscle memory of a super computer.
Multiplayer is a pleasant experience. The netcode is exceptionally good and the fact that you can crossplay with people on xbox one and Win 10 makes it bonus (excluding ranked matches though). Just to give you an idea of how good the netcode is, I live in South Africa and all matches that I've played have been smooth as a baby's bottom. The game also doesn't require a super computer to run and is optimized. If you love fighting games and want to support developers who bring their fighting games to PC, then buy KI, immediately.
Trust me, you won't be disappointed!

This review is based on online co-op (I have not bothered with single player).

The bugs I mentioned before are Relic pickup glitches and even sometimes items/relics lost upon reloading (rare but has occured with 2 friends of mine) which is enough to make any gamer rage. The most frustratng was figuring out how to connect with friends online.  The dedicated servers and even peer-to-peer are inconsistent for visibility of friends games in the lobby.
TL;DR
The game itself is probably worth it for the $6 price tag, but DO NOT expect a smooth online experience until (if ever) the bugs/crashes have been fixed.  If you do choose to gamble on this game, the only reliable solution (from my experience) to connecting with friends is for the host to forward port 5610 and having your friends "Connect to IP"

For the most part, it's F2P, but progress is a bit slow and cash-weapons are good, expensive and hard to get with grinding.
The game however is a lot of fun, there are different tactics and loadouts for a constant challenge.
What I like is that the PVP part is quite quick (3 minute matches) and PVE has different missions with specific rewards, mostly resources. You will have to play some PVP to get required items, so PVE-only is not working well.
The crafting system is not very logical and jobs are expensive, but you can buy most stuff in the market.
Resources that you can obtain are cap'ed per week, but this is usually not a big deal since hitting the max with higher level resources takes some time. There are daily login rewards and a refill of your fuel needed for special missions.
Levelling up takes a lot of XP later on, and will keep you busy for some time. Every level gained gives you some parts from the active factions (5 for now), and there is a co-pilot that has some perks from every faction that levels up with you.
So thumbs up, try it for yourself, and if you made it to level 10, start getting high level resources.

I can say this is the most entertaining game I've played in 15 years, hands down. The last games that hooked me so were Diablo and Civilization--much different genres but similar levels of addictiveness and immersion.
So my current colony is doing well. It is almost entirely self-sufficient, well protected by thick stone walls, and earns tons of silver by producing and selling huge quantities of hard drugs to other colonies. One of my colonists is Ronen, a sentient bi-pedal fox who loves crafting and loves her minigun. But she also loves alcohol, ambrosia, and cocaine; she has a "massive addiction" to each of the three. This has lead her to develop aggressively spreading carcinomas in her kidneys and life-threatening liver cirrhosis. I tried to rehabilitate Ronen. Weaning off to sobriety. But even with massive quantities of methadone to ease the withdrawals, she still flew into an unquenchable rage and senselessly eviscerated the colony cook with her minigun right where he stood in the walk-in freezer.
I made a difficult but necessary choice: the colony has begun harvesting kidneys and livers from captured pirate and tribal raiders and stockpiling them. Now Ronen need not halt her addiction at all; she can keep drinking her booze and huffing her lines as much as she'd like, and when the cirrhosis and carcinomas return, Donkey the doctor simply replaces Ronen's fouled organs with fresh ones from the organ stockpile.
10/10 would shamelessly enable sentient minigun-toting cokehead foxes via organ harvests again.

RimWorld
What is it?
RimWorld is a 2D top-down stragegy colony simulator where you control your colonists and well...make a colony :D, with the ultimate goal of escaping your planet.
Big Features and Selling Points.
-Good performance on low-end machines (i5 3230 and 730M lol)
-Every playthrough is different due to the fact that everything is randomized, as in: The World is completely random with the possibility of setting a seed, all colonists are completely random (Names, Skills, Injuries and relationships with other colonists), you can pick any of the 9001 bamboozilion tiles avaiable on the world and start your colony there (tiles can have different biomes, temperatures, texture and land, resources and even structures as of A17)
-Long and if you want to infinite game-length (because you don't have to win, you can stay and survive forever.)
-Low and easy difficulties for filthy casuals up to INSANE DIFFICULTIES FOR PEOPLE WHO THINK MR.TORGUE IS LAME (BL2 reference)
-You can make the base of your dreams which can also be self-sustainable, or make a hell on your planet.
-You can put two cannibals together in a room and watch which one kills the other first (what else do you want lol)
Positives:
-Workshop integration allows for hundreds of mods to be installed and played with (I recommend Ultimate Survial Mod, EDB Prepare Carefully, Mending, Psychology and therapy, Stuff that just make the game better lol)
-You can survive on a Ice Sheet or burn in a dessert burning at 70-120 celsius.
-Infinite replayability makes this game worth the price
-The game seems to get constant updates and is generally feature rich
Negatives
-The games "storyteller" AI is pretty cruel sometimes sending you events with which you cant deal with
-In the EULA (Yes I read it, I know I'm weird) the dev states that he can stop developing the game at any time for any reason which is quite a jerk move
-Some features are still sort of stupid and somewhat unfinished (Maybe make Planet Killer event into a Tile Killer?)
-You will easily lose yourself while playing this resulting in no sleep at all (I once checked the time and realized I played for 13 hours straight wtf but I guess that's kinda personal)
Neutral rant
-this game kinda relies on mods but considering it has great support of them then it's fine.
-It is quite expensive for just 50MB of content lol
-I have a "Life" so I don't have enough time to play too much of it.
Rating?
Graphics: 9/10 -they are pixel art but they are always descriptive enough, but some need changing
Performance: 8/10 -if you have a massive colony IT WILL DESTROY YOUR CPU (not really but it will take a lot of it)
Gameplay: 7/10 - 9/10 but -2 because the AI is sometimes COMPLETELY ♥♥♥♥ING ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FOR ♥♥♥♥S SAKE DAMMIT and let's itself get killed often.
Overall: 80% (Subject to change this game is in early access)

I had bought this game many versions ago while still in Early Acsess, which the game still does remain under that title as of writing this review. I had played similar games such as Prison Architect, but never enjoyed that game as much as I do enjoy Rimworld.

My hours are inflated due to frequent AFK's, but I'd peg my hours around 350. This game is amazing. I'd call it probably the closest spiritual successor to Dwarf fortress, that despite lacking the multiple z-levels, has all of the "fun" that DF promises. The creators are updating constantly with new stuff like Caravans, Quests, and the ability to have more than one settlement (if your computer can handle it). The modding community is vibrant and allows you to transform this game into a lovecraftian tale, a technocratic paradise, or cannabalistic dictatorship.
Of course, the game is still in Early Access which means it's always evolving and considered "unfinished." That being said, this game is more complete than some full releases you will see in the Steam catalogue. The devs make significant updates every few months which will blow up your mods for a period of time. But I encourage playing the vanilla game at least once to completion to appreciate the original intent of the game. I do not have bugs occur very often, I honestly struggle to think of one at this time.
When you start up, you can either choose to read up guides or go in blind, whatever style floats your boat. But remember that losing is part of the fun - the community actively shares the tales of their triumphs and tragedies:
-I had my first major colony collapse because all of my huskies became raging alcoholics who vomited everywhere and wouldn't fight or haul. The colonists died to a raid, and the dogs lived out the last of their days getting rip roaring drunk.
-I operated on an individual to give them bionic arms, legs, spine, and organs. During fights he was a flash on the battlefield who could annhilate an army alone without a scratch. He died from a javelin in the head because I forgot to make everyone helmets. His wife went insane with grief, drugged herself  into a stupor, and ended up in the hospital. Nobody else was trained for combat at his level besides his wife. We died to a mob of wolves, his wife being torn apart in her hospital bed.
-After seasons of trying to create a respectable colony selling poorly crafted clothing, I moved to becoming drug kingpins. I started mass producing drugs, selling them for massive profits, outfitting every colonist with guns and advanced bionics. Walls could be built in an instant, one individual punched a scyther to death, massive raids would die before even hitting my kill box. I turned the colony into a depot, taking in new refugees daily and sending periodic ships of colonists to space. It only ended after a developer update that added the caravans.
Anyway, if you're still reading, just buy the game. It's worth the 30$ regardless of how you play because of the multiple "storytellers" that randomly choose events of varying threat levels. You can play on base building mode with minimal threats, or back breaking hard mode. It's your rimworld, your rules. Don't let your dreams be dreams, just do it!

She's a harsh mistress, EVE. If you're cocky, or careless, she'll put you on your knees and keep you there. But the rewards are equally severe. To some it's a nightmare, to others it's a second life. Amidst the miners, traders, pirates, captains of industry, loyal servants of the state, pioneers and explorers, you'll find your place.
EVE is an investment, and for a long time it can seem like that it won't pay off, it's not a simple, instant-gratification game. Although the old tired line of "being whoever you want" and "do whatever you want" gets tossed around a lot with MMOs, open-world games and other similar genres, it does ring true to an extent. You can do what you want within the boundary of the game, but guaranteed you will rub up against people who are doing what they want. As I mentioned previously, EVE is a harsh mistress. You may think your simple mining vessel isn't a threat to anyone, and maybe it isn't. But there will be somebody out there who will see you as a target, encroaching on their territory, or their resources, or just see you as a fat juicy killmail.
It requires a lot of work, but the rewards in the long-run are fulfilling. When you spend those weeks, training skills, piloting small ships, mining and making scraps, only to finally step into your new battleship, or mining vessel - there's no feeling quite like it.
And it's not easy to let go of, either. I've played seperately over 5 different periods since I first entered the world of EVE 7 years ago, and while to some I am nothing but a whelp in terms of power, skills, finances, or reach, I feel I have come a long way. I have my place in the EVE Universe, and it is forever changing.
It's not for everyone, but for those who do find the pull to jump and seek our their destiny amongst the stars - you're in for a treat.

Okay, so this is an easy one: It's LEGO. And it's The Lord of the Rings. TOGETHER. There's no possible way this could go wrong, right?
Indeed!
Before anything I'd like to admit this is not my first playthrough of this game. I've beaten it on the alternative (AKA Torrent download) version but - hey - I did bought it after all, it actually deserved it.
It's basically a LEGO "action-rpg" (more action, less rpg) experience around Middle Earth, following the story of the Lord of the Rings movie trilogy but also containing some neat candy for those lore-freaks (oops) like the stone trolls and the troll hoard - for example.
The gameplay is that expected from a LEGO game: puzzles, basic combat, more puzzles, a lot of stuff to collect. It's not the gameplay that makes this game shine, tho. It's the around an hour and a half (plus mid-mission scenes) of rendered cutscenes full of the purest strain of Lord of The Rings Awesomeness.
Seriously, they're worthy every nickel you could spend on this game.
Not only they were smart enough to use the original movie dialogue for all the scenes brilliantly but they also managed to recapture the magic of Peter Jackson's trilogy and twist it into their own LEGO style. They're amazing and I can't describe them well enough - just buy it and see it yourself!
Full of nice and fun moments, good jokes - some even going into the world of inside jokes and internet memes (They're taking the Hobbits to Isengard!) - and, well, LEGO and LOTR together - I dare say that this is the best single-player Lord of the Rings yet.
And I mean it!

0) Maximize the connection points on your robot to decrease its Crit points

This game was pretty awesome! I'm not much of a "hardcore" puzzle solver, but the difficulty of this one is perfect for beginners.
Story: You try to find out what happened to your uncle, who opened up a museum, and the backstory is revealed by notes scattered around in the museum. It's a combination of detective work and horror.
Graphics: There's a lot I can describe about the graphics, as they captured the feel of a museum and theme. It's a combination of mystery and horror.
-Inside the museum:- I love the theme of the museum they were going for. It gave more of a mystery atmosphere. However, other than the rooms and anubis statue, it could have had more going for it. It feels like it's just mostly offices and hallways.
-Demonology room:- The demonology room was slightly bland, but I have to give props on the rune designs as they were gorgeous. Those gave more of a "mage" atmosphere than demonology. The walls and floors were mostly stone and bones, which was good, but there is more to demonology than just that.
-Atlantis room:- Oh my god this room design was to die for! It felt like you were in an underwater temple! I loved the wall and floor designs on this. I wish there was more on this. I would enjoy just walking around and exploring more in this atmosphere!
-Egypt room:- It seems like the same materials use from the demonology room. I do like the heiroglyphics, scarabs, and vases, but I feel there could be more. When I think of Egypt, usually sand comes to mind. I know they were going for a "scary" egyptian feel, but there are other ways to do that.
Gameplay: The gameplay has a sort of "Amnesia: Dark Descent" feel, but it's only because there are things to avoid and not to shine the light on. Don't worry, it's not as scary as that game. I promise. The game does have an item system, but it's just picking up items and placing them. There is no inventory. The only thing you should be concerned about is your flashlight in order just to see dark areas. It's more straightforward in most cases, which I have to say I like. I hate it when there are too many items in games and you either have to use them for weird reasons or do weird combinations.
Controls: The game is very, very vague on controls and customization. First off to point out, each time you start the game, the gamma option comes up and you have to adjust it, which is annoying. Second, not much of audio options, but I have to say if you have headphones, it will work automatically. For gameplay, while the game tells you about the flashlight and running, it does not tell you that you can throw items by right clicking(left clicking if you're left handed), which is very important to the dynamite part.
Overall: Overall, Astray is a small game that deserves recongnition, and a good first game for puzzle/mystery beginners. It has a pretty good blend of mystery and horror. I find it's hard to find games that balance mystery and horror well, and this one nailed it. The story and puzzles kept me engaged and made me want to play the game until the end.And this game is worth the play in both story, graphics, and atmosphere.

The game certainly has potential, but the same can be said about a lot of titles that have not delivered what was promised.  While graphically pleasing, the game currently lacks what I consider to be any decent gameplay.  Multiplayer death matches are pretty much all you have to look forward to if you buy this game which is *not* worth the money in my opinion.  With these things in mind I will point out the pros and cons of this game as best as I see them.
Pros:
(The graphics are more than I expected and makes the game look quite believeable.
(Weapon performance is surprsingly good, with the sounds and recoil reminding me of actual rifles I have fired.
(The heads up display mixed with the toggle modes on the helmet makes me feel like my head is actually in the helmet, which reminds me somewhat of the metro series.  This is a great immersion modifier.
(The dynamic weather system the have in the arena is very well done and they demonstrate that they can develope immersive environments within their game.
Cons:
(While the devs have multiple "gamemodes", all of them occur within an enclosed arena which, for me, gets dull really fast.  Again, the lack of gameplay variety just ruins this for me.
(Next to no visible progress on this game.  I understand the time it takes to develope such things but their updates  are both irregular and sparse.  I see no indication that this game is going anywhere fast.
(Lack of player customization leaves me feeling like a stormtrooper with no identity.  This breaks the immersion greatly in my mind.
Overall I'd say that this game has the barebones framework that can be the foundation of something awesome, but sadly I don't believe it will be.  As I said, I see no noteworthy progress on the game and with that fact alone, I don't reccomend buying this game.

So I've followed this title on the top-seller list on
for a loooong time. Now that it's on
I had to see what all the fuss was about.
---
By 'fringe' I suppose I am loosely referring to games that get lots of knee-slap laughs and are quick and relatively lite. There is a even an option in-game to play with
viewers interaction. I was also surprised to find that this title is only single player.
There is a small but digestible skill tree of upgrades you choose from between each wave. You can get things like a jetpack, a fire sword, the ability to kick, more energy, etc. The choices are small, but they are potent which is all that matters. There are bosses and slightly different level layouts. The controls are fun and work well. Another interesting aspect is that there are robot commentators that say all kinds of semi-random and fun stuff that keep it fresh. This part probably did well with the streamers.
Well, overall I found it enjoyable. I definitely see the appeal and will keep it, for sure. It's definitely something you play in short bursts. For instance, I've played for a mere 30-40 minutes before writing this, and that felt like a long time. That was over probably 6 play sessions. I enjoyed them all, but tire quickly after a burst.
The one thing that I have to say is that it probably isn't worth $15. Yeah, it is well done and it is
, but I think a $10 tag would sit better with me. I think the content is kind of slim for $15. The skill tree is quite limited, and the combat is relatively simple. There is no controller support, either.
+It is fun. In fact, I think the trailer doesn't capture it well enough. You have to try this to actually
the draw (or at least I did).
+While there isn't much content, what is there is high quality. For example the skill tree is small, but the choices all make for interesting strategies and all change how you play the game.
+Controls are good.
+Robot commentators are both funny and a nice addition. Interesting and novel idea for this kind of game.
-While it is well done, I think the price point is a tad high for the content offered. I think I'd like to see a bigger skill tree, different kinds of playable robots, and controller support.
If you find yourself on the fence, I bet you'd be glad you picked it up.

Astray is a fairly compact first-person horror experience, but it's worth every minute. While not without its issues, Astray does a nice job of tying several different histories with mysticism linked to them under one roof, and provides just enough menace to put the player off ease.
The story premise for Astray is a bit odd, at least to me. Thanks for the museum where a bunch of people died, dad? Grandpa? Uncle? Whatever? Reasons for being there aside, there's plenty to do in said museum, and enough scenery changes to keep it from being boring.
There are some menacing bipeds to avoid from time to time, but for the most part, they're not particularly threatening. It's fairly easy to learn their movement patterns and time your progress to avoid them entirely, and the bits where you are forced into closer quarters with them, your panicked evasion sprints aren't overly obstructed or ill-pathed. How they fit into the plot isn't entirely clear, as the story's a bit jumbled until the last few sections explaining what's behind all the weirdness.
My one big issue with the game is the final battle, which can be incredibly frustrating. Margin for error is very slim, and it will likely take you a few attempts to work out the optimal path and consistently deliver on it. Be ready to yell a lot, especially when the rest of the game has been combat- and mostly conflict-free. They don't hand you a weapon out of nowhere or anything, but it's definitely something of a fight.
Unforgiving finish aside, Astray is solid. Narrative could've been a bit tighter, but I wasn't disappointed overall. Play it.

Been a Borderlands fan since the beginning in 2009, and this is a great addition to the Borderlands universe. If you enjoyed Borderlands, Borderlands 2 and the Pre-Sequel, you need to get this! Great job Telltale!

Borderlands is the cult classic loot shooter, where the main goal is to kill stuff and collect guns and guns and even more guns.
Borderlands takes place on a planet of Pandora where danger lurks around every corner, we play as the vault hunters who came to Pandora seeking a vault, a place that contains fortunes. You can pick from four different characters Brick, Roland, Lilith and Mordecai
The game is an RPG infused FPS. You run around killing stuff and looting chest for better equipment. The game is very fun and getting better equipment is also incredibly fun. The four characters you choose from have different abilities. Brick has berserk mode where he punches stuff and in rage mode regains health, Mordecai releases his pet Bloodwing which is a one hit kill on a random enemy in the battlefield or damages bosses, Roland puts down a turret which kills anything it sees and Lilith goes into phaselock mode where she goes invisible and after that releases a shockwave which kills or damages anyone around them. Each character is awesome but it's best to use the one to suit your play style the best.
Graphics are awesome. The cell shaded look is awesome and even though some of the textures are mediocre this game is very appealing. The environments are very bland since all of them are deserts. I'm still very glad that the change from realistic to cell shaded happened.
Audio is mediocre, I like some of the soundtrack but overall it's very bland. The gun sounds are awesome and everything but a lot of it is re used and some of the sound effects are quite bad.  Overall very mediocre sound design
The game can get quite tough at certain points, some of the enemies are higher levels than you and will kill you in seconds. Your best option is to do every side quest to level so the later sections in the game aren't as tough.
Level design is alright for the most part but some of the maps in the later sections of the game get really confusing. Overall it's okay for the most part.
The main game itself took me 18 hours to complete everything with every side quest, with all the dlc it took me around 30 hours. The game also has tons of replay value, you can play Ultimate Vault Hunter and True Hunter which are more difficult versions of the game and you can also try the different characters and not to mention you can always play the game with friends which is a lot of fun.
The game has one big problem. It's incredibly buggy. I've had many problems playing the game and DLC and constantly look for solutions to the problems I was having. Some of the issues were quests not showing up, I couldn't turn in quests. get stuck in the environments and fall through the levels. Overall there's nothing too game breaking and with enough time you could find a fix for the problems.
Borderlands is a must play for everyone. To date this is one of my favorite games of all time. This game is incredibly fun and funny too. This is incredibly fun game and even despite the issues this is a must play for everyone. My suggestion is get the main game and skip the DLC's cause they're not very good but if you want more then sure go ahead and buy it but I suggest saving your money for Borderlands 2. This is a must play for everyone. I give Borderlands a 9/10

(Would like to start by stating that this is a review from the perspective of someone who is not exactly into traditional fighting games, this is more in hope of getting other people not into them to get this game)
What's that? You suck at regular one on one fighting games and its hard for you to both focus on doing combos and doing special moves?
Killer instinct has an amazing mechanic that makes it so much more accesible than many similar fighting games, and its automatic combos.
Now, don't you go think its just a "press to win" type of deal, hell no. Lemme explain.
The automatic combo system works as follow, upon mashing light, medium or heavy attack buttons, you automatically perform a combo of this type of attack as if it was a beat-em-up. But what keeps things interesting, is that to initiate combos and break defenses or combos, you still need to go with special inputs and proper timings, thus requiring a certain ammount of skill regardless.
And veteran players of classic killer instinct titles or fighting games in general will not have to worry as the auto combo system can easily be disabled so they can have much more controls over their combos and inputs.
Gameplay wise, KI is surprisingly fun, welcoming for new players and packed with a♥♥♥♥♥♥ton of content for people to play around.
Now that we got out of the way, can we talk about the art and sound design of this game?
Sure, the game does not have netherrealm quality polycount and cinematics, but the game still looks absolutely amazing thanks to its art direction and great characters and backgrounds designs. The sound design makes basic moves feels absolutely brutal to use (so you can imagine how it goes when you do ultra combos and special moves).
And then there's the music. The music alone was part of the reason this game got my attention. Mick Gordon and the crew did an absolutely amazing job with it and it might be imo his best work even out-doing doom 4. Some track might feel a bit underwhelming but trust me there's gonna be one you will want to take this stage for it alone.
So killer instinct the best fighting game ever? Couldn't tell, i don't feel exactly qualified to compare this to other fighting games.
Do i recommend it? Absolutely. This package is an Ultra Combo.

Some rich kid can buy a high level gun in an instant and slap it on a dinky vehicle, thus tricking the matchmaking system. The other problem with this fight is that there is a pit in the ground that is exactly as wide as your character. Sometimes you can walk over it, sometimes you will fall in if you try. It depends on if the physics like you.
The other was a very frustrating level where all your abilities are taken away. That's not the annoying part though; what makes it difficult is the enemy placements, which are placed such that you have to move away from the exit, back towards the start of the level, to avoid dying. It's weird.
Not only that, but it's a lot more fun to play the game as fast as possible, and try to go for good times- but almost every level is an auto-scroller! And if you get too quick and go off the edge of the screen, you die! This is a HUGE problem in the aforementioned level; it would be extremely easy if you could just run to the end, but you need to wait for the screen to slowly move to the exit while more enemies keep spawning.
I found the humor really weird... I didn't think it was funny, just strange and random. The first boss is the Pope, for example. Also, every time you touch a checkpoint (this includes when you respawn) there's a sexual moan. I think some people would find it funny, but it wasn't for me. The randomness also leaks into the plot; in other words, the plot is just random crazy junk happening.
The music was absolutely awesome, though, just as advertised, and the flashy lights and general art style fit together great. I really liked it when the stage would rotate a bit, making you tilt your head in order to play. It was a nice touch.
Short version:
Pros:
-Awesome music
-Great art
-Game is fun at times
Cons:
-Game is mostly too easy, but has huge difficulty spikes
-Humor doesn't really work (for me)
-Nonsense plot

I haven't been able to play a Dragon Ball game since Budokai Tenkaichi 3. So i was very excited when i heard this was coming out for PC! Hold on cause this will be a lengthy review~
Alright, so here we go. This game is definitely a hit or miss with fans. The combat itself is very good, feeling just enough like previous games but also adding some nice features to keep it interesting. The camera can sometimes be your enemy, especially when backed into a corner or fighting at the edge of a mountain or piece of terrain. The removal of a Charge Energy button is head scratching, as it was replaced with a Skill you have to buy that let's you charge your Ki, but that means wasting a skill slot which to me seems really backwards and unessassary.
The graphics are just stunning. This is by far the best looking Dragon Ball game i've seen. The cell shading and lighting make this look exactly like the anime itself, and gives a nice bright feel to all the crazy action! This carries nicely into the fact you can make your own character and dress them up. Howver i don't like the RPG aspect of the clothing having stats. It really forces you to choose clothing based on the stats they give, rather then how you want to look. The game has an attributes system to place points into what you want, so having the clothing effect it too is rather pointless in this style game.
The sound design is what i expect of Dragon Ball really. Great music, top notch voice acting, great sound effects. Even the Team Four Star cast from Dragon Ball Abridged got to record some voice work which was great! The only thing that was confusing and a bit pointless was that they decided to go with the Silent Protaganist angle. Which to me kinda messes up in this case. I was hoping to pick one of the 10 voices and hear my character talk to all my favorite heroes and villains of the show. Bit dissapointing.
As for the character creation itself, i'd say it's definitely good enough for what there is. You have 5 races, all with a variety of things you can adjust. You also can make a male or female of most of the races. Nemekians and Frieza's Race have no genders, which keeps in canon with the show. To me it feels like they'll probably add more later on as part of a DLC pack or just an update, which i'd like to see.
Alright so final thoughts. This game is definitely worth picking up, especially if you're a Dragon Ball fan. Yes it has some flaws, like the always online aspect of the servers, camera being a bit wonkey, slight frustration of unfair missions that you need to grind for a while to get strong enough to beat, and a few more. However, overall this is a fun game, and should be givin a good look at. It looks and feels like the anime and gives you plenty to do and explore for hours of entertainment.

Everything desynchs, from player position to platforms, weapons, bullets, anything you can think of. Even health desynchs, and dead players will stay alive and kill everyone else around.
Now, don't look at it as if it were a bad product. Overall, it's not. It's one of the funniest, fast paced LOCAL multiplayer games that manages to stay fresh and entertaining even after many hours of gameplay.
However, I will leave a negative review, hoping that devs will start focusing on fixing their own damage. This game has never been released as "early access", but a complete experience. And instead of progressing or at least being fixed, it went from a "vanilla state" to "current state" which is several times worse.
I almost feel like being robbed from a product that was ok-working to a non-working piece of code.
The worst thing? Developers stated from the very beginning that they won't be doing updates to the game. The following weeks they started introducing new maps, weapons and even an Halloween themed update with a new game mode. But they never focused on improving online gameplay quality, somehow making it worse with every patch.
So, congratulation for shoving in the market just another game which doesn't give signs of improvement, was fakely advertized as some complete product while it's clearly still in testing stage (and with an user interface that really requires some major rework, imho) and for using customers as testers instead of players. If you can easily find major game breaking glitches within minutes in your first casual playthrough, that's not nitpicking, it's a serious problem.
PS: I like this game, I simply now dislike the work these developers have been doing so poorly.

This is a damn good game.  Build your own bot of all sorts.  Fight them against other people.  Every bot design strategy has a strategy to counter it.  Don't want to design a bot?  There's a factory where you can get bots other people designed.  Then when you play the game, Battle Arena mode has plenty of strategy, or just go Team Deathmatch if you want to kill other people's bots.  There's even a custom match system if you want to do various battle types with friends.
Yes, there are some balance issues, but with a game with this many possible combinations of structural parts, weapons (lasers, railguns, AoE ground and anti-air, shotguns, healer, lock on missiles and bullets, machine guns, and melee), movement parts (hovers, jets, wings, propellers, helicopter blades, wheels, tank treads, insect legs, robot legs, etc.), and special power modules (shield, teleport, radar, EMP, powerup, and ghost), it's really not easy to balance all of that.  They do frequent balance updates however, so it constantly gets better.
The complaints about "pay to win" are complete nonsense, because all paying for premium or crates does is get you stuff faster than if you played for free.  Big whoop.  The people who pay keep the servers running and the game getting constant updates (new parts, new maps, new game styles, etc...) for everyone else.
The fact is, this is a damn good game.  I've played it since 2014 (and I only payed for a week of premium once) so I know that there is a lot of misplaced nostalgia for old systems that were removed because they were broken.  (For example, they got rid of tiers, which just kept new players from having access to certain parts until they leveled up, which was hard to do if you had no possible access to those parts.)
It also has a pretty great community, both in the forums and on YouTube.  If you need help, there are plenty of people willing to help in the forums, and I'm sure the YouTube tutorials will be updated to all of the new changes that led up to the v1.0 release.
Don't believe me?  IT'S FREE.  Try it and find out if it's a game you'd like for yourself.  I've gotten thousands of hours of enjoyment from it.

Secondly, there are better bridge builder games out there. Poly Bridge, for example. That game has a better physics and more variation in the puzzles.
I would only pick it up if you can get it on sale. Even then, I would recommend looking at the competition first.

Interstellar Marines is futuristic, online tactical first person shooter which has unique gameplay elements. In example you're actually playing in a virtual battleground which changes its' weather settings, platform levels and there is "day/night" cycle.
The gameplay has a realism aspect in its' own way. Projectile damage is high. Dark is really dark; you have to find your way with your flashlight and using momentary lightings such as thunder or a malfunctioning light sources etc. You have a helmet which contains your GUI but time by time it limits your view because of raindrops or dusty particles on the helmet glass; so you have to elevate its' front side from your face.
So, why don't i recommend this game to you (...yet)? Simple: Updates are occasional, framerate is still horrible despite the fact that developing process started a long time ago. Gameplay elements are still missing according to their gameplay plans but it's kind of OK. It has a dedicated player community as i see but they are few (or they are just playing the game when a new update comes).
Keep this game in your mind if you like tactical shooters but don't buy it yet.
