Caution: contains mild spoilers.
Conditionally recommended. The game's strongest points are its atmosphere and setting - using a museum is a great idea that I haven't really seen done in a game like this before, and most of the areas are very pretty and eerie. It's really a fun experience just to go through and see what the developers built, and I wish there was a museum this size and scope in real life.
The story, however, is about as cookie-cutter-Cthullian as you can find. There's no variation whatsoever on the standard "lost artifact brings chaos" plot, and the character you play as is little more than a camera for you to pilot around - no personality whatsoever. I don't mean his/her personality was written badly, I mean they literally say nothing, think nothing, and have no motive for doing all this except that someone's playing a horror game. The first thing you do is solve a very deadly electrical puzzle, and I can't help but think there is no motivation for anyone to do that so early on, no matter how long the uncle's been missing. There are a few well-written moments that build a bit of suspense and even make you question whether something is real or not, but it passes without much impact. What irks me about it so much is that this game is set in a
One "based on unusual cultures, legends, and supernatural themes." There was so much opportunity to build a complex and dreadful mystery between different cultures, historical periods, and mythologies, and all that atmosphere was wasted on fetch quests instead of lore-building. Adding an experienced writer to the team could have done so much for this game.
The puzzles are very simplistic. I've seen others compare this to Myst, but I wouldn't even call it close. The hardest thing you'll do is an "A = weird symbol" alphabet puzzle. There are enemies of an Amnesia: The Dark Descent variety, but they are quite unthreatening after the first encounter. They won't attack unless you shine a light on them (a creative touch, but it backfired) or are within a foot or two of them. Be aware that this game probably will not give you more than two hours of gameplay at most as a result.
As a final note, several elements lead me to question if the devleopers have finished their work on it or not.
I know I've been hard on this, but in the end, the fact is I did enjoy it, and two hours of extremely well-built environments is not a bad use of $7. I hope the developers revisit this concept with a larger team and more time to invest, because it really could have been so much more. Just be aware that, if you're looking for a really scary experience or challenging puzzles, this game will probably disappoint. But as an intriguing exploration built by only two people, it's a worthy experience.

I am a fan of their original snes version of the game. I used to play this for hours on end and now it comes onto PC. As I get in more hours I'll update it but in the short amount of time I've had to playing this I really am impressed with how well they did and wanted to write a review. I mean I would have just been happy with a clean import of the snes version but this is waaaaay better.
Here is a quickie of the shell of this.
Pros:
-All original characters are free
-There is a freaking battletoad
-Music is the same as it was in the 90s with some tweeks
-I never knew they had a story line, really the last time i saw them was when they were pixalated to hell
-They have a leveling system and somewhat of an RPG element with items you can use within battle. Leveling unlocks skins so it's you earn it or you can buy it with real money.
-You actually now know wtf was going on in the the first killer instinct
-The animations are beautiful and strong, the movements are fluent plus the characters actually have character dispite the story mode being kinda weird with the frozen models that have clothes flying in the wind still.
-VERY newb friendly, BEST tutorial for anyone new to fighting games I only recommend a controller
-Lots of character Customizations and the option to play a retro version of an original character.
-Make a shadow of yourself, kill a shadow of yourself, make another shadow of yourself, die to shadow of yourself, be proud of your new born spawn as it rakes in the shadow dough.
-Plenty of characters to learn and have fun with, tons of motivation to play different modes. All the characters have special abilites, special skills and different fighting styles that are very apparent.
Cons:
-It's not the 90s/80s :(
-Would recommend a controller (steam controller is not the best for this, xbox is best because of the + pad)
-Unfortunately most of the community seems to be a much higher level of skill so if you are a beginner I would recommend not playing multiplayer
-Orchid is still a pain in the bum
-Shadow Lord, Store and Shadow Lab require internet connection.
Wishes:
If they made a pixelated time machine or put the original snes version inside of this one :3 or even an all classic mode with everything looking and sounding like it did in the first snes version, I really liked the first one but this one is great!
Last words:
Now as for microtransactions they are completely optional and do not effect the game at this time. You don't even have to buy anything, most of it is just you have to earn it by playing that specific character alot. So far it does have a tinge of grind to it, but it doesn't seem like you have to play the game 800,000 times to get this skin. I can also see this getting popular with competitive play since the style actually negates combos better, and can make a break for turn arounds and such. This is also a very newb friendly game, sure it can get hard very quick if you make it that way. But, it does encourage you to keep going which I don't see in many combat games.

For a fighting game that just came out, this game has a metric ton of content, even if they don't add anything in the future, it fully justifies the $30 base price.
First of all, it's very noob friendly, even if you've never touched a traditional fighting game in your life you'll have a blast. (Honestly last TFG I played over 30 mins. was MK Armageddon over 10 years ago and before that probably MK2 or Killer Instinct at the SNES), but it's deep enough you'll have tons of things to learn and master if you want to go competitive.
Pros:
- Graphics are pretty damn nice.
- 29 characters with pretty unique playstyles, it's hard to get bored with so much variety
- Gameplay is incredibly fluid and fun.
- Very easy to get into, it even has an optional combo-assist system if you struggle with key coordination.
- IT HAS A TUTORIAL SYSTEM THAT IS ACTUALLY GOOD. Actually it's wonderful. You'll learn everything from movement/jumping/comboes to hitboxes/frame data/juggling/other advanced techniques. Many things you'll learn actually translate to other TFG's so it's even a great starting point.
- Crystal-clear Netcode which allows for smooth multiplayer.
- Survival mode and a Shadow mode which records your gamestyle and makes a bot out of it, which you can later challenge or send against the world!
- Combo system is the soul of the game, expect some massive enjoyment out of pulling them off or pulling off that combo-breaker that saves your life!
- Diverse AI difficulty, nothing to complain about it.
- Soundtrack is entertaining as hell, the game even plays its theme in basic tunes while you scroll through a menu!
- Game is very polished.
- While it's far too early to make a proper assesment, fighters seem very balanced even if they're so drastically different.
Middle:
- While it has microtransactions, they honestly may as well be removed from the game and nothing would change, it's only a quicker way to unlock skins/portraits/fluff you'll unlock on your own eventually. I'm not even sure why they put them in in the first place aside from "just because". It displays a huge ! icon everytime you unlock something or start up the game for the first time (removed pressing R on the subscreen), which is pretty distracting TBH.
- Characters has it's own "story mode", basically a small "survival" where you go from one opponent to the next. They have 3 endings each, and that's great and all! But what confuses me is that not every character has their own story, just about 18/29. Also it lacks unique dialogues between fighters or cutscenes or something that makes the feel out of a story mode besides having an intro and an ending.
Cons:
- While characters are memorable, some lack a little extra something to make them really stand out outside of its own world.
- It's quite resource-intensive, I can easily see some computers struggling to run it properly.
- If you can't run it properly, you won't be able to play ranked or public multiplayer (You can still make/join private rooms as far as I've seen).
- Shadow Lords ("Main" story mode) story is BAD, at least the introduction and world-setting. Not even so bad it's funny, just generic and bland, will update if it has a good twist or turn, but doesn't seem likely. It also has a mission-deploy like subgame and consumables which seem oddly out of place, still kudos for trying something new though.
- Some joysticks might be hard to configure without external aid, this is the main thing I hope gets fixed... (I tried with a couple PS2-like generics with no luck... keyboard works amazing for this game but makes it a struggle for local multiplayer)
And honestly that's it, I could rant more about details but honestly you're here for the core experience and a game with polish, passion, and a good value proposition. And it's all there. It baffles me that this game didn't get many news covering it or any advertisements at all... It's definitely worth the try even if you're not into the genre, if you are then I'm sure you'll love it.

Not worth it (have 40+ hours on it and also on RA3)
The biggest problem is that you have to micro manage every single unit if you want to use them effective and to their full capabilities. That is because every unit has a secondary ability that is usefull in some situations. But the AI (especially on Brutal) does it so much faster and can micro manage so many more units than you it becomes near impossible to play your faction effectively. This is really unsatisfying because you see your troops getting slaughtered brutally but cant do something about it because the AI (Brutal) will always be faster. So often you will resort to building massive armies and ultimately defeating the AI with massive numbers, but with very poor statistics (kill/death ratio etc.) Again very unsatisfying. The commander challenges are not that fun either. There are only 2 ways to complete those, either a Dojo rush or a VX rush (Dojo= Empire barracks, VX= empire helicopter and AA unit). Where is the fun in that? You will never build the elite units (kirov airship, century bomber etc.) of each faction if you take on these challenges, that is not fun.
The skirmishes are not an improvement either, The ammount of resources on every map is limited to 30K per ore mine. Which means that resources are scarce. Thus to get most bang for you buck is to make as many possible standard units and rush the enemy base. While the whole cool thing about this franchise are these very special elite units. Which because of limited resources are not economical to make because they are too expensive and a single one of them is not going to win you battles.
Now which faction benefited to most from this 'expansion pack'? The Empire of the Rising Sun.
they've got what they lacked in the Red alert 3: anti air infantry and a good/decent anti armor unit. Making them one of the better factions in the game if not the best since they are also not limited to a construction so they can build everywhere.
The Allies get a good tank unit and a even better bombardment plane. Making them strong in all aspects of naval, air and land warfare. But they also get a elite infantry unit the cryo legionaire, which is useless because he cant kill anything directly unless you micro manage him. The AI can micro manage him perfectly however...... The Allies are probably tied with Empire as the best faction in RA3: uprising.
The Soviets are (sadly) the most underpowered faction in RA3: uprising. They got a grinder tank which litterally grinds enemies to death but it is not a as good as an apocalypse tank. So you dont really need it actually. They also got a elite infantry unit: the desolator trooper. Which, unlike the Allies elite infantry unit, does kill infantry directly but only infantry. But it is very expensive and you can get more bang for buck purchasing their helicopter unit. So again, a useless unit since you have so little resources. When picking the Soviets as your faction, be prepared to get slaughtered and humiliated by the AI (Brutal). When Fighting the Soviets however, they seem a lot better because the AI micro manages units much better.
To ad: the campaign is very short. only a couple of missions.
Long story short: RA3: uprising is unbalanced and poorly designed. RA3 is better balanced and making elite units in that game makes actually sense. So stick with red alert 3.

The game certainly has potential, and I really like the concept and end goal the developers want. A fresh tactical FPS, that blends good co-op gameplay with a hit of XCOM.
First Impression Video
Sadly the current version disappoints horribly, and cannot be recommended.
The game currently barely features anything it's supposed to be. In single player you simply walk about alone, aimlessly on maps with nothing really to do. Multiplayer is simply some team deathmatch with a bit of capture points thrown about, and there are currently only two weapons to use.
The RPG aspects are non-existent, as is the so called non-linear gameplay.
Graphically the game is rather lacking overall, and uses the Unity Engine. The engine is not an issue, and if you run at low resolutions you'll be fine for quality. Although at full screen on my 3440x1440 display the game showed horrible banding, and crushed blacks. So bad in fact I had to show other screenshots to see if something might have gone wrong with my hardware calibrated IPS display.
The environmental and lighting is rather nice, and I do like the rain and dust effects on the visor to help try and draw you into the game.
Screenshot
Walking is terribly slow, although it's most certainly a gameplay mechanic; as a tactical squad is hardly supposed to sprint all over the place.
Gunplay is rather good, I do enjoy it and the weapons have decent recoil and feedback when used.
It's rather disappointing, although given the development team's size I hope improvements continue.
If they can pull it off, this is going to be one hell of a good game. It's just not worth it at the moment.

is clearly the result of an energy drink fueled all-nighter. Its story is full of holes, contradictions, and dropped threads. The level design is chaotic and lacks any sense of scale. Other than the odd hidden pressure plate (no spoilers) the puzzles are dull and uninspired and, except for the last one, serve only as a means to move from one level to the next and have nothing to do with the story.  The opening puzzle, which contains a multi-part solution, is the most thought out in the game, though it fostered the expectation that the puzzles would be challenging (they weren’t) and varying (they’re all basically variations on the same thing, other than the final one). games. There’s nothing especially original here, and much that is frankly and obviously derivative.
The world lacks any kind of human touch. The resources used (lamps, desks, bookcases, etc) are scattered about very sparsely. The result is barren, lifeless, echoing places that you run through looking for the next puzzle piece. You can't hide the lack of detail with fog
of the time! There are bad textures as well as missing textures. It is not conceivable that a mansion in 1909 would have modern galvanized steel air conditioning ductwork that looks like something out of, once again,
or any of a number of
games. Don’t get me started on the water puzzles or the doors that mysteriously open (or close) triggered by things you do elsewhere. And hey, what about all those large crates in small rooms that could not possibly have gone through the doors--any of them?
On the brighter side, the music seemed appropriately chosen for mood-setting and atmosphere, though the atmosphere loops were highly repetitive.
That brings me to the ending, which consists of a final puzzle and a series of cutscenes. Here I threw up my hands. It was like cutting the Gordian knot. Important questions were tossed aside, quest objects were ignored, well trodden game mechanisms went out the window, entirely new and unexplained symbols appeared, and then suddenly it was over. I think I even saw a screenshot from Amnesia, but I can’t be sure. What a mess. Think of the worst head scratcher you’ve ever seen. This is much worse. Adding cowbell wouldn’t make it worse.
Finally, the title. Really? I don’t mind so much that ignorant people have pointed out that it looks like “ashtray.” That’s the level of fan we’re dealing with, and that’s okay. I also don’t mind the people who have posted videos in which they prove that they don’t know what the word means by pronouncing it incorrectly--we live in a world in which ignorance is celebrated and correcting people is considered a microaggression--but what I do mind is that there is no discernible connection between the adverb “astray” (as in “Mary’s little lambs have wandered astray and she can’t find them”) and anything in the game whatsoever, on any level. It's hard to recommend this game.
It's got some damn decent visuals every now and again, and there were some areas that really stuck out to me.
But as far as horror goes, it was mostly meh. The only real bit that scared me was the recurring noise of a light that was, for some unexplainable reason, relatively unsettling to the point where I actually kind of jumped.
The enemy ai in this game seems dull. Sure they react when you run near them or shine your torch their way, but I was able to escape one by standing on top of a double box combo. It proceeded to run up to me, get stuck on the boxes, get confused, then turned around and walked away.
But the biggest thing that kept gnawing at me throughout the entire 107 minutes I spent in the game was the lack of anything. It felt like there were sizable chunks of the experience where I waited for something to happen, a startling noise, musical cues, a monster showing up out of nowhere, but no. Nothing.
There aren't even any musical bits letting you know you solved a puzzle. It's just *press button* "alright moving on".
The visuals are the thing that stands out the most for this game. Unreal engine was utilised pretty well for this venture.
All in all, the end sequence is probably the most exciting bit of the game. While there wasn't any music, there was plenty of different sounds and things going on to spice up the solitude.
TL DR: Pretty on surface, shallow with the horror. Overall very quiet.
If you do want to get it, it's already not horribly expensive. But I kinda wish I got it on sale.

I know what people normally do with this game, which is compare with Mario Kart... Which they have very close features, but this game deserves to be tested and felt on its own. So... forget any previous MK experience and give this game a try!
I've bought this game while on sale, so it was very cheap. And I have no regrets! This game really drove me nuts trying to perfect my drifting skills.
Unlikely any normal go-kart arcade game, this game actually benefits from some real racing techiques like following the corners apex to get the fastest lines like no other arcade game I've played so far. That really made me happy, since I'm a huge fan of sim racing style gaming, and for a 'just for fun experience' kind of game, this really made a fusion of what I like on a sim racing game and the fun chaos of an arcade game.
But, that doesn't mean you need to have any kind of experience in sim racings to have fun in this game. It's just that to get to a perfection (Specially trying to beat the devs fastest laps on each circuit), it's something to be considered.
Some pros and cons that I really would like to show:
Pros:
- Really fun go-kart/arcade racing game. Easy to get into, hard to master.
- Power-ups that range from a homing rocket, to a Super Star item which makes you invincible and can change the race results at any time.
- Very good sense of speed and physics.
- Stunt/Drift techniques that gives you boost.
- Some tracks completely change from one lap to another, which makes each lap a unique experience.
- Different kind of vehicles at different sections of the race (Car, Boat and Plane).
- Very good amount of tracks to choose from. (Not too many, but not too few)
- Great host of drivers to choose from, each with their own ups and downs, all from different SEGA Games.
- Great soundtrack!
- Very nice visuals.
- Several different game modes which changes completely the way you play.
- Lots of unlockables.
Cons:
- A Little bit tricky to learn the controls at the beginning (Specially when flying).
- Some cars are better at some tracks than others.
- Online multiplayer is a little bit weird. Sometimes you finish a race, but it doesn't actually finish the race. On server side, your character gets stuck somewhere and you dont get to finish the race.
- Sometimes the stunts don't work and try to compensate in the next trick, which results in 'Stunt Failed' and boost loss.
Overall, this game is a really fun experience, wether your looking for a fun time playing with your friends, alone or online, or trying to master all the tracks shortcuts and routes.
Definitely a must buy if you're an arcade racing game fan!

Clone Drone in the Danger Zone is a fun, creative game. The combat is voxel based, meaning damage is based entirely on where the weapon hits, rather than arbitrary numbers, which greatly adds to the immersion and combat. The weapons are varied, fun to use, and useful, while the enemies also provide a wide variety of challenges. That, combined with the sheer amount of levels, means that there is massive replayability. The announcers provide funny dialogue, which gives this game personality you'd be hard pressed to find elsewhere, and makes Clone Drone stand out from other games in the same genre. While the game is not entirely without bugs (it is still early access), it is completely stable, with very few bugs, none of them gamebreaking.
In addition to all that the game has to offer already, its community and its dev team is also excellent. The creator regularly streams development of this game, and takes suggestions and feedback form the chat. Doborog can also be found in forums, both here and on itch.io, where it was originally released. In fact, the hammer bots in game were originally conceived by the community. The community of this game is funny, creative, with some avid fanfic writers thrown in. In addition, the development speed of this game results in major updates every month or so, each one making the game better than the last, adding new features and changes.
In conclusion, this is a magnificent game, with fast paced, fun, and varied combat, excellent humor, a great community and dev team, with a nice soundtrack to top it off. In other words, get it already.

Because its the Month of October, i thought I'd try out some games on my steam library that I've never played before. Of course since Astray starts with a "A", it was at the top of my list. Looking at this game before jumping into it, it reminds me of amnesia and garry's mod horror maps. And with people on the steam page recommending this game, i thought it was going to be good. Especially since its a $7 cheap game. So here i went, into the world of Astray.
This game is mainly focused around solving puzzles more than a actual horror game and had a few pointless puzzles that were not even needed in the game, causing the player to feel like their time was wasted and not well rewarded. The puzzles here were quite easy to complete but if you want a challenge, then this is like Amnesia's younger brother. Especially since the game feels like it was inspired heavily by Amnesia with similar puzzles. Besides the puzzles, this game is also a scary game with only one monster walking around trying to get you in this museum as you look for your missing uncle. You would think the main goal was to find your uncle since it says so in this games description, however this objective gets dropped by the end of the game which leaves you wondering what happened and why none of the story makes sense. Its not a bad game, but here is how i saw it.
As you venture on into the museum, you soon realize that the story line doesn't flow well with whats going on and you start to lose interest in what's happening. The story unfolds in notes being left by others where you have to piece together what's happening in order to follow along. But honestly you don't even need to look at the notes because of how dull the writing is and how it doesn't connect the player at all to this mysterious museum. The atmosphere is creepy but not in a good or bad way. The graphics are pretty to look at but nothing truly horrifying and many rooms felt like fillers with lack of details. but if it really wanted to be a horror game, the only jumpscares are just lights flickering, monster moaning like a smoker and your death scene which lasts only a sec or two followed by a falling object here and there. The scare factor was simply not there, or at least it was 30 minutes into the game till you realize the only horrifying thing are puzzles to complete.
I should mention how awful it is to see a "Saving progress" icon at the bottom right of this game. Every time you got to a important area where there was about to be a jumpscare or just to keep the suspense up, your game pauses as its being saved randomly, making it a mood killer for anyone who wanted to feel terrified. Also the bugs in this game are troublesome. Even if i enjoyed spending 3 hours total on this game, the bugs made me restart my game 3x whenever my game glitched my mouse into moving my character on its own or when i glitched into the floor or out of the elevator. I would think by now that the developers would patch this up but it still has issues.
But do i hate it despite all of its flaws? No. Astray is a game that is easy on the eyes, easy on the wallet but has a few flaws in its design and storyline and overall fear factor. But i did enjoy playing through this game, despite how frustrated some things made me. To me this is a O.K. type of game where if you bought this right now or even on sale, its acceptable to play but don't expect greatness from it.
Just a great game hope the devs keep making it better.

so there are a few annoyances with this game that prompted me to give this game a thumbs down
- the bridge building physics are bad (you basically cant reinforce any joints with more braceing because more often then not trying to brace a joint will actually make it weaker because instead of diverting the strain elsewhere like it would do in real life the game reads it as there is now more weight on that joint and therefore the piece that was already strained is more likely to break)
-when one piece breaks it doesn't matter if any other part of the bridge could or would be able to take the load, they all are suddenly unstable and brittle and WILL break
- to compound on the inability to brace joints they also have very few "braced points"(and or starting placement points" in this game) which with only having 1 point on many levels on each side of the gap makes it increasingly difficult to make any type of stable bridge
-the wood and metal beams must be made of a heavy paper because they can hardly hold up their own weight (bridges HAVE to be minimalist in function because of the weight of the materials is too heavy for their strength basically trying to have a huge bridge is impossible)
- building the bridges has a few glitches, quite often like every 20th click when placing a bridge piece (not deleting it) it will delete any other pieces located in that area. about every 30th click your delete button will not regester no matter now many times you click with it until you then click on a available building material

The alternate history world building and characters make this game. Story is SCHLOCK, which is a good fit.
First handful of levels were brilliant. Later levels have the player going through the motions: shooting bad guys through a handful of rooms, opening a cutscene door, shooting bad guys through a handful of rooms.
Occasionally the difficulty will spike noticeably, such as getting dropped into a scenario with minimal weapons/ammo/cover and hounded with bullet sponge enemies with high damage output. On higher difficulties cover is absolutely necessary - so a gameplay style akin to a shooting gallery combined with a slow walk speed make the game feel mind numbingly slow at points. When shooting from behind cover at mid/long range it feels wrong - as if everything except for the damage output of enemies and ammo type distribution was designed for high speed and close up encounters.
Collectables, concept art an character bios will pop up during gameplay. You can look view the current level's collectables from the journal menu or all collectables from the main menu. There's sections of downtime between some levels, it would be nice if you could read previous level's collectable text in those.
In comparison to Doom 2016 which delivered above expectations, "The New Order" was a disappointment. While suffering from the same issues, standalone expansion "The Old Blood" has a few encounters which give the player more agency during combat, with fewer cutscenes to slow down the game.

So nice to see this game back 20 years later. Having played the original for SNES with the black cartridge when I was very young, it was very addictive then. 20 Years later, the game is revived for PC with a modern overhaul, and this couldn't be more exciting. For the price, it is totally worth it for anyone that likes KI (was an even better deal on its release promo). The soundtrack is very worth it too. If you are a Mortal Kombat fan, and can give up the gore, this is a better fighter IMO. Actually,
What separates this from MK, aside from the no gore (so it is more friendly in all countries / younger players), is that the gameplay is not overly hard with having to press 8 buttons for a skill, and comboing is very smooth. There is also a combo assistance program for those learning, but I recommend turning it off ASAP in order to properly enjoy the game and raise your skill. It can also get quite difficult on the higher difficulties that will test the elite. There are several elements that add a lot of depth, but never feel overwhelming. Of course you need to practice each character, as there are several "role" styles, such as rusher, tank, etc.
This is 100% optional, and used to unlock shadow or mimic skins currently. It can also be used in Shadow Lords mode to buy packs, but this only effects your gameplay (unless you do multiplayer shadow lords, but MP shadowlords is designated as a wacky experience, not serious, not to mention it would be a huge waste of cash for people that use these power ups)
In short, it is purely to buy cosmetics or speed through the long-term story mode. You can unlock all this through natural pay too, that is all there is to it, no advantages.
Also, by doing your dailies, you will gradually get small amounts here and here.
-No more humilition finishers or any gorey finishers. Not every character has an ultimate (Orchid really needs one :<), but those as as close to gore as it will get. The sinister nature is implied (setting up daggers beneath the neck, then an offscreen sound effect that implies the head was pushed through them)
-Lots of characters compared to way back - 29 in total.
-Many characters moves are altered, namely in terms of projectiles. I miss Orchid's projectile, and every character used to have one, but now it is select characters only
-Obvious graphics overhaul. They look great really, without being GPU/CPU intensive
-Combo Breakers are unlimited now, but you only have 1 chance per combo set to get it right
There is a lot going on for single player in relation to a fighting game. Unless you buy your way through, or absolutely dislike Shadow Lords mode, this will keep you busy for a quite some time.
-Regular story mode: Fight through a roster and perform specific accomplishments to unlock canvas pieces. This is a long term goal where you complete 10 characters worth about, x2 seasons
-Survival mode: Survive with one character through as many fights as possible
--Shadow Survival mode: Same as survival, but with shadow players (harder clones of real people in a sense)
-Dojo: This is where you practice and learn all the elements of the game.
-Shadow Lords Mode: This is the main story/SP element. You fight, make story choices, gain items/power-ups, with the ultimate goal being to take down the shadow lord. This will require a lot of time investment, but your items and stuff carry over to the next playthrough. This makes it a nice progression system without losing your time invested
-Dailys: Several dailys, resetting each day, that give you rewards for Shadow Lord mode & general player exp
I have not really touched this mode, as the SP modes are super fun. I tried fighting a friend though, and even while downloading near my bandwidth limit, the fight worked flawlessly. Usually when I download like this, there is noticeable lag, so that in itself speaks something
-You got ranked / standard playmodes
-There is also a Shadow Lords multiplayer, but it is a non serious mode as people can use their power ups, making for a one sided match. There are dailies tied to this though (the biggest being play 5 matches, win or lose) so you got nothing to lose
For the most part, each character feels unique, but they do fit into one of several roles, which determines their playstyle. Rushers for example are fast and combo focused fighters, but they deal less damage in exchange. Tanks take blows like champs, but are slower of course and hit harder. There are more categories, and some are unique such as using their own health to fight, but having the ability to siphon it back. In total you have 29 characters, and it comes down to finding what fits you, then having fun practicing the rest and trying to get good as them as well.
Several characters use or share button skillsets, so it isn't overly complex. Each has their own set, but many use a Down - Bottom Right - Right - Attack - as a single for example.
The fighting is satisfying. It is not difficult, the combo system is smooth, but there is enough depth and complexity to go at it from many ways. There is a slight limitation in how it is set up. You want to perform combo openers > auto > linkers > auto > linkers > ender, or something like that. Doing this is what lets you effectively chunk the most health for your efforts. Other methods work too, but for less damage.
-Shadow skills are a nice touch, as they are simply a stronger, more lethal version of your key combo skills.
-Winning the fight and performing that Ultra finisher is really fun and never gets old. Alternatively you can convert it into a stage ultra if possible, or an ultimate finisher if the character has one.
-Combo breakers: A fighting chance to break out of a combo, if you can read the enemy hit set right (High, Medium, Low). This is a fun system, and unlike past KI's, it is unlimited, but you only have 1 chance to break out per combo set the enemy performs.
Mimic & Shadow Skins, + a stage or two. You can earn all this through regular play or buy it with KI gold. There is also all the achievement, progression, and performance side stuff like lore, alternate costume colors, and so on. Most of this is tied to simply playing the game and leveling up the characters.
Personal experience score: 10/10
Story: -/10 - Hard to rate this, but Shadow Lords offers a form of story, along with lore for each character, and some general story to them. It is a fighter so it isn't the main focus, but there is a bunch of it.
Sound: 10/10 - KI has always had one of the best soundtracks out there since its SNES edition, Seasons 1-3 just made it even better.
Graphics: 10/10 - Excellent. Runs perfect on GTX 960 and it looks perfect, without sacrificing any performance
Controls: 9/10 - Easy to use on my 360 controller. I find using a control stick a bit harder and the Dpads on these aren't so great, so if you can use something with a pad or joystick (like SNES controller or an arcade controller), that is your best bet. The controls are easy regardless though, you just have to learn the few pattern styles consisting of 2-4 buttons, and many characters use similar combinations.
Game Length: 10/10 - The play is infinite, ultimately. The longevity of the game will be user based. If you are looking to play an hour or 2 here or there, willing to learn and get good at playing characters outside your comfort zone, if you are going to multiplayer, etc.

I just wanna get this outta the way immediately: I'm getting a refund for this game because unfortunately it doesn't run properly on my LAPTOP (I expected it, it no way detracts from my love for this game. Just means I have to play it on XBone)
Those who play street fighter, uMVC3 or Tekken may find this game to be simple on the technical side of things, that's because this game puts an emphasis on adapting to an opponent's patterns, since the combo pattern is relatively straightforward. (Opener -> Auto Double/Manual -> linker  -> ender. Steps two and three can be repeated until the KV (Knockdown Value) reaches 100, at which point the character being hit will spin out and the combo will end without being able to end it. Keep in mind that you can end the combo if the last hit before the ender pushes the KV meter above 100.
The complexity of this game comes from, as I said, the adaptations that players make during matches. I'm not going to go into detail with just HOW complex it is, because that'd make this review longer than it needs to be, but tl;dr if you're quick to adapt, you will excel at this game. Punishing an opponent's mistake is very satisfying as every combo can potentially do 30%+ damage, depending on how you do it.
But, alongside the layers upon layers of guessing, adapting and predicting what your opponent is going to do, further complexity is given through the mechanic of combo traits. These are character-specific traits which aid them in some way. For example, I'm a Sadira main. Sadira's combo trait is air juggle,  she is the first character in the series to have a proper air combo system, and you can have some really fancy comboes that start on the ground and end in the air.
ON TOP of combo traits, there's also a mechanic specific to this game that adds a way to extend comboes: Instinct mode. When you activate instinct mode mid-combo, it resets the KV meter I spoke about before, while keeping your ender level the same. Not only does it reset the combo, allowing you to essentially double the damage, but it gives your character MORE traits that help them. Again, take Sadira as an example. Her instinct mode gives her access to web traps, which allow you to place a static, area-controlling web in front of her. This has a myriad of uses: making combo breaker attempts safe, anti-airing, extra damage/hitstun, just to name a few. It really has Sub-Zero ice clone vibes. Not only that, but during her instinct mode, she also gains the ability to jump-cancel her normals. This leads to, assuming you're in a combo, A LOT of damage, as you can link a heavy kick into itself for massive damage. But your opponent has the choice of whether or not to break it, or predict that you're going to throw an occasional light kick in to try and block them out from counter breakers. Or you could take a chance and throw out a counter breaker to reset the combo AGAIN.
That's what this game is about. Risk vs reward: knowing when to take a risk, when not to take one, and even by not taking a risk, you're taking one, if that makes any sense.
I haven't even brought up one-player modes. As with every fighting game I've played, the AI on very hard/maximum difficulty feels cheap, especially in this game where breaking a combo all depends on if you adapt and choose the right attack strength to break against. The AI has an "Ultimate" difficulty, also known as Kyle, I'm assuming a programmer who developed the game. It's unbeatable, I gave it two tries and stopped because it wasn't fun. It gives off classic Mortal Kombat vibes, where you have to cheap the game out with safe moves and conform to a playstyle that you don't necessarily want to use and don't have fun with. That being said, medium/hard difficulty is fun.
Shadow lords is a refreshing amalgamation of RPG elements combined with the core game to make a less serious but still really fun game mode. Upon first glance you may think "WOW, that enemy has 50% extra health? That's BULL." But you'll soon realise that you, too, have the opportunity to buff your character's stats through the use of consumable items and guardians. Consumables range from using them before the match to give your character full instinct/shadow meter, healing the character (because health carries over after a match if you win, if you lose, that character dies but can be resurrected if you have the item for it) to dealing more/taking less damage in the match. Guardians give passive boosts to your stats (Trust me, if you want to unlock the astral plane stage by beating Gargos on challenging difficulty, you're going to NEED the stat boosts) but they also give an active effect that you need to charge the guardian to use. You charge the guardian with astral energy that you gain by playing the game mode. I mentioned unlocking the Astral Plane as a stage because it shows that, even though there's microtransactions in the game, that stage cannot be unlocked by paying for it. You can accelerate its unlocking by paying for KI gold to buy strong guardians, but it isn't paywalled: you can earn those guardians by playing the game, and I did, I didn't spend anything on it. It just took longer.
As for online: I don't know, I haven't played it on PC so I can't judge the netcode, I live in Australia so the connections to other players on a good day would be average at best, and I haven't played it online on the XBone.
Now for the tl;dr pros&cons:
Pros:
Every character feels fresh and unique, and aren't typical/stereotypical (Jago isn't a Japanese Ninja or black belt, he's a Tibetan Monk, how many fighting games have such an unorthodox character/personality?)
Combo system is relatively simple and easy to grasp; friendly/welcoming to new players, easy to master and excel at
Looks great.
AWESOME guest characters from other Rareware/xbox games (Rash, Arbiter, General Raam).
AWESOME music. DYNAMIC music, aka the music changes depending on what's happening in the match, never seen it before.
FULL transparency of moves (frame data, other info on moves such as invincibility, frame advantage on block, etc. For people like me who want to know their character inside out, this is GREAT.)
Despite the simple combo system, the game still has footsies, spacing, etc.
You earn extra colours/cosmetics while playing the character and levelling them up, giving more incentive to play the character.
Tier lists aren't as conclusive in other games. While Fulgore is REALLY good, characters are really well balanced.
Lots of characters.
Cons
While the combo system is fun, comboes can start to feel stale after doing them so many times, even if you mix up attack strengths.
Microtransactions: You can buy all colours except for the level 50 colour, letting you buy the colour you want and not bothering with the rest, devaluing the whole "earn it through gameplay" system.
Microtransactions : You can buy guardians and healing items in Shadow lords, which (for me) devalues unlocking the astral plane as a stage.
AI can feel cheap, as with every fighting game, and inhuman in reaction times.
Microtransactions: Just because they're a trend in games nowadays doesn't mean I have to like them.
In summary: If you're a fighting game fan, give it a try. Do I recommend it? YES. It's such a fun game.

There are quite a few things I liked about this one and overall it's a solid effort with some cool ideas. Setting it in a museum is a good start, and some of the areas have a very believable, real look to them. I'm always a fan of setting-based horror games and this one uses that well. It has some effective creepy atmosphere and sound, and some of the puzzles were fun to solve, if a little easy. And I don't say that to boast. I'm a terrible puzzle-solver in games who frequently needs a guide, but this one didn't stump me at all.
But, sadly, the shortcomings just kept it from working for me. The one monster, while creepy, was dumb and non-threatening, easy to escape or just glitch out entirely. An obvious setup for a chase scene had me just walking right in front of it with no reaction, as the detection radius seems to actually be very small. The moments where I was tense that I had almost been seen, I probably wasn't close at all. That along with some irritating physics puzzles that can glitch out and send boxes flying across the room, and a player character with a painfully small jump ended up eating up all the goodwill inspired by the positive aspects of the design. I don't like voting down games that I thought were original and creative, but the execution lacked too much for me to recommend this one. It might work for you if you're willing to overlook its flaws, but it didn't do it for me despite my love of all things horror.

Astray is a first-person horror game with gameplay very reminescent of Amnesia: The Dark Descent. It's a microbudget indie game made by only two people, but unlike many such games on Steam it's actually very solidly made and professionally presented. It definitely comes across as a professionally made game, rather than (unlike many first-person horror games on Steam) a programming student project.
The game has fully rebindable keys, invert mouse, and decent graphics options, and as far as I've seen the game doesn't have any major bugs or other amateurish weirdness.
It's a fairly short game (I finished it in a little over 2 hours, and that was on a blind playthrough where I explored around quite a bit and had to take several minutes for some of the puzzles), but there are several different environments/levels and overall the game does feel like a "complete" game.
Graphically, the game isn't triple-A quality but is still reasonably decent. Overall, I'd say the graphics are on par with the average games' graphics from 2010-2012.
The story is fairly simple and straightforward, on par with a Lovecraft short story. You play as a standard faceless silent protagonist, and there's no real voice acting in the game, with the story being revealed through readable notes scattered throughout the game (the notes are generally in obvious locations and you don't have to explore hidden areas to find them). Overall the game is more about the atmosphere rather than the plot.
Gamplay is a mixture of exploration, steath/evasion, and puzzle solving. The puzzles are decent and not too difficult; I never got stuck trying to figure out how to complete a puzzle, although there were a few times I did get stuck trying to progress because of other reasons (finding the switch for the hidden door in the Egyptian area is the example that most comes to mind).
Item-hunting is minimum as the game doesn't really have an inventory or item system. The only items found in the environment are key items, notes that give snippets of the story, and batteries to instantly recharge your flashlight to 100% (the flashlight also slowly recharges when not in use, so you won't get stuck if you can't find a battery).
Like Amnesia, the game has monsters you need to stealth around or run away from. The monsters patrol along a fixed route, have a visual detection range of about 20-30 feet, respond to noise (i.e. running fast) as well as if you shine the flashlight on them. There's only one monster type and graphically they don't look great up close, but are decent and unlike some other games are at least not Playstation 1 quality models. Their A.I. is quite simple, but functional.
The monsters actually appear fairly sparingly; there are only 9-10 of them in the entire game. They're mostly to create the possibility of a threat instead of serving as a constant, ever-present threat (the monsters are actually fairly scarce, but the fact they
be anywhere are what creates tension as you move through the environments). I actually appreciated this as this allows them to create tension without becoming obnoxious or frustrating.
I did feel that the Museum of the Supernatural setting of the game was under-utilized. For the most part, the museum setting (with creepy exhibits etc) was only really majorly used in the first 1/4th of the game, Later areas (which comprised most of the game) were a more generic backstage office area, a dark basement, and an underground area.
The ending was rather abrupt, but if you read all the notes and take in mind the fact the game takes place just a few years prior to the outbreak of World War I, it may kind of make sense what the developers were trying to imply with the ending.
Overall, I wouldn't say Astray was great, per-se, but it was a good, competently and solidly made, complete experience, especially when you consider the fact it was made by only two people on a minimum budget.  Overall, it's one of the rare first-person microbudget indie games on Steam that is a full legit game that actually does "deserve" to be sold on Steam for money, rather than being a glorified programming student project.

Tales from the Borderlands is based on the first-person shooter game series by Gearbox Software. Telltale transforms it to a narrative driven, episodic point-and-click adventure.
I was never fan of the game series before. But Telltale converted me with their terrific writing of characters and dialogue. World of Pandora has never been this interesting and fun! The story itself, isn't that remarkable. It's told by two characters, both controlled by the player. What shines in the writing is the hilarious dialogue. Characters have great personalities and are very memorable. Some characters are new and others have been introduced earlier in the series. Besides some familiar characters, there are other nods to the games too.
This is the best looking game by Telltale so far and It's also faithul to the style of Gearbox's games. Every episode has an awesome intro sequence that sets the mood for the game, it's accompanied by a great soundtrack. None of the five episodes felt filler at all and the last episode especially holds up. You get to see how your choices mattered and the familiar quick time events bring on a twist almost like Street Fighter style.
Tales from the Borderlands is a welcomed change of pace for Telltale, their other recent games have all been so dark and gritty. This takes them back to the tone of Monkey Island and Sam and Max games. But no puzzle solving this time either.

I bought this game a while ago, and at the time It was the first or at least one of the first early access games I've bought. At the time it seemed like a good deal. Now that I have more experience with early access, I feel that this game is on the lower end of the early access experience. The concept is great, and the game looks good on a graphical level, yet there are things that I feel make this game not a good game to buy just yet:
- When I was looking at buying this game, the previews on the store page showed more than the game offered. I feel like I was cheated out of my money a bit because I pretty much paid 15$ for a tech demo when the previews showed a decent alpha/beta game.
- Updates are slow, which isn't a problem for me usually, but the fact that the only time I hear from the developers is when an update is released makes me a bit frustrated. If updates are maybe 2-3 months apart and those are the only times I see news from the developers, It makes me think that they are giving up on the game, or just don't feel that the players are worth spending time on to write a little news about what they are doing or planning.
- Playing only two gamemodes for months until the next gamemode comes out isn't exactly my kind of multiplayer game. I feel that the choice to release a FPS multiplayer game with only two gamemodes was a bad choice.
I don't hate the game, I actually think that this can be a really cool game later on during its development. However, the game isn't what I expected. The thing that bothered me the most was the sort of false advertising on the store page. Again, the game isn't too bad, but I would wait to buy it.

Great little horror game, made all the more impressive by the scant numbers of guys involved in its design.
The setting and the atmosphere it evokes is absolutely spot on and this is the most impressive part of the game in general.  Every area is unique and well done.  The puzzles fit and are in general more challenging at least than find-key-unlock-door without being too frustrating.
What also deserves a note was the fact they included a maze and actually made it fun to run through, hurriedly backtracking when you hear the heavy breathing of an enemy round the corner.
The enemies (there was only one type, barring the end boss), unfortunately didn't maintain their fear-inducing presence throughout.  Once you were killed by them once and saw them up close they just didn't evoke the same sense of dread.  Especially when later in the game you find them shambling about in a large, open, and brightly lit room.
There were some little oddities I encountered, like how running will make noise to attract enemies, but throwing chairs round the place is like throwing weighty balloons in terms of the noise they make.  Not to mention the occasional very obtuse puzzle and unnecessary invisible wall.  But these are minor grievances.  All in all a very impressive Amnesia-alike, and I look forward to seeing what these produce next!

I did not know how they would handle the combat, the over the top shooting, the billzion guns.... you know the game people :).  I have to confess here and now I was wrong, I was very very wrong. Basically Blondie BeefCakes McActionMovieProtagonist has a superpower.  That superpower is killing Nazis.  It does not matter what kind of Nazis, or how many Nazis, Blondie is ready to

The main quest boils down to "Hey, we want to kill Nazis, and/or this particularly important Nazi.  All we have is a knife and a pile of first aid kits.  WHAT WILL WE DO?!"  To which Blondie replies "I GOT THIS, everyone else just sit here and look important.  Oh, could you please queue up some heavy metal action music?  BBIAB."
Sometimes there are side quests.  "Please, Not-Chris-Evans-As-Captain-America-But-Pretty-Darn-Close, I know you are busy killing Nazis, but there's a Nazi I want you to kill."  Or the variation of "The Nazis have this thing that is really important to me, but you'd have to kill, like, a lot of Nazis to get it.  Like a ton of Nazis.  Need killing.  Can someone PLEASE help me kill all these Nazis?"
I really shouldn't have to explain the basic gameplay of Wolfenstein to anyone.  If you've never played classic Wolfenstein, go find a chatroom and ask a 14-year old girl.  They are most likely a middle-aged guy named Carl who has extensive experience with classic videogames.  They will be happy to help.  Once you know what that was like, imagine everything much prettier and you get the basic idea.
Shooting Nazis is good.  Probably the best part of the game.  Often at the start of a level they take away my guns and that makes me feel sad.  It is hard to shoot Nazis when I don't have a gun.  But then I stab a few Nazis and find a gun and all is right with the world again.  Sometimes I have two guns at the same time.  I like that.
Sometimes, there are "stealth" segments.  Wolfenstein is not a great stealth game.  It's not really clear where enemies are or how they manage to detect you, they just do and it sucks and you die or maybe you just end up shooting lots more Nazis.  There's one pistol you can find a silencer for, (if you know precisely where to look) and it can headshot for instant kills at an obscene range.  You can also throw a knife into someone's leg and they will crumple into a disorganized pile of limbs.
Sometimes Blondie Wolfenstein gets all emo and starts talking about how the war, Nazis and/or this one important Nazi are terrible and murdered a lot of people, which really puts a damper on my current objective of murdering a lot of people.  But then he stopped talking, I got back to murdering Nazis, and the game was fine again.
There's also swimming and it's quite bad.  One time my girlfriend called me while I was getting all emo about swimming and started reading me her dead cousin's diary while I was slowly asphyxiating.  There were no Nazis nearby.  I did not enjoy that level.  I wish I was making that up.

Cute Things Dying Violently is a game where the player may choose to rescue cute critters. These are the types of critters that one would expect to find wandering around aimlessly in a flower bed, through grassy planes, or even in a lightly wooded forest area. However, as I said, the player has a choice, and that choice may lead the player into causing a certain and painful death. Either intentionally, or even quite possibly accidentally. The player may choose to throw these critters onto spikes, into fire hazards, within a bolt of lightning, cause death due to falling, or the player’s choice of small to large buzzsaws can be utilized as well. I really think the developer watched one too many “Saw” movies.
Cute Things Dying Violently is created by ApathyWorks. The game has 60 pre-designed levels. However, with the integration of Steam Workshop and a Level Editor, the potential amount of levels is pretty limitless. This game is heavily integrated onto the Steam PC platform, and as such it also possesses Steam Trading Cards and Steam Achievements. The developer truly went all in, on the Steam platform. Another nice feature is the weekly challenge through the level of the week format from the main menu.

Received for free from a Desura giveaway.
A decent puzzle game where you try and flick things to the exit. The closest thing I can think of is a cross of lemmings and golf.
It's annoying that there isn't a setting to keep the mouse cursor inside the window in windowed mode. Once your cursor moves outside your flick gets messed up so you need to up the sensitivity and try to keep your mouse inside when flicking. And because they don't let you move the camera the objects are almost always near the edge of the screen.
Non-16:9 resolution options are 'broken' in the sense that you can't move the camera so parts of the screen are cut off. It only matters in the wider stages. For example, in stage 2-3 you can't see the button that will stop the fan (so the level is impossible). For another example, in stage 2-7 the creature can walk offscreen and part of a button is offscreen).
The aim trajectory guide isn't 100% accurate but is passable. However, it can get really terrible in certain circumstances.
In order to unlock the next set of puzzles, you're forced to complete all 7 and then beat the boss (level 8). I think that requirement shouldn't be there or it should be relaxed (complete half the puzzles and boss to progress). It's a puzzle game so it's easy to gate people from seeing all the mechanics that are introduced. There are a lot of things introduced in the second set and I'm guessing a lot of casual puzzle players will have trouble. There are six sets of 8 puzzles to try in the main mode so if you get stuck on a puzzle on the second set you miss out on over half the game. They offer 'level of the week' and user-made levels so if you can't progress at least you can try alternative levels.
I'm not really a fan of puzzle games but if you want a more polished game that has a similar basic premise (get the guy to the exit), you can try something like Eets Munchies. However, I'm not sure there is another game that does this exact premise. If you like the premise but care about any of the problems above you may want to wait for an update. These problems seem like they could be fixable so you might want to wait and see if the developer changes anything.

Great game, I recommend it to anyone who grew up with Dragonball Z!
Pros:
-Combat is fun and rewarding
-The story is cool and follows all of the major parts of the Z series
-The story mode can be difficult and challenging in various ways
-Lots of skills and outfits (even from the original DB and GT)
-Art style is perfect, completely perfect. Adds to the immersion of the game
-Parallel Quests give interesting alterations to the story and some have very indepth secret objectives
-Lots of fun options and customization for characters, whether you're minmaxing something for PvP or just making a fun gimmick character (like my female human who has android moves and an android-like outfit)
Cons:
-Servers are really wonky, though that seems to have subsided in the past couple days or so
-Lots of bugs that sometimes break the game in the middle of a PQ
-Certain race/sex combinations are way stronger than others, and some just seem to be designed weakly (for the latter, Namekians)
-Only Saiyans have the ability to transform into anything, while that feature should also be made available to Frieza race, Majins, and maybe Namekians
-Super Saiyan spam is annoying
-Certain skills and zsouls are gamebreaking in PvP, so of course there will be a ton of people running combinations of those
-The grind is irritating and PQ secret objectives don't always happen despite meeting the conditions.

Lego The Lord of the Rings is easily the best Lego game to date. There's a ton to see and do, with a large but not overwhelming Middle-Earth overworld containing lots of subquests and items to acquire as well as eighteen action stages that take you through the movie trilogy. I say "movie trilogy" since that's what the game is based on for the most part, but the developers have clearly done their homework and include a fair number of references to things only found in the books. Tom Bombadil and Radagast make appearances, for instance. This reverence for Tolkein's work makes this game a sheer joy for anyone who really loves The Lord of the Rings in any form.
About my only complaints are the lack of online co-op and the length of some of the action stages. They can take upwards of half an hour to complete, and the mid-stage saves don't seem to work reliably enough to allow for quitting and resuming the stage from where you left off at a later time. There's almost no real difficulty to speak of, with death being almost inconsequential and both combat and platforming being extremely basic affairs, but I don't consider that a negative since the game controls really well and has enough clever puzzles that you can't just turn off your brain if you want to collect everything.

Game development is just taking far too long.  It seems that the focus has been big time on graphics and little else.  So if they can apply the level of quality in their lighting effects to ANYTHING else in the game at some point it has a lot of promise, but after a few years I just don't see it coming. Just grab it when it comes out (if ever) or when it gets closer to completion, you won't be missing anything.  They take so long to do anything the "future expansions" you're guranteed with preorder will probably never exist or will take so long you'll have moved on to something else.

Attention ** Non Spoiler Review as follows**  If you have any feelings for Borderlands and Borderlands 2 this is a MUST PLAY.  If you enjoy the tell tale games from walking dead, to wolf amoung us this is a MUST PLAY.  An if you enjoy a good story, or as a casual gamer enjoy watching the game as much as you like playing games I would urge you to pick it up on the steam Thanksgiving or Christmas sales.  It really is well crafted, has some of the GREATEST music for every chapter intro, and has allot of heart.  With that said I am now going to delve a little deeper and do not wish to ruin anything for someone who wants absolutely NOTHING that can even remotely be similar to a spoiler.  So again I loved the game, it is right up there with Walking Dead from tell tale, AND it made me love Borderlands all the more....
** Will try to keep it very non spoiler below as well, but best not to chance it if your someone wanting to know NOTHING before you play..... So you have been warned...... do not read below.... your fault if you do :)   **
The game really really makes me hope for a sequel to this game, and hope one day for a proper Borderlands 3.  Borderlands to me is a game I forget how much I miss it until I play it, or hear a song from it, or remember the funny dialog lines.  I must confess when I first heard tell tale was doing Borderlands I was confused, and thought this a poor choice.  I did not know how they would handle the combat, the over the top shooting, the billzion guns.... you know the game people :).  I have to confess here and now I was wrong, I was very very wrong.  This game has heart, a ton fo heart.  Some of the best voice acting talent in the business (seriously it is a fckn who's who of voice talent) , and great writing.  This game had me smiling from the oepning scene, and watching every chapter intro for great music and opening scenes I wish were all twice as long.
**The Good**  Tell tale respects the Borderlands world and mythos, while still added their own touch of humor, feel's, and spin on Pandora and all we Borderlands fans know and love.  The music (like most borderland games) is phenominal, great in every song, and WHEN the songs are used.  The voice talent is as i said a who's who of talent.  Easily using 4 or 5 of the top 10 to 15 we have in the industry, and it makes a difference.  It helps the humor, the sad, the mad, the feels, the everything....  The story (which is one of my top 2 hooks to me as a gamer) is really well done.  Nothing new or game changing, but very well done.  Adding some new heroes and villians to the world of Borderlands that quite frankly I want to see again.  An..... an this is hard for me ...... I wish to keep this spoiler free...... so I will simply say this game has a gut punch in it..... then even tho it brought me to tears... I really REALLY give tell tale and 2k games and gearbox A HELL OF ALOT OF CREDIT for doing it... and doing it very well.  I was told (research this may be wrong here) that this game is canon in the Borderlands universe and if that is true then I give them 10x more credit for doing what they did.  The ending felt right, and I was emotionally satisfied with the way they went.  I really hope this makes enough money and gets enough respect to get a season 2 to this game.
** Final Thoughts**
I loved nearly every minute of playing this game.  I was happy to see new heroes, new places, new villians, and new stories (kinda) put in Pandara and the Borderlands Universe I love very much.  You get great insight to some new heroes, some old favorites and more into Handsome Jack himself.  Overall this was a very very fun game for me, and one i will definately buy for friends, and tell anyone who likes point an clicks, borderlands, or story narrative games to definately play this and enjoy this for thereselves.  Thank You Gearbox, Tell Tale, and 2K Games.  This was a very unexpected gem.  It made me love Borderlands even more....

Even for a game that's in it's pre alpha stages, it's a very good game. Don't get me wrong. Like all games in existence, this game has it's fair share of problems. You really can't expect much from a game that's currently in alpha, or pretty much ANY game at all since every game as I've stated before has their own set of issues.
As of right now, the game is very lackluster and barebones, but again, you really can't expect too much from an alpha, so have caution if you're expecting this game to give you a lot because as of right now, there's not too much for this game to offer at the moment in it's current stage considering it's an early access title.
Another issue I've come across, which I'm still confused on determining what exactly the issue is that's causing this. Regardless, hit detection is another issue (when I'm not in U.S. servers). Any combination of these three reasons could be the cause: Netcode issue, tickrate issue, server location. But again, since it IS an alpha title, I can't really expect it to be perfect considering this game has been in the works slowly for the past decade, which definitely tells you how much the developers care if they're taking their time to perfect their game.
One other issue is engine optimization. The graphics, while great, are also very simple, and with simple graphics, I shouldn't be having such huge FPS fluxuations with my FPS dropping as low as 10 FPS at times. Now, the prototypes of the different game modes on the official Interstellar Marines website (especially Bullseye, which ran at a solid 60 FPS for me) looks, sounds, plays, and runs much better than what we currently have on Steam (again, alpha stage, you can't really expect much) which tells me that they're probably taking the DayZ route of things and most likely going to change engines in the future to a more optimized, a more playable engine. Again, it's an alpha. Not only is this game an alpha, but Zero Point Software is an independant game development company. You gotta start somewhere. Gotta be patient with this one considering how careful the devs are being and how delicate they're treating this game. Obviously, this game still has a lot of work to be done, but it's still great nonetheless for an alpha. Pretty much, most of the issues we're seeing currently is due to it's alpha status, which really NO game as an alpha or even a beta can avoid. It's just part of early access games and development. It's natural and it takes time.
Regardless, the game is great, and the prototypes of the different game modes on the official Interstellar Marines website are also fantastic as well, which pretty much gives you a taste or a hint of what's to come with this game in the future.
Although this game has been in development since 2004, I'd rather a game take 10 years to develop just so it can be perfect and up to it's full potential as opposed to having a broken game released to me that clearly isn't finished yet *coughcoughBADCOMPANY2coughcoughCALLOFDUTYcoughcoughBATTLEFIELD4*.
With that being said, I'd really suggest supporting Zero Point Software as much as possible considering they've been busting their asses off for the past 10 years just to dish out a good game, and that right there tells you that these developers take this seriously and pour every ounce of their tears and blood into this game.
Get this game. If not now as an pre alpha, get it as a full release when it's finally complete.

This Indie production suceedes in building suspense and fear using atmosphere, silence, and space. The environments, although somewhat generic and lacking in variety, are nonetheless well-designed to instill a sense of vast openness and foreboding.  This feeling is built less on cheap jump scares than on a more deeply-rooted, Lovecraftian cosmic fear. Astray takes a very minimalist approach to sound design, which works well. Without any music, every footstep sounds menacingly loud, and the slightest breath sets the player immediately on edge.
Overall, while Astray succedes in building an atmosphere of dread, it is somewhat lacking in story and overall content. The game itself is very short (most players should finish it in under 2 hours), partly due to the incredibly easy puzzles found in the first half of the game. The backstory builds slowly through various notes found throughout the environments. Although the writing is fine, the story is somewhat thin and, until the very end, fails to evoke much intrigue or mystery. Despite this, Astray ends on a very strong note, and it is certainly worth playing through to experience the conclusion.
Overall, Astray is a great effort by a small, independent team and succedes in building atmosphere and fear. Although quite short, the game offers a suspenseful journey through some unique environments, and is well worth the play through.

Taking the ring to the Mount Doom in Lego Style! A familiar story full of quirks and humor. The lego gameplay fits the LotR world surprisingly well.
The "hub" is the best I've seen so far in any lego game. There are also loads of hidden things from the lore as well as a bunch of easter eggs. The cut scenes are directly from the movies - as well as any voice acting. This means that the game is even more loyal to the movie than some other lego games (HP, PotC, SW). This also makes the levels super linear and full of cut scenes (which you cannot skip on your first playthrough btw). This means that a level consists of a number of sequences and you cannot backtrack to a previous one without starting that level from the beginning.
Unfortunately the game does not really add anything more to the mechanics either. It still is mostly smashing things to get coins, changing to a certain character to get stuff done and unlocking things in the attempt to get 100% complete.
Still, I found the game addicting and do not regret the time spent with it. A person not familiar with LotR might not feel the same.
TL:DR
If you love Middle Earth and silly stuff: Buy it
If you dislike grinding, too easy gameplay and have no interesting in LotR: Maybe not

-Easy gameplay to pick up and put down casually, makes for great short bursts of fun
-addicting gameplay
-The ability to spawn up to five waves at once, making it as hack and slashy/bullet hell as you choose.
-Great entry point at 60 cents
-Contains meme and game reference voice acting, this can be a pro or a con depending on the person.
-Multiplayer is not synced, not even over LAN/Ethernet at less than 10ms, mobs seem to teleport as the clients send each other conflicting data on positions, the official servers currently do not work and without proper netcode they shouldn't bother fixing them.
-Typing in multiplayer (even though MP barely works) will open random menus and interactions such as trade, items and skills.
-There is no semblance of balance, some relics such as Winners Drug make you basically immortal with stacking buffs that don't decay ) while others don't even proc after you change maps (hand of midas)
-Item rarity and level scaling seems wrong and level seems to barely affect the stats of an item compared to the rarity , in the aspects of that at level 50 and act 4 my drops are usually less than level 20, yellow/orange 40 weapons are worse than my 21 purple i got in the first act.
-Primitive mob damage system, being too close to an enemy will instantly hurt you without an animation, even on ranged enemies, this severely hinders melee classes and forces you to strafe backwards for a considerable amount of your time playing, although some argue this is a design decision.
-Half the game is locked away behind DLC, which arguably is justified now considering base price is on sale at 60 cents
-mob spawning seems to happen quite often outside the boundaries of the map and they do not enter the map, i've had rare encounters and loot goblins spawn outside the boundaries, which can be quite frustrating to see but never reach.
-I have been teleported(item proc) out of boundaries, as well as dashing through map boundaries, in overworld maps it teleports you back almost 100% but in dungeons you're stuck, forcing you to end your run completely.
-You can use skills such as Demon Hunter's Dash to cut half way through dungeons, I'm not sure if this is a perk/incentive to buy DLC characters or a bug, but I use it to skip most puzzles and gates.
-seemingly random types of projectiles fly through walls (DH sword throw proc for example)
-melee attacks seem to clip corners and edges of walls, making one way vantage points to funnel mobs, this could be called strategy but its a clear oversight of code or collision
-Unable to remap controls leaves me sometimes summoning a portal when I am navigating the inventory when using a controller.
even though I bought this thinking multiplayer was functional and that my friends and I would be able to play together, the singleplayer is an okay experience and it wont hurt to buy the base game now to enjoy the singleplayer content, but if you're someone who enjoys balance or multiplayer, I would strongly recommend waiting for future changes.

Never trust a bridge you find in Camatuga.  Go well out of your way to find a ferry, or go all the way around the river to get to the other side, but don't go across a bridge!
Bridge Constructor is a game where you build bridges in the fictional lands of Camatuga.  Your budget, and sometimes your available supplies (wood, steel, concrete, and rope) are limited, which means that sometimes you have to get creative.  But beyond that, it's all about figuring out how you can build a bridge, on budget, that will carry across cars, then medium trucks, then tanker-trailers.
While it may sound like a fairly straightforward physics building game, the wacky bridges you'll often wind up with and the explosions of wood and steel when things don't quite work out, make it hilarious.  The game is both a lot of fun by yourself, but also a lot of fun with friends, especially towards the more difficult later levels, where you can pass around the mouse and try your own approaches to building spans on low budgets.  Inevitably it will take a lot of tries to get it right, and laughter will ensue as unlikely bridges collapse - or occasionally prove just good enough to support the load, despite their "I'd never drive across that in real life" appearance.
Among the Bridge Constructor series, I'd put this one and Medieval at pretty much equal for gameplay, as Medieval introduces some interesting new elements, but the three vehicles types per bridge extends the challenge, in a good way, of each bridge here (while not preventing you from moving to the next one as long as you have cars getting across).  However, this iteration gave me much more playtime before I'd completed most of the game, and they're the same price, so my recommendation would be to get Bridge Constructor, have a blast, and if you're still wanting more, picking up Medieval after that.
