ESJ is one of the best games I have ever played in recent years - and I've played a lot of games. The soundtrack is amazing, the levels are tricky but enjoyable, and the storyline is quite strange but oddly memorable. The protagonist is the strong, silent type, but that's the only "typical" thing about this game - and that's perfectly fine, as he has a bit of a problem that he needs to work out, anyway... you wouldn't be talking either if you'd been through half of what he's been through himself. The characters that populate the BEAUTIFUL!!!!! levels will make you laugh, as will the story, but I'll admit that some of these levels are absolutely brutal. You won't be able to stop yourself from rage quitting.
What's great about it, too, is that the replay value is there! Once you've beaten the main game, there are lots of challenges for you (beating gold times, and collecting all the stars) - and, once you've collected everything, a new world unlocks that will provide you with more fun times. World 4 is brutal, but if you get tired of that, there are the holiday levels that were released for free, and those are a lot of fun. Also, you'll probably end up replaying favourite levels just for the heck of it.
You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll pull your hair out, you'll get up and dance, you'll buy the soundtrack and all the DLC for this game - ESJ is the game that you'll have fun trying to beat. Buy this game and learn to appreciate good music, good level design, and butts.

Originally I gave this game a thumbs down due to the fact that the game simply refused to start. The problem was with the Steam version of the game, which - for some reason - could not generate the file where the game saves the graphics settings and tried to force a resolution my computer simply could not either handle or compute. This problem has been remedied now thanks to a good friend of mine, who bought this game just so that he could try and fix it. And fix it he did. In less than five minutes.
My problem was related to the start up problem some seem to have, where starting the game will bring up only a white window with the words "not responding" in the upper left corner. You will need to download someone's configuration files - who did not have this issue - and place them into your Killer Instinct root folder. If you wish to do this yourself, set all your graphic settings to low or off and the resolution to 720p and then pack all the configuration files from the KI’s root folder into a .zip or .rar file and send it to your friend(s) who might be having this problem. (I will provide a link to the one that helped me at the end of this review, once I’ve found a place where I can host it.)
- Graphics-
The graphics of this game are surprisingly good looking considering its age. True, they've been enhancing it over the years, but the core models and the textures are still there, and they look good. I like how much options they've given us to adjust the visuals, something which many fighting games have failed to do when they've been ported to PC. Though to some the particle effects may be bit much at times; the screen is filled with literal fireworks when the characters clash and beat the tar out of each other. I myself like it, as it gives the fighting its own kind of intensity.
-Gameplay-
The game play is surprisingly solid for a western fighting game. One of the best, if not the best, I'd say. Some people I've heard complaining that the inputs are too forgiving and how it’s too easy to pull off visually impressive combos in this game. I say, that's the whole point. This game is all about going crazy, rushing your opponent and delivering all sorts of insane combos you rarely see in any other fighting game in the market. In terms of pacing, I don't think there really is any other fighting game in the market - aside the BlazBlue series - that comes close to KI in terms of speed and intensity.
-Sounds-
I really like the voice acting, though some of the lines the characters say are bit cheesy at times. And while some of the music in this game can be bit average, vast majority of it really gets my blood pumping. I'd like to recommend that you look into buying the game's soundtrack, but only after taking a small sample what they're like from youtube - just in case you're not friend of metal, because that's the genre of majority of the music in the game.
-Advertisement-
Ok...what the Hell? There was literally no warning whatsoever; they just up and put this game up in Steam without proper advertisement. While I'm sure people will find it, the publisher would have gotten far better initial sales if they'd put at least some marketing into this release.
-Micro transactions-
Yes, there are micro transactions in this game, but they can be largely ignored, unless you're really impatient on unlocking the cosmetics for the game's characters through playing the arcade-, vs-, story- or survival mode (And unlike in Street Fighter 5, in KI it doesn’t feel like a chore). Everything else in this version of the Killer Instinct has been unlocked from the get go.
(Get it while you can, I hope it helps those who are having the whitescreen problem. Just unpack the file into your Killer Instinct root folder in the Steam library folder.)

Wolfenstein: The New Order is an enjoyable FPS game. Is it mindblowing? Not really. Will I remember it in 5 years? Probably not. But did I enjoy the 10~ hours I spent with it? Yeah, I certainly did. Wolfenstein ticks most of the boxes for being a good AAA game. It's cinematic, it's got solid gameplay and variety within its demolition/stealth/cover shooter mechanics, the story and writing are both passable. I guess all I can say is that I was just a bit disappointed. It certainly wouldn't have made my GOTY in 2014, but I can also see why people would give it an 8. For me it's hard to hate but unfortunately nothing that I found myself enamored with. It's probably better than 9 out of 10 modern shooters, so if that's convinced you then I'd wager you've already played this game. Otherwise, go play it. It's pretty damn decent.
Apparently people really loved the story and writing. I can't really understand why, other than getting engrossed by the cast. And I mean, the cast is quite likeable - but they aren't exactly the most well written characters I've encountered. I honestly felt like the random notes and tapes you found were a lot more interesting and memorable than any single moment throughout the main campaign. Like I said earlier, it is passable and even enjoyable... but well written and masterful, not so much. I would only really recommend this game for solid variety and mechanics with AAA flair.

An A+++ title with some frustrating segments, boss fights, unbelievable stab wounds and a perk system that can take away from the game play.
The fps action in New Order is splendid, the ability to dual wield weapons and gun down nazi's and large robots is superbly done. The story overall keeps things moving and adds some replay ability with two different time lines based on whom you save. The health upgrade line is best for help with harder difficulties.
A laser welding tool adds a different utiltiy kind of weapon to the game, usually a flashlight, some sort of radar, a telescope that can highlight enemies - have all been done, the welding tool and using it in a variety of places added something different to Wolfenstein.
The stealh action in wolfenstein was okay, the typical crouch and takedown, or throw a weapon and takedown, or a silenced weapon - it wont be thief or styx if thats your preference.
I played through four times, and by the fourth I was ready to be done and uninstall, there isnt much to explore and the gun fights while fun have a decaying factor I havent exprienced in awhile. Having just beaten F.E.A.R and its two expansions 3 times each, I have to say that FEAR was more fun, the fps action and the feeling of spectacular gun fights and wiping out squads of baddies was not there in The new order: Run down corridor or up a stair case takedown this guy take down that guy, it was somewhat ho hum after the first play through, even with FEAR being 2006, the graphics didnt matter as much as the atmosphere and accomplishment. Additionally FEAR still has the best AI around, Wolfenstein like so many 2010 plus titles was lacking in the smarts department.
Nazi Guard on duty: Mmm just my commrade there lying on his back with red jam all around his neck, odd. I better report him.
The game has a four bonus rounds, that are cool, harsh, over the top, and WTF? The only one to intrique me was the IRONMAN which i called - One Life To Live - which I only played because it felt like RTCW Multiplayer Days, you get one life and you cant save, beat the game in one shot which is about 4hr 30min, or leave your computer on...exit the bonus mode and its "game over man". Unlock all the perks in regular gameplay and they will be there in the bonus modes, but perk progression cant occur in the bonus modes so have them done to assist in the UBER bonus modes.
With that said IRONMAN was the only real challenge and satisfying part of the game, it was so much more tactical and fleshed out The New Orders FPS potential and this is were the game exposed itself as being just another gun game with flashier new graphics.
A few parts of the story were messed up too; two times in the game your character is stabbed with a knife - not paper cut  wrap it and kiss it kind of stab but, 3 inches of a 6 blade knife lodged in your gut kinda stab, with a few extra matching holes.... yet your character goes on performing his heroic deeds....nonsense. A good beating with a pipe, being knocked around by the butt of a gun would have left it "possible" for the hero to continue on, but 5 3+ inch stab wounds to the chest (right or left) and your not dual wielding two 10 lbs shotguns and sliding between doors in a hallway.
I know this is fiction - but these two moments were just too far fetched, there were better way to make the nazi's seem atrocious.
The ending sequence between the final boss and the hero is once again too far fetched, especially since the hero makes a return in the sequel.
The final boss fight is - wonky. There is no good indicator as to when youve won, its about burst damage and lots of it, and very unsatisfying end.
The perk system, has some problems namely 4: Throwing back a grenade for a kill 5 times, killing 5 mechanical enemies with a grenade, use the LKW and empty it without missing, use assault rifle and get 80 cover kills.
The first two are such crap - its best to find certain checkpoints go kill and restart in order to obtain them. The third is best done before getting the scope on the LKW, and the last one is just fricken annoying... how about 30 or 40 or 50... 80? and then the upgrade is - 7 more rounds in the mag. Wow save the universe with that one.
The New Orders pace, its broken up with different areas and time frames, and this leaves the continuity and progress in a bit of a mess. Its more realistic, who would carry 15 guns on them like in Resistance or Doom? So that was understandable but going to and fro from the hideout did break up the action a tad too much.
The New Order actually played better AFTER i beat it a few times, you can replay the story and do the other timeline with your perks saved, this gives a chance to get both the health and armor upgrades - then go for the harder bonus modes. It also allows for you to stop hunting down collectibles and finishing perks so you can just enjoy the gameplay - it is then that wolfenstein finally blazes to life.
A note on the armor upgrade is it increases the value of the armor picked up: meaning if you get 5 armor for default - having picked up all 10 upgrades you will get a value of 10 instead, it does not raise the armor value above 100. There is a perk that gives armor beyond 100 for kill streaks (autopanzer) but with so much action going on, you rarely look down to reflect on your armor, and the buff is very short lived, I rarely during fights looked at armor, mostly the health as it begins to flash red at lower percentages, and topped off armor during calmer moments.
The New Order is a deal on sale, its not built for longevity, but gives a lot of bangs for the buck.

Savage in its brutality yet delicate in its intimacy, Wolfenstein: The New Order is a fantastic resurrection of an old franchise; meshing incredibly satisfying combat with a beautifuly realised world, lore, and character.
I never played any of the previous Wolfenstein games. Pretty much all I know about them is that you run around killing Nazis and apparently there is a mecha Hitler. The New Order certainly has its fair share of Nazi-scalping goodness, but under all of the blood and gore there is a heart of gold to be found here.
One of the things that stuck with me the most was the opening cutscene to the game, which  reminded me of the opening to Spec Ops: The Line. It was a beautiful, serene moment in a game where the primary focus is on the gun in your hand and the enemies in your sights. For all of the giant robo Nazi dogs patrolling the streets, the Nazi war machines towering above the skyline of the New Order, and all of the Nazis on the moon, Machine Games never forgets about its chracters.
This is where I believe Wolfenstein: The New Order's biggest strength lies. I absolutely loved hearing BJ's internal monologues throughout the game. For a man who is presented as a gruff, swol, good old fashioned American GI joe, BJ has a incredible amount of perspective. This can be said of the other characters you meet throughout the game too, I enjoyed hearing what people had to say, and I enjoyed learning about this fearsome new world order ruled by the Nazis. Seriously, this game has some really good lore and world building.
And of course I have to mention the fantastic soundtrack by Michael Gordon. The score for the New Order weaves in some very grungy, Doomesque melodies that are accompanied by beautifully delicate guitar symphonies. My personal favourite two tracks on the album are Ransacked and Ende, highly recommend.
All in all Wolfenstein: The New Order is definitely worth picking up. Whether you want to have some good FPS fun, a great story, an interesting world, or all of that and more, Machine Games certainly delivered.

TALES FROM THE BORDERLANDS FAST REVIEW (NO SPOILERS)
- I had heaps of fun playing this game. It easily ranks as one of the funniest games that i've ever played.
- If you enjoy good story telling, you should play this.
- If you like reading comic books, you should play this.
- If you like the Borderlands franchise, you should play this.
- If you've played any of the other Telltale games,  you should play this, it's the best one yet.
Like i've said above, i really liked this game, & i honestly think there's no reason for every single person who likes gaming, to give it a try.
The story was fast paced, & gripping the whole way through. It was told from a two-person perspective, with the two seperate storys constantly overlapping with each others continuity. The characters were interesting, & since you control the direction of some dialogue, it's upto you how likeable they are (to some degree).
If you've played the Bordelands game, then there are heaps of cameo apperances, & easter eggs for you to go "Ahh, i remember that..." over, but i think even with no previous Borderlands experience (i've only played the 1st & 2nd games, not the Pre-Sequel), if you enjoy a good story, then this game has it.
The graphics/ art was very comic book like, similar to the style of the Borderlands fps games, as well as being easily recognizable as a Telltale game.
The comedy was great, the highlight of the game, in my opinion. I laughed out loud a lot during this game, i'd even say, just as much as during the South Park game.
Overall, i'd have to say, this is the best Telltale game i've played (G.O.T. next), & i really hope they make another in this series. Even if it's new characters, with cameos by this games cast (just an idea).

It's as fun as I remember - Actually, it's better than that, since we have a dozen more civilizations to choose from, and campaigns to play. That may be, in fact, the best part of this game. The developers/distributors aren't simply cashing on the nostalgia, but actively adding new content, without changing the baseline that made it so sucessful.
Worth every penny.

This is getting a recommended for the single player and other features in the game such as leveling up, shops, items, accessories, and etc. If you're going to get this game for mainly online, then you're out of luck.
The game is working well in single player but the online is just terrible. Very rarely would you be able to connect to the xenoverse server and when you do, you get random disconnects. There are times it worked well enough to last me an entire session but that was only once.
Leaving the online asside, the game holds on its own fairly well in single player. Story is average but the great thing is the character creation and being able to customize your character as you progress through the game to choosing your own attributes to level up, and picking up new items and abilities from quests and masters. The game is a dumbed down version of previous dragonball games (I'm referring to the ps2 era, I've never played the PS3 ones) but that was so you can easily switch out your special/ultimate attack/evades/transformations.
The single player can net you 10+ hours fairly easily because there is some grinding involved, just so you can learn new skills from your masters/quests. For someone like me, who doesn't like grinding, the game's grinding isn't insane like the majority of MMOs where you're required to grind for days on end for items/skills/leveling up. In the 30 hours of my play time, I've maxed a character and a half. All items, skills, and quests you've achieved are universal to all your characters so you will not need to unnecessarily grind for those things again.
The quests you've unlocked with your characters will be available to all your other characters so you can level up rapidly by skipping the quests appropriate to your capabilities. I went from 2-3  star quests to 9-10 star quests within an hour; so my new character went from lvl 1 to 40 in that time, compared to my first character which took me about 15 hours because I didn't know what to do. This allows you to mix your play style and character types in a very short amount of time so you can move on to playing online with your new character (thinking about online saddens me still).
At the moment, I'm giving this game a 6/10 because of the unstable online service. If that online component was fixed, it would definitely be an 8 or above.

As a long time fan of the C&C series I was extremely excited when I heard of Red Alert 3's development. Although Westwood Studios (former publisher of the C&C Red Alert series) was liquified back in 2002/early 2003, not long after RA2 Yuris Revenge released, some of the crew assimilated into EA. Although this was a sad time, when RA3 was announced I had high hopes and Id like to think that RA3 hit almost all the expectations.
And then I saw this. I had been a little caught up with exams and such when this was originally released so I completely missed it and stumbled upon it on Steam a few weeks ago. I gleefully wrung my hands together and bought it, excited at the chance to try some new tactics and try out the new units and maps.
The campaigns are short. Four missions per story and they are very basic missions although I personally found most fairly challenging, more so than the base game.
However whilst playing most missions I felt extremely overwhelmed by the seemingly unstoppable enemy forces. For example in one Allied story mission you are expected to transport an MCV to a set location then set up and defeat any Empire units and bases in the vicinty. The transportation part was simple enough and once the base is set you are introduced to a new unit The Harbringer, a large AC130 esque ship with some capabilities to deal with ground units. Suddenly all hell breaks loose, as soon as I was given control of the base, resources and units I instantly come under attack from a (almost cheat worthy) slew of enemy units when Ive had less than 2 minutes to begin producing anything. Needless to say I was slaughtered and had to try the mission at least 4 times before successfully finishing it.

Before I knew it I had burned my way through all the main army stories leading me to play the equally as short story of Yuriko Omega (that hero unit from the Empire that was kinda meh). Her story was taken in a different approach than the others as it was made into a Dungeon Siege esque 'minigame'. You have different abilites each mapped to 1-4 of your keyboard numbers. This was rather enjoyable and the new take on the gameplay was refreshing. Like the main armies her story was short but even more so than the mains as it was only 3 missions (2 of which take place in the same location).
After I finished her story (which still gave her barely any backstory at all it felt more like a filler episode from Naruto) I decided to head into Commander Challenge mode.
This is a new mode implemented specifically for this standalone. This mode allows to you play missions with any army but limits what units you have until you beat certain missions to unlock. Each mission has a par time and scores depending on various factors, giving it plenty of replayability if you are one of those people who like to beat record times and such. I however am not and burned my through it, enjoying the story mission feel of the challenges but also the limitations made me test new tactics.
Now the part I really wanted to get too.
The skirmish mode. Sucks♥♥♥♥♥in this game.
Although no description in the game says so there are quite a few new maps in the game which offer new skirmish fun...HOWEVER MOST OF THE BASE GAME SKIRMISH MAPS HAVE BEEN REPLACED. There a few select maps taken from RA3 but most are new maps which are barely creative, fairly generic and small. Even the 6 player maps are tiny, which can be fun if hectic battles where you can barely build anything is fun.
Additionally the co-commander features have been completely removed. Gone. Disappeared from existence.
Even in Skirmish mode where you could have Ai teammates to take on other enemy AI they have completely removed the team based battles. I understood that they removed it for story but removing it from the standalone altogether? Little bit OTT if you ask me.
And I bet you're wondering where the multiplayer part is............well there isnt one. Multiplayer isnt a thing in this standalone for some unknown reason. They decided to isolate the multiplayer community for this game because "♥♥♥♥ you we're EA". Not that many people played online anyway.
So to sum up the points

Alternate history at its finest. The Nazis have conquered Europe, Africa, most of Asia and nuked New York. Hitler is realizing his visions and dreams and humanity suffers. Citizens are under constant surveillance, culture is censored, but against such technologically advanced war machine, no one can do anything reasonable. It's up to you, the degenerate, antisocial terrorist to change the flow of history a little bit.
Because of the new world order, your actions in-game will always succumb to the oppressive feeling that you are making just a small dent on the face of an unshakeable system. This system has many manifestations and its creator is only mentioned in this game. You will encounter diabolical General Deathshead and you will be hunted by masochistic Frau Engel.
The game is heavy on the narrative front with many supporting characters and allies. You will become a part of the Kreisau Circle resistance group stationed in the hornet's nest itself: Neu Berlin. Its headquarters function as intermezzo periods of respite between chapters and feature some rich dialogues. The narrative is relayed mainly through many cutscenes, which are of top quality and keep you interested in the cast, mainly the protagonist: B.J. Blazkowicz. His internal monologue consisting of short sentences is a great window into a mind of a troubled war hero, dreaming of having a family and living peacefully. The cast is rich in variety including a big guy with a bit of his head missing, a paralyzed leader, a Jewish scholar or a Polish girl that you fall in love with.
Honestly, it was refreshing to see a modern game with such mature and developed storyline. The story will take you to Berlin, London, Poland, Croatia and you can read newspaper clippings about the situation in the countries you won't visit. The game is thoroughly Germanized with much of the adversaries' dialogues being in German and the game constantly pulls out German posters, quotes during loading and even all of the notes in the game are written in German with the English translation underneath it. The English language is indeed a dying tongue in this world and you truly get the feeling of an alien world, if you don't know much German.
Now after the exquisite story I finally get to gameplay! It's, of course, amazing like the rest of the game mainly because of the perfect cover system and the ability to dual-wield your weapons. Enemies are reasonably variable, including mechanical Panzerhunds, armored Kampfhunds and hulking Supersoldats. Unlike the 2017 sequel, all of the weapons have amazing handling and sound so the gunplay is lots of fun.
The soundtrack is nothing short of amazing and Mick Gordon really made a name for himself with this one. I also loved the collectible records of songs by fictionalized real-world bands like The Beatles, now Die Käfer, forced to sing in German about conquering Moon and all of Milky Way. Visually, the game was given much care to portray the Über Concrete cities and all that dystopian feeling feels very real. The only problem I had was with vistas being too blurry and the game lacks some real anti-aliasing support.
9/10
+ a perfect rendition of alternate history world, splendid action, heavy narrative
- some technical discrepancies

TALES FROM THE BORDERLANDS FAST REVIEW (NO SPOILERS)
- I had heaps of fun playing this game. It easily ranks as one of the funniest games that i've ever played.
- If you enjoy good story telling, you should play this.
- If you like reading comic books, you should play this.
- If you like the Borderlands franchise, you should play this.
- If you've played any of the other Telltale games,  you should play this, it's the best one yet.
Like i've said above, i really liked this game, & i honestly think there's no reason for every single person who likes gaming, to give it a try.
The story was fast paced, & gripping the whole way through. It was told from a two-person perspective, with the two seperate storys constantly overlapping with each others continuity. The characters were interesting, & since you control the direction of some dialogue, it's upto you how likeable they are (to some degree).
If you've played the Bordelands game, then there are heaps of cameo apperances, & easter eggs for you to go "Ahh, i remember that..." over, but i think even with no previous Borderlands experience (i've only played the 1st & 2nd games, not the Pre-Sequel), if you enjoy a good story, then this game has it.
The graphics/ art was very comic book like, similar to the style of the Borderlands fps games, as well as being easily recognizable as a Telltale game.
The comedy was great, the highlight of the game, in my opinion. I laughed out loud a lot during this game, i'd even say, just as much as during the South Park game.
Overall, i'd have to say, this is the best Telltale game i've played (G.O.T. next), & i really hope they make another in this series. Even if it's new characters, with cameos by this games cast (just an idea).
9/10

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

This game used to be a fun random roguelike top-down shooter. Now the difficulty has been ramped up so much you are forced to die over and over and over just to slowly grind levels.
Before you could get tons of cool stacking random equipment, now they treat your character like a persistent RPG character with a single inventory and limited equipment slots.
I think most of this was done for the co-op players who probably thought the game was too easy but if you play solo prepare for a ridiculous grind and millions of completely unfair deaths.
The UI has also regone surgery and is horribly unintuitive, you will find yourself pushing random buttons to get through menus mid-game which will get you killed. Previously their in-game UI was so simple all you had was one button to go to your skill page and another to open the store and buy stats/items/hp.
Now you have to find everything, even the useless NPCs in town have nothing for sale.
I tried giving the game a chance I even bought the Amazon cuz I figured I used to like this game. Now it just feels like a chore, death will happen over and over and it's not your fault. Volcanoes pop up out of random boxes, enemies explode in your face, your companion wanders outside the map boundry and dies. And when you die you just get to start over from the beginning of the Act.
Maybe this game is fun for certain "hardcore" gamers out there but I am not recommending it based on how much it has changed. This is not the game I bought two years ago. Not even close. (It's sad too because it looks the same and wants to be the same, but it's completely different.)

So I dont typically like many fighting games, and while I do like the anime Im not really a fan boy. If I "were" though Id tell you how excited I am for the new Frieza movie coming out in japan sometime this April ;) Since the servers seem to be functioning now Im editing my review, but honestly I still cant give game companies a free pass when they release games in such a broken state. Plus there are STILL issues with playing online, such as the broken "idle checker" that will boot you even when you've just come out of a game.
"Would it really have been so hard to just...?"
In depth review is as follows - you were warned.
1= Now I don't mind RNG in games, but Xenoverse relies on it to a rediculous extent. Not only is the loot not explained but it has only a chance to drop if you meet the hidden criteria for it to drop. What makes it worse is many PQ missions play out similarly. For instance many events require something to happen, say killing a specific character last. And even if you fulfill these special requirements the event that is supposed to happen might not even occur due to no fault of your own, simply RNG. It makes the whole experience largely a guessing game of what you have to do to make something happen to fight someone to maybe get a drop from them at those times. For example when farming Brollys clothes, you have to sit back doing nothing and wait for the terrible AI to decide when it will fight and kill Videl, then hope Brolly kills Goten and Trunks so Gohan appears. This gives the best CHANCE of Brolly deciding to revive. Then after you kill him the second time [if he revives] you still only have a small chance to get an item. Much of the game works like this, its lame.
2= Now a very close second, the lack of any actual chat in game. I mean for crying out loud... this is obviously a straight up console port with no love for PC enthusiasts. You're limited in game by already scripted comments like "Hello" and "yes" and "no". What is wrong with just a chat lobby for people? Maybe the ability to private message someone or send someone little messages through steam at the very least? It really makes me wish steams default ways of doing things didnt prevent you from simply messaging people who you just met and havent added to your friends list. Anyway, one particularly annoying situation is I'll be in the game trying to offer some help to anyone who wants it and Im limited to "Seeking Friends" "I'll help!" and so on, and then when we set up a team we STILL lack in game voice options until we actually make a room and pick a level. So theres litterally no way I can ask someone which specific mission theyd like help with until we're already in a random mission. *shakes head* Communication is important, and the ball gets dropped hard here. This is on PC, I have a keyboard, LET ME USE IT! *shakes game*
3= No online story mode, wouldn't have been hard *sigh*. Now I understand that its perhaps for a more immersive single player experience but I would have liked the ability to at least make a new character and do a co op campaign with friends or something. Perhaps be able to go back to already beaten missions and play them again with friends to get a better rank... something at least? But especially for a game that requires you to be connected to online servers at all times [unless you set steam to offline mode] why isnt there more content to do online with people?Theres a lot of possible content here that would be fun to play, yet we are limited to side quests and versus mode only. I really wish there was more co op content in the game other than side quests. As it is, other than pvp theres not a lot replayability here yet.
4= The online play has problems too. Now I wont get too much into bugs, or balancing issues. I wont get into lame combat mechanics like ult spamming and such either. I mean the actual game play... for one the Host has a very large advantage since the game lags and desyncs a lot, which strikes me as odd if we're supposed to be connecting to some official game server right? Im not sure what the purpose of these servers are if people are hosting their own games honestly. Lots of times attacks that should hit miss, and in a fighting game that relies a lot on well timed blocks and split second timing of attacks to get a hit in this can easily be a game changer, or, a game ruiner. And like I said earlier, most of the game seems centered on pvp fighting, it really wouldnt be as big an issue if the single player or co op parts had more replayability.
5= Lack of customization, sorta. This will be my longest and most in depth critique, and I admit its mostly opinion. Dont get me wrong theres lots of options and outfits, and even the ones with the most stats barely affect anything so its pretty close to being entirely cosmetic other than for hard core minmaxers. My problem stems from more deep seeded issues. For instance most of the outfits aren't tintable/recolorable, which would have been pretty easy. Theres also no way to take a favorite outfit of yours and make your own version of it, say with your own preference of stats or styles, so if you wanted your character to have goku's torn up gi and be bare chested then your SOL. Theres other problems too, if you dont want to be a fat buu you have to make a female buu. And while I understand that namekians are genderless why couldnt we have female frieza's? Speaking of, different genders have different stats, as well as your size and such. Its strange that your appearance wouldnt be completely cosmetic considering almost everything else is, but my suggestion is if your wanting a female character make her as large as possible since they're super tiny. My first Saiyan couldnt even see over the counter at the default height, and even at max height possible she's right in between Gohans and Videl's height, for reference.
Otherwise, Buu's and Frieza's have no different forms. And super saiyans, well where do I begin?Theres only SS1 and 2, theres a super vegeta form but its the same... its supposed to increase your ki blasts a little more than super saiyan instead of melee but Im not seeing it so if the difference there they probably ♥♥♥♥ed up and put the decimal in the wrong place so its probably like 1% and 3% difference instead of 10 and 30 or whatever. I'll go super saiyan when a friend is looking at me on their scouter to see my power levels and it doesnt change at all. It would have also been nice if our hair changed AT ALL when we went super saiyan. While it DOES turn colors, the style is completely static. I was really hoping that my hair would spike up and nope, the model didnt change what-so-ever. Would it have really been that hard to include a normal and super saiyan hair style versions?
Lastly for complaints about customization, it seems the same voices are used for all races. I was expecting different races to sound different but humans sound the same as every other race... which is a let down. Would it really have been that hard to get a few more voice actors for a major title game? Your character is stoically silent in the story mode anyway so all your character says is names of attacks while battling... like SPECIAL BEAM CANNON! and "Hi" or "whatsup?"
Otherwise, all that aside [and it is a lot] the gameplay is amazing. Its primarily an online fighting game so I think thats where the majority of people are going to be concerned with. Balance, bugs, latency, etc are all issues but Ive ran out of room in my review, sorry.

Don't get me wrong - Titan Souls is a pretty good game, especially in terms of its soundtrack and the ending. However, it is not quite worth the full price of $15.
Pros:
- All of the bosses play uniquely and are mostly pretty memorable.
- The art style is good, though it's definitely not the best or most visually appealing I've seen in an indie game.
- The game has a great OST that creates a sense of epicness.
- Each of the bosses feels supremely satisfying to beat once you've managed to pull of the trickshot required to beat them. They also feel like individual puzzles of finding out how to get in the position to hit their weak spot and defeat them.
- There's a hard mode to try if you want.
- You can roll.
Cons:
-  The game revolves around getting 1-4 good shots on the bosses' weak spot, and ending the fight quickly. It sounds interesting to have a game focused on the idea of avoiding attacks until you are finally in the position to take out the boss, but it's frustrating in practice.
- Every time you die, the death animation is long and it takes time to walk back to where you were. The music also resets each time. It's annoying in a game where you're expected to die about 10 times per every fight that lasts twenty-five seconds.
- The game's length is short for a $15 game.
- Besides the music, there's nothing very special about this game that makes it stand out to me.

LEGO The Lord of the Rings is the classic tale we all know and love set to prop comedy and Louis Armstrong's seminal hit "Blue Yodel No. 9 (Standing on the Corner)". All the major beats of the classic teleplay are present: young Frondo Baggins is left to care for his uncle's estate after uncle Bilbo announces his retirement from the LAPD. However, the wise wizard Gonald realizes that a piece of confiscated bling Bilbo passed on to Frondo is in fact The Ring, and sets him off on a quest with his gardener Rudy.
However, Frondo is situatied somewhere in the back of the title card for the game, and the story does not truly begin until reaching the elven city of San d'Oria, where Viggo Mortensen and a young Jimmy Connelly (stunningly rendered in LEGO form thanks to advancing mocap technology) join the group. Many trials and tribulations await our heroes, not the least of which trials and tribulations await our heroes, not the least of which the mad Gallum.
If you've played one LEGO game, you know what to expect. LEGO The The Lord of the Rings ups the ante by introducing a basic questing and crafting system, as well as an inventory management system that puts the likes of the Resident Evil series to shame. Many medieval stand-ins appear for similar elements in other Legos games: minikit pieces become treasure chests, gold bricks become mithril (used for crafting and the exclusive one million dollar cash prize Traveler's Tales is running), and red bricks become red bricks.
The LEGO Lord of the Rings takes the idea of an open world, first attempted in LEGO The Batman 2, and tweaks it in an interesting way. The hub world is in fact a completely explorable LEGO The Middle Earth, complete with side objectives. While the normal level-by-level gameplay occurs in the same static camera layout we've all come to enjoy, these little breaks between levels are a nice median between the tiny hubs of elder lego games and the huge, yet dull, world of LEGO Batman 2.
Traveler's Tales has opted to pull dialogue straight from the movies for this game, which makes sense because they ultimately do not have the budget to bring on amazing, well-paid and respected actors like John Rhys-Davies and that guy who looks like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Paulie Shore. Not only does this make the dialgoue volume slightly inconsistent, but it also creates interesting scenarios, like that part where Boromir dies like a ♥♥♥♥♥ being voiced with all the seriousness it deserves, while portraying a LEGO man dying of a banana to the chest.
The game supports local co-operative play, which is also a staple feature of The LEGO games. The games are fairly simple to pick up and play, and provided you don't play with some♥♥♥♥♥♥who keeps wanting to kill you it's sure to be a good time. The game also splits the screen if the two players stray too far from each other, which demonstrates the amazing power of the Cell. Just don't play with your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ younger cousin, because at some points in the game the two players control two different aspects of the same scene, and he's not going to get anywhere if you aren't there holding his hand.
In conclusion, LEGO the Lord of The Rings does not disappoint, but that's only because it's impossible to set the bar for these types of games too high to behin with, and any attempt the game makes to surpass the bar is worthy of praise. Buy this game for something fun to do with friends over the weekend. Just don't invite the sperglord who loves Lord of the Rings, because I swear to God Kyle nobody gives a♥♥♥♥♥♥if this isn't a 1:1 reproduction of the movie we're just trying to have a ♥♥♥♥ing good time.

Despite all the problems in this game (Which are referred in this review) this game is fun and the base of this game is very unique with creative artwork and designs. Although I am recommending this game I will list the Pros and Cons below.
There is a lot of Mad Max aesthetic to this game which I automatically enjoy because I like how the game allows you to build whichever car you want and whichever weapons you want on it but the battery can only charge so much which is difficult, but I like a challenge.
I love the art in this game, My personal favorite design was the Lunatic Leader. There is a high attention to detail in the character models and each faction having their own design which is very creative and cool!
Playing with friends is very fun even with the problems in this game. Lots of laughs and playing with friends reduces the rage building.
Now the cons....
The game play of this is very frustrating. The timer alone makes things more painful waiting for 3 minutes for a match and the estimated time for each match is roughly 6-7 seconds. Once you eventually get into a match, there is no balance when it comes to the other online players, so you can be a noob fighting against the toughest person ever with no way to win.
The Pay-To-Win in this game is very despicable. There is almost no way to win against high ranking players in matches without paying for something that bumps up your defense or weaponry. Almost every time a match begins, there's somebody that has purchased the Immortal Warrior tank pack that costs about 60$ and is impossible to destroy with the base vehicles.
Grinding (collection of resources for crafting things in this game) is also very bad. most weapons take about 400 scrap metal and about 50 copper metal (only win 15 scrap per won game and 5 copper per won game) and you only usually win 1 game per 5 games, so it takes quite a long time and it just isn't enjoyable.
Please fix these issues to make a better game

Do you like fast racing, doing tricks in midair, and most of all, SONIC?
This is the game for you!
Pros:
- Fast racing
- Tons of missions to complete and tons of things to unlock!
- trick mechanic. (see below)
- Absolutely blows Mario Kart out of the water. The tracks are constantly changing, each vehicle transformation controls completely differently, and the items take skill to deploy.
Cons:
- There's lots of bugs. I've lost a race on the third lap multiple times because I hit an object at a weird angle and fell out of the stage.
- S class difficulty is full of cheating CPUs.
One of the most important features in SASRT is the "trick" mechanic. In mid air, you can preform a trick by flicking the right control stick. Doing these in succession gets you more boost.
Why is this so important? The more skilled you are at this game, the more you can successfully land tricks. As a plane, you can even dodge objects to get risk boosts.

Upfront: this is the second time I've bought the Definitive Edition of this game. It is worth EVERY CENT for a fighting game fan.
What Iron Galaxy did when they took over this game from Double Helix is nothing short of remarkable. They made this game a must buy by filling it with the feedback and love of the community that developed around the game. They made it a must buy by filling it with unique characters and modes. They made it a must buy by filling it with enough content to pad out fifteen modern Capcom fighters. The ONLY reason this game has been overlooked is that it was shackled to the XBONE and Games for Windows. Now that it is on Steam I've bought it again because Iron Galaxy earned my loyalty. If you're a fighting game fan and you buy this game and take the time to learn it they will earn your love too.
tl;dr Robust single player, great cast, great tutorials, unique fighting game systems. The only flaw with this game is that Mick Gordon wasn't back for the Season 3 soundtrack.
